Fire TV help

Fire TV help

This guide holds the help Amazon publishes for Fire TV, gathered on 18 August 2026. Amazon publishes one help estate covering everything it sells, so the gathering was held to Fire TV by reading each page’s own heading before following its links, and the build sets aside any page whose title and trail never mention Fire TV. The categories are Amazon’s own, taken from the trail printed above each article.

The guide covers the streaming sticks and boxes, Fire TV built into televisions and soundbars, the remotes, profiles, settings, app and playback problems, and the Recast recorder. It does not cover Amazon’s other devices or its shopping account, which are documented elsewhere in the same estate.

Four pages are deliberately left out. Amazon publishes the open-source software licences for its devices as help articles, and the one for the Fire TV Recast alone runs to nearly 150,000 words of package names and licence text — half again as long as everything else here put together. Safety and compliance pages are kept, because those are real device documentation; only the licence lists are gone.

Auracast Streaming on Your Fire TV Smart TV

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Accessibility on Fire TV ›

Auracast Streaming on Your Fire TV Smart TV

You can pair up to four Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)/Auracast headset or hearing aids (BLE audio device) with your Fire TV Smart TV.

Note: The following devices support BLE audio:

  • Panasonic W90/W95 Series Fire TV Smart TV
  • Panasonic Z85 Series Fire TV Smart TV
  • Panasonic Z90/Z93/Z95 Series Fire TV Smart TV To learn how to set up a BLE audio device, visit Pair a BLE or Auracast Headset to Your Fire TV Smart TV.

To share your Auracast streaming with other users:

  • After pairing up to four BLE audio devices with your Fire TV, turn on Auto Join for each device:
    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV Smart TV.
    • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices > Audio devices and features.
    • Select your BLE audio device from the list of available devices.
    • Turn on Auto Join.
  • If you prefer to join the Auracast using your BLE Audio compatible mobile phone:
    • Pair your BLE audio device to a compatible mobile phone.
    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
    • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices.
    • Choose Audio devices and features.
    • Select Auracast and turn it on.
    • Locate and use your Auracast Name and Auracast Passcode to join the Auracast network.
  • To change Auracast Name or Auracast Passcode as per choice, select Change Auracast Name/Change Auracast Passcode
  • If you change your Auracast passcode, or update the encryption, rescan the BLE audio device with your compatible mobile phone to rejoin.
  • To allow others to join your Auracast network without a passcode:
    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
    • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices.
    • Choose Audio devices and features.
    • Select Auracast, and then turn off Encrypt Auracast.

Can’t Pair a BLE or Auracast Headset with Fire TV Smart TV

Troubleshoot issues using BLE/Auracast headsets or hearing aids with your Fire TV Smart TV.

Note: The following devices support BLE audio:

  • Panasonic W90/W95 Series Fire TV Smart TV

  • Panasonic Z85 Series Fire TV Smart TV

  • Panasonic Z90/Z93/Z95 Series Fire TV Smart TV If you experience issues while pairing your BLE audio device to your Fire TV Smart TV, try the following suggestions:

  • If there’s no audio after connecting to the BLE audio device:

    • If you’re not using the Auracast feature:
      • Unpair your BLE audio device from your Fire TV, and then pair it again.
    • If you’re using the Auracast feature:
      • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
      • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices > Audio devices and features.
      • Select your BLE audio device and then turn on Auto join.
        • If Auto join is already on, turn it off and on again.
      • For hearing aids, turn on Hearing aid compatibility.
    • Restart your BLE audio device.
    • If you still can’t pair or hear audio on your BLE audio device, factory reset your BLE audio device and pair again.

  • If you can’t listen to Auracast from your Fire TV, join the Auracast network through a compatible mobile phone:

    • Pair and connect your BLE audio device to a compatible mobile phone.
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices > Audio Devices and Features.
    • Select Auracast and locate the Auracast Name and Auracast Passcode.
    • Use the name and passcode to join the Auracast from your mobile phone.

  • If you can’t hear audio from your Fire TV Smart TV speaker after disconnecting a BLE device:

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Audio Devices and Features, and then select Auracast.
    • Turn off Auracast. For more help, go to:

  • Pair BLE or Auracast Headset to Your Fire TV Smart TV Was this information helpful?

Pair BLE or Auracast Headset to Your Fire TV Smart TV

Learn how to pair your BLE/Auracast headset or hearing aids to your Fire TV Smart TV.

Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) audio device refers to any audio device or hearing aid that supports BLE audio or Auracast technology.

Note: The following devices support BLE audio:

  • Panasonic W90/W95 Series Fire TV Smart TV

  • Panasonic Z85 Series Fire TV Smart TV

  • Panasonic Z90/Z93/Z95 Series Fire TV Smart TV Before pairing your BLE audio device for the first time:

  • Fully charge your BLE audio device.

  • Use the manufacturer’s recommended mobile app to update the firmware and configurations.

  • Tip: For some BLE audio devices, you can use the app to turn on BLE Audio.

  • Connect your Fire TV to a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network for the best audio experience.

  • Keep your audio device within 16 ft (5 m) of your Fire TV Smart TV.

  • For hearing aids, make sure that your hearing aid supports BLE audio. To pair your BLE audio device:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Controller and Bluetooth devices.

  • Select Audio devices and features.

  • Select Add New Audio Device, and then do the following:

    • Put your BLE audio device into pairing mode.
    • Select your BLE audio device from the list of available devices on your Fire TV.

  • While using Auracast:

    • Use a Fire TV remote to control content playback.
    • Use the manufacturer’s mobile app to control the volume of your BLE audio device. For more help, go to:

  • Can’t Pair a BLE or Auracast Headset with Fire TV Smart TV

Turn On Subtitles or Closed Captions on Fire TV

You can turn on subtitles or closed captions (“CC”) on your Fire TV device to display the audio for movies and TV shows as text on-screen.

Note: Subtitles may not be available in some languages.

To turn on subtitles:

  • Start playing the video.
  • Press the Menu button on your Fire TV remote or the Fire TV App.
  • Select Subtitles.
  • Select the Off button under Subtitles.
  • Select from the options on-screen to turn captions on.
  • Tip: You can set preferences for the way subtitles display, including text size and style, when enabling the feature.
  • Press the Menu button again to return to video playback with subtitles on. You can turn off the feature by following the same steps and selecting Off.

White Box on the Fire TV Screen

The white box on the Fire TV screen appears when text banner is on. Text banner is an accessibility feature that helps customers with visual impairments and a limited vision range.

The Fire TV experience differs across some devices.

Learn how to navigate the New Fire TV Experience

If a rectangular white box appears on your screen, it’s likely that the text banner feature is on.

To turn off the text banner feature:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select Text Banner to turn it off. To learn more about text banner and other accessibility features on your Fire TV device, go to Accessibility Features for Fire TV.

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Audio, Video, and App Issues on Fire TV ›

4K Ultra HD Not Working on Fire TV Devices

To troubleshoot issues with 4K Ultra HD playback, use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool on your Fire TV device.

The Audio and Video Diagnostics tool checks the capabilities of connected HDMI devices like your TV, soundbar, or AV receiver. The tool tests your TV’s maximum resolution and refresh rate, HDR, and Dolby Vision support. It also detects support for various surround sound standards.

Note: The Audio and Video Diagnostics tool isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

  • Check that your equipment supports the video resolution you’re trying to use. To check supported video settings, use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool on your Fire TV device:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Audio/Video Diagnostics.
  • If the max resolution detected is 4K, but the content you’re streaming is at a lower resolution:
    • Make sure you have a streaming service with a plan that supports streaming in 4K Ultra HD.
    • Check that you have a strong internet connection, and there isn’t any issue with your bandwidth.
    • Go to your TV’s picture or input settings and check that the resolution is configured to 4K, HDR, or FHD. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions if needed.
    • Try moving your Fire TV device closer to the router or use a wired connection with an Ethernet adapter.
    • Make sure you’re using a high-speed HDMI cable. Try to unplug the HDMI cable and plug it in again.
    • Sometimes your Fire TV device streams at 1080p 60 Hz for smoother playback if you have a 4K 30 Hz Dolby Vision TV. Your TV might support 4k 60 Hz resolutions with other formats. To set your resolution to 4K 60 Hz, go to Settings on your Fire TV device and then Display & Sounds.
  • If the resolution you want to use isn’t detected, it can’t be played with your current equipment setup:
    • If you’re using an AV receiver or soundbar, make sure it’s connected to an HDMI port with HDCP 2.2. The port also needs to support pass-through for 4K resolutions.
    • Make sure that your equipment supports 4K resolutions and is set up correctly. Check the user manual that came with your devices or contact the manufacturer for more help. For more help, go to:
  • Dolby Atmos or Surround Sound Not Working on Fire TV Devices
  • Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range Not Working on Fire TV Devices

Alexa Home Theater Isn’t Working with HDMI ARC on Compatible Fire TV Device

If audio from your TV and other HDMI sources (like a game console) isn’t playing through your Echo speakers, try these troubleshooting steps.

Note: The steps to adjust the following settings vary by TV brand and model. Check your TV’s user manual or online support pages for more information.

To get started, check these device settings:

  • Confirm that your TV supports HDMI ARC.

  • Check if your Fire TV device is plugged into the HDMI port labeled “ARC” on your TV. If you have another device connected to HDMI ARC port, move it to a different HDMI port.

  • If you are using an HDMI extender, use the one provided with the Fire TV or ensure that it’s ARC-capable.

  • If you have a sound bar or A/V receiver, unplug it from the HDMI port on your TV.

  • Turn on the HDMI ARC setting on your TV. Use the remote that came with your TV and go to the settings on your device. You can also find steps for some common TV brands on Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.

  • Check the audio settings on your TV. Go to the settings on your TV and select audio settings such as PCM or Stereo. If you have an Echo Studio, select Bypass, Passthrough, or Auto. These terms may vary based on your TV brand.

  • Make sure that you select the HDMI output option on your TV sound output menu. These terms may vary based on your TV brand.

  • Plug your Fire TV device into the HDMI port labeled “ARC” on your TV. If you have another device connected to that port, move it to a different HDMI port. If you’re still having issues with Alexa Home Theater, try these troubleshooting steps:

  • Use your TV’s remote to switch to the HDMI input for your Fire TV device. Then, switch back to your connected device (such as a game console).

  • Restart your ARC connection:

    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV device.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Home Theater Settings.
    • Switch ARC Setup to Disabled to turn it off.
    • Switch ARC Setup to Enabled to turn it on again.

  • Restart both your TV and your Fire TV device. Unplug both devices, wait 1 minute, and then plug them back in.

  • If you’re still having issues, unpair your Echo devices, and then set up Alexa Home Theater again:

    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Alexa Home Theater.
    • Select Edit Alexa Home Theater.
    • Select Unpair and confirm.
    • To set up again and recalibrate your system, select Create Alexa Home Theater. Tip: If you had to move your devices to different HDMI ports, update the port locations on your Fire TV:

  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.

  • Select Equipment Control.

  • Select Manage Equipment.

  • Select the device you had to move.

  • Select the new HDMI port it was plugged into.

  • Repeat these steps for each device that was moved. For more help, go to:

  • Intial Set Up for Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC on Compatible Fire TV Device

App Crashes or Won’t Load on Your Fire TV

If your downloaded app is not working as expected, clear the app cache and data, or restart your device.

If an app on your Fire TV crashes, won’t open or isn’t responding, try these steps:

  • Restart your Fire TV device. You can restart from Settings or unplug the power adapter for one minute, and then plug it back in.
  • Clear the app cache and data. This resets the app without deleting it. Go to Clear App Data and Cache on Fire TV.
  • Uninstall and reinstall the app. This ensures you have the latest version. Go to Uninstall Games & Apps on Your Fire TV.
  • Check for a Fire TV software update. An outdated system can cause app issues. Please follow the below steps:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Devices & Software.
    • Select About.
    • Select Check for System Update. For more help, go to:

Apps Using or Providing Access to Unlicensed Content on Fire TV FAQs

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Audio, Video, and App Issues on Fire TV ›

Apps Using or Providing Access to Unlicensed Content on Fire TV FAQs

1) Why am I seeing this warning message on my Fire TV app?

To protect both customers and content creators, Fire TV disables apps that are identified as using or providing access to unlicensed content. We encourage you to explore the wide range of content options available through the Amazon Appstore.

2) How do you determine which apps to disable?

We have a thorough review process that identifies apps that use or provide access to unlicensed content.

3) This isn’t a piracy app. Why is it disabled? Can I get a refund?

We have a thorough review process that identifies apps that use or provide access to unlicensed content. When an app is identified as using or providing access to unlicensed content, we inform you and provide the option to uninstall. For app-related refunds, please contact the app developer directly. For more information on how to uninstall an app, go to: Uninstall Games and Apps on Your Fire TV.

4) Can I get an exception to keep using this app?

We can’t make exceptions as these measures protect all customers and content creators. Our device protections help safeguard you from risks associated with unlicensed content.

5) Can I stream or mirror these apps from another device?

We don’t have information about other devices. Fire TV disables apps that are identified as using or providing access to unlicensed content.

6) Why are you making these changes now?

To protect both customers and content creators, we recently introduced new measures to identify and disable apps that use or provide access to unlicensed content.

7) Will this change affect my other apps?

Only apps identified as using or providing access to unlicensed content are affected.

8) I bought a Fire TV device specifically for these apps. How can I get a refund?

If you’re eligible, you can return your device within our standard return window. For more information, go to our Online Returns Center.

9) I bought this device from a third-party seller. How can I get a refund?

Please contact the seller of the device regarding refunds for third-party purchases.

10) I purchased an app subscription from a third-party seller. How can I get a refund?

For app-related refunds, please contact the app developer or seller directly.

11) Is there a different app that offers similar content for free?

The Amazon Appstore offers a wide variety of apps, including free options. These apps provide access to various live and streaming content. For more information on how to search and download apps on your Fire TV device, go to Download Apps on Your Fire TV.

Audio Is Out of Sync on Your Fire TV Device

To fix issues with audio delay, go to Settings on your Fire TV and use the AV Sync Slider.

For audio delay issues with a Home Theater setup, use Lip Sync Tuning instead.

Note: The AV Sync Slider isn’t available on all Fire TV Smart TVs.

To use the AV Sync Slider:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Display & Sounds.
  • Select Audio.
  • Select AV Sync Tuning.
  • When audio and video are in sync, every bounce of the on-screen ball happens at the same time as a flash and a tone.
  • Make adjustments:
    • Use the right and left buttons on your Fire TV remote. If the tone happens before the flash appears, move to the right. If the tone happens after the flash appears, move to the left.
    • Press the Select or OK button on your remote to apply the changes.
    • Check if the ball, tone, and flash sync up, and make adjustments as needed. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Clear App Data and Cache on Fire TV

Clear app data and cache on your Fire TV to resolve intermittent app issues or fix any low storage messages that appear on-screen.

Note: For Echo Show devices, you can find Fire TV Settings in your Echo Show Settings.

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

      • Select Clear Cache, and then Clear Data. If you need to uninstall an app from your device, go to Uninstall Games and Apps on Your Fire TV.

Note: If an app is unused for more than 30 days and the device is running low on storage, the storage optimizing feature will automatically clear the app cache. This feature runs in the background and can’t be deactivated.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Dolby Atmos or Surround Sound Not Working on Fire TV Devices

To troubleshoot issues with Dolby Atmos or surround sound, use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool on your Fire TV device.

Note: The Audio and Video Diagnostics tool isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

  • Check that your equipment supports the audio format you’re trying to use. To check supported audio settings, use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool on your Fire TV device:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds
    • Select Audio/Video Diagnostics to display supported settings.
  • If the audio format you want to use is detected, but you’re not getting that format from the content you’re streaming:
    • Use the test video at the bottom of the page to confirm that your equipment setup supports surround sound.
    • Check that the content supports surround sound.
  • If the audio format you want to use isn’t detected, it can’t be played with your current equipment setup:
    • Make sure that your equipment supports surround sound and is set up correctly. Some AVRs will require height speakers for Atmos support. Check the user manual that came with your devices or contact the manufacturer for more help.
    • Make sure that you’re using a high-speed HDMI cable. Optical cables don’t fully support surround sound.
    • Connect your Fire TV device directly to the HDMI input on your soundbar or AV receiver. You can use another HDMI cable to connect your soundbar or AV receiver to the HDMI ARC input on your TV.
    • Change your audio format to a lower setting. Go to Settings on your Fire TV device and then Display & Sounds.

Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range Not Working on Fire TV Devices

To troubleshoot issues with Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range (HDR), use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool on your Fire TV device.

The Audio and Video Diagnostics tool checks the capabilities of connected HDMI devices like your TV, soundbar, or AV receiver. The tool tests your TV’s maximum resolution and refresh rate, HDR, and Dolby Vision support. It also detects support for various surround sound standards.

Note: The Audio and Video Diagnostics tool isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

  • Check that your equipment supports Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range (HDR). To check supported audio settings, use the Audio and Video Diagnostics tool:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds
    • Select Audio/Video Diagnostics.
  • If your TV supports HDR, but the content you’re streaming is in a different format:
    • Confirm that your TV supports Dolby Vision or HDR formats by using the test video at the bottom of the page.
    • Check that the content supports HDR.
    • Go to your TV’s picture or input settings and check that the resolution is 4K, HDR, or FHD. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions if needed.
  • If the Audio/Video Diagnostics tool doesn’t detect the format that you want to use, check your current equipment setup:
    • Make sure that your TV supports Dolby Vision or HDR. If you’re connecting your Fire TV device to an AV Receiver or soundbar, make sure it’s able to pass-through Dolby Vision or HDR formats.
    • Sometimes your Fire TV device streams at 1080p 60 Hz for smoother playback if you have a 4K 30 Hz Dolby Vision TV. To set your resolution to 4K 60 Hz, go to Settings from your Fire TV menu and then Display & Sounds. For more help, go to:
  • Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range Not Working on Fire TV Smart TV Was this information helpful?

Troubleshoot Cloud Apps on Fire TV

Try these troubleshooting steps if you encounter a blocked UDP port issue while using Cloud Apps.

Follow these troubleshooting steps if your Fire TV displays an error message about a blocked UDP port while using Cloud Apps.

  • Access your router’s admin panel
    • Open a web browser on your computer
    • Enter your router’s IP address (typically 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1)
    • Log in with your router credentials
  • Unblock required UDP ports for streaming services
    • Go to Advanced Settings or Firewall Settings in your router admin panel
    • Select Port Forwarding or Port Settings
    • Allow public UDP ports in the range 2001-65535
    • Save your changes
    • Restart your router
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
  • Select My Fire TV.
  • Select Restart. If the issue persists, contact your internet service provider to ensure that the required ports for streaming services are not blocked.

About Auto Offload on Fire TV

When your device is low on storage, the Auto Offload feature helps to free up storage by offloading infrequently used apps.

After 60 days, unused apps may be offloaded automatically. Offloaded apps save your login information and settings preferences so you can easily redownload the app and start using it again.

When an app is offloaded, a cloud icon appears on the app.

Note: To use Auto Offload, you need an internet connection.

You can also choose which apps you’d like to offload by:

  • Going to Manage Installed Applications in your Fire TV settings.
  • Highlighting an app and pressing the Menu button on your remote.
  • Note: For devices with the New Fire TV Experience, press and hold the Select button. Auto Offload is on by default on your device. You can turn Auto Offload on or off in your Fire TV settings by going to Applications, and then Auto Offload.

The storage optimizer isn’t available on:

  • Fire TV devices that have Kids profiles set up
  • Amazon Fire TV (2nd Generation)
  • Amazon Fire TV (1st Generation)
  • Fire TV Stick (2nd Generation)
  • Fire TV Stick (1st Generation)

Fire TV Devices Low Power Mode

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Change Device Settings on Fire TV ›

Fire TV Devices Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode is available on select Fire TVs, Fire TV Sticks, and other accompanying devices.

Low Power Mode is an energy-saving feature that reduces power consumption when your Fire TV device enters sleep mode.

Your Fire TV device goes into Low Power Mode when the device goes to sleep. This occurs due to inactivity or if you put the device to sleep manually through the Settings menu.

Your device exits sleep mode when you wake up the device by pressing the Select button on your Fire TV remote.

Certain features or settings prevent your devices from maximizing the energy efficiency gains from Low Power Mode in an idle state.

These include:

  • When you activate “Alexa Anytime” using the “Voice Commands When TV Screen is Off” setting on your Fire TV.
  • When you set up your TV using the process in this Frustration Free Setup help page.
  • When you turn on/off your TV using a paired Alexa device.
  • Changing the Sleep Mode Behavior setting to Black Screen in Display settings prevents the device from turning off HDMI on your Fire TV device. Note: If your Fire TV device has the Low Power Mode feature, the mode activates by default when your device goes to sleep. You can’t deactivate this feature.

Initial Set Up for Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC on Compatible Fire TV Device

To play audio from your TV and other HDMI sources (like a game console) through your Echo speakers, set up Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC.

The following Fire TV devices are compatible with Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC:

  • Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)

  • Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation)

  • Fire TV Stick 4K Max (1st Generation)

  • Fire TV Stick 4K (2nd Generation)

  • Fire TV Stick 4K Plus To set up Alexa Home Theater, you need:

  • A compatible Fire TV device.

  • Compatible Echo devices. For a list of compatible devices, go to Alexa Home Theater Device Compatibility Guide.

  • A TV that supports HDMI ARC. To check if your TV supports this setting, review your TV’s user manual or online support pages. To set up Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC:

  • Plug your Fire TV device into the HDMI port labeled “ARC” on your TV. If you have another device connected to that port, move it to a different HDMI port.

  • For TV Cube (3rd Generation), plug the HDMI cable from the Fire TV Cube into the HDMI port labeled “ARC” on your TV.

  • If you have a sound bar or A/V receiver, unplug it from the HDMI port on your TV. Alexa Home Theater only supports playing audio through Echo devices.

  • Turn on the HDMI ARC setting on your TV with the remote that came with your TV. You may need to turn on the HDMI CEC setting manually.

  • Tip: For step-by-step instructions on how to turn on the HDMI CEC setting on your TV, go to Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.

  • Check the audio settings on your TV. Go to the settings on your TV and select audio settings such as PCM or Stereo. If you have an Echo Studio, select Bypass, Passthrough, or Auto. These terms vary based on your TV brand.

  • To finish setting up your Alexa Home Theater, go to Set Up Alexa Home Theater on Your Fire TV. If you move your devices to different HDMI ports, update the port locations on your Fire TV:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Equipment Control.

  • Select Manage Equipment.

  • Select the device that you had to move.

  • Select the new HDMI port that you plugged it into.

  • Repeat these steps for each device that you moved. For more help, go to:

  • Alexa Home Theater on Fire TV Stick 4K Max Isn’t Working

  • Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV Was this information helpful?

Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV

Follow these steps to turn on the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on some common TV brands.

Turning on HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC is different for every TV brand. These steps are general guidelines for some common TV brands. The steps may vary from model to model or may change when TV software is updated.

If your TV brand isn’t listed or the steps don’t match, check your TV’s user manual or online support pages for more information.

Note: You may need to turn on HDMI CEC and HDMI ARC to use some Fire TV features.

To jump to your HDMI CEC set up instructions, please select your TV brand in the table below:

Brand

HDMI CEC Name

Samsung

Anynet+

LG

SIMPLINK

Sony

BRAVIA Sync

Sharp

AQUOS Link

Toshiba

CE-Link or Regza Link

Hitachi

HDMI-CEC

Panasonic

HDAVI Control, EZ Sync, or VIERA Link

Phillips

EasyLink

Roku TV ™

CEC

Vizio

CEC

Samsung

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Home button on your Samsung remote.

  • Go to Settings on your device.

  • Select System.

  • Select Expert Settings.

  • Select Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC).

  • Select On. Some TVs may use the following steps for HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Home button on your Samsung remote.

  • Go to Settings on your device.

  • Select General.

  • Select External Device Manager.

  • Select Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC).

  • Select On. HDMI ARC:

ARC is turned on automatically on Samsung TVs when Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) is on.

LG

HDMI CEC:

  • Go to the settings menu. Press and hold the Settings button on your LG remote for 5 seconds.
  • Select All Settings.
  • Select General.
  • Select SIMPLINK (HDMI-CEC).
  • Set SIMPLINK (HDMI-CEC) to On. HDMI ARC:

Note: SIMPLINK must be turned on using the HDMI CEC steps before you can use HDMI ARC.

  • Go to the settings menu. Press and hold the Settings button on your LG remote for 5 seconds.
  • Select All Settings.
  • Select Sound.
  • Select Sound Out.
  • Select Audio Out (Optical/HDMI ARC).
  • Set Digital Sound Out to Auto.
Sony

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Home button on your Sony remote.

  • Select Settings.

  • Press OK.

  • Select Watching TV.

  • Select External inputs.

  • Select BRAVIA Sync settings.

  • Turn on BRAVIA Sync control. HDMI ARC:

  • Press the Home button on your Sony remote.

  • Select Settings.

  • Press OK.

  • Select Display & Sound.

  • Select Audio output.

  • Set eARC mode to Auto.

Sharp

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Sharp TV remote.

  • Select System Options.

  • Select AQUOS Link Setup.

  • Set AQUOS Link Control to On. HDMI ARC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Sharp TV remote.

  • Select System Options.

  • Select AQUOS Link Setup.

  • Set Audio Return Channel to Auto.

Toshiba

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Toshiba TV remote.

  • Select Settings.

  • Select System.

  • Select HDMI & CEC Functions.

  • Set CEC Control to On and detect the connected HDMI device. HDMI ARC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Toshiba TV remote.

  • Select Settings.

  • Select System.

  • Select Sounds.

  • Select Speakers.

  • Set Audio output to ARC.

Hitachi

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Hitachi remote.

  • Go to Setup.

  • Select HDMI-CEC.

  • Select On. HDMI ARC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Hitachi remote.

  • Go to Setup.

  • Select ARC.

  • Select On.

Panasonic

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Panasonic remote.

  • Select Setup from the menu options.

  • Select HDMI Control.

  • Select CEC Function

  • Select On. HDMI ARC:

  • Press the Menu button on your Panasonic remote.

  • Select Setup from the menu options.

  • Select VIERA Link.

  • Select On.

Phillips

HDMI CEC:

  • Press the Home button on your Phillips remote.
  • Go to Setup and then select TV Settings.
  • Select Installation.
  • Select Preferences.
  • Select EasyLink and set the following:
    • EasyLink: On
    • Master EasyLink: On
    • Auto: On
    • RC Key Forwarding: On HDMI ARC:
  • Press the Home button on your Phillips remote.
  • Go to Setup and then select TV Settings.
  • Select Installation.
  • Select Preferences.
  • Select EasyLink.
  • Set HDMI-ARC to On.
Roku TV ™

HDMI CEC

  • Press the Home button on your Roku remote.
  • Select Settings.
  • Select System.
  • Select Control other devices (CEC) and turn on the following:
    • System audio control
    • 1-touch play HDMI ARC
  • Press the Home button on your Roku remote.
  • Select Settings.
  • Select System.
  • Select Control other devices (CEC) and turn on ARC.
Vizio

HDMI CEC

  • Press the Menu button on your Vizio remote.

  • Select System.

  • Select CEC and turn on CEC Function. HDMI ARC

  • Press the Menu button on your Vizio remote.

  • Select System.

  • Select CEC and turn on the CEC Function.

  • Set System Audio Control to On.

  • Select Device Discovery and wait for your TV to discover your Roku device. Was this information helpful?

Set Parental Controls on Fire TV

Turn on parental controls to restrict access to videos, purchases, and certain types of content.

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Preferences and then select Parental Controls.
  • To activate or deactivate parental controls, select the Parental Controls option and enter your PIN.
  • Select the options that you want to PIN protect. You can turn on or off PIN protections for the available options on your device. Depending on the options you turn on, you have to enter your PIN before watching videos in restricted categories, purchasing content, or opening apps.

Note: For Echo Show devices, you can find Fire TV Settings in your Echo Show Settings.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Use Your Amazon Fire TV in a Different Country

Take compatible Amazon Fire TV devices with you if you’re moving or traveling outside your home country.

Note: Residents of the European Union, while traveling within the European Union, have access to the same titles that are available when streaming from their country of residence.

Amazon Fire TV devices work in the following supported countries:

  • Australia
  • Austria
  • Brazil
  • Canada
  • France
  • Germany
  • India
  • Ireland
  • Italy
  • Japan
  • Mexico
  • Netherlands
  • Poland
  • Spain
  • Sweden
  • United Kingdom
  • United States Fire TV Stick Basic Edition works in:

Albania, Barbados, Belgium, Bermuda, Bolivia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Cambodia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Ecuador, Estonia, Finland, Ghana, Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Jamaica, Kenya, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Macao, Malta, Namibia, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Panama, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Trinidad & Tobago, Uruguay, Venezuela.

To use your compatible device in a different supported country, change the country settings for your Amazon account.

Important:

  • Content availability varies by country.
  • When you change the country settings for your Amazon account, you’ll no longer be able to access any of your Prime Video purchases or rentals. Your purchases will still be available if you change back to your original country settings, but any rentals will no longer be available.
  • Some apps and games may not work in your new country. If you have questions about app compatibility, contact the app developer.
Watch While Abroad

Note: Residents of the European Union, while traveling within the European Union, have access to the same titles that are available when streaming from their country of residence.

The Movies and TV Shows categories in the Fire TV menu change automatically to include Watch While Abroad rows. These rows show all titles included with Prime that are available to watch while traveling abroad without changing your account settings.

For more help, go to:

Audio Playback in the Fire TV Ambient Experience

Listen to and control audio playback while in the Ambient Experience, or switch to full-screen audio interaction.

Note: The Fire TV Ambient Experience isn’t available on all Fire TV devices. To check if Fire TV Ambient Experience is available on your device:

  • Select Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • If available, the Ambient Experience option appears in the menu. While in the Ambient Experience start an audio stream by:

  • Voice request (“Play music from my library.”)

  • Casting audio from a mobile phone.

  • Note: If casting audio from an app, such as Spotify, make sure the app is installed on the Fire TV device and signed into the correct account. When audio plays in the Ambient Experience, a “Now Playing” indicator appears on-screen. It shows album art, current playback state, the artist, and song. Control the audio with the remote buttons or your voice.

While audio is playing in the normal Fire TV experience, short-press the power button or say, “Go to Ambient.” Audio playback continues in the Ambient Experience, with the “Now Playing” indicator on the screen. To switch back to the full-screen audio playback, use your voice to open the specific app or press the Select or OK button on the remote with the “Now Playing” indicator selected on the screen.

Connect Fire TV to Supported Third-Party Devices

Use your voice to control supported third-party devices, such as antennas, soundbars and AV receivers.

Before getting started, locate the remotes for the devices you’re connecting to Fire TV.

Fire TV devices automatically detect compatible equipment and provide an on-screen interface to add them. If equipment isn’t detected, or you’d like to set up Equipment Control manually, follow the steps on this page.

To connect your devices:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment.
  • Note: Select Advanced Settings on this screen to activate or deactivate Automated Device Discovery.
  • Select Add Equipment and choose the equipment you’d like to add. For supported devices visit Compatible Devices for Fire TV and Alexa Equipment Control.

Control Your Smart Home on Fire TV

Your Fire TV can act as a smart home command center, letting you monitor cameras and control your devices without missing your shows.

What Is the Smart Home Dashboard?

The smart home dashboard is a hub for viewing your connected smart home.

You can control your Alexa-compatible smart home devices, such as smart lights, plugs, or switches.

To use the dashboard, you need:

  • A compatible Fire TV device
  • One or more smart devices connected to Alexa
How to Access the Smart Home Dashboard

You can access the Fire TV Smart Home Dashboard several ways:

  • Voice: Say, Show my smart home dashboard.
  • Alexa Voice button: Short press the Alexa Voice button on the remote to open the Alexa Shortcuts Panel, and then select the smart home tile.

Create AI Art in the Fire TV Ambient Experience

Use your voice to describe an image you want to display and then watch it come to life on your Fire TV.

Note: The Fire TV Ambient Experience isn’t available on all Fire TV devices. To check if Fire TV Ambient Experience is available on your device:

You can say things like:

  • “Create an image of a cyberpunk city in Yosemite.”

  • Choose from a range of suggestions to create new variations of your image.

  • Select Show more to generate more images based on your original description.

  • Save the image to the AI Art collection in your Ambient Gallery.

    • You can also find your AI Art collection on Amazon Photos. Once you save an image, you can set your AI Art collection as the Ambient background on your Fire TV.

How Does the Continue Watching Row Work?

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Device Features on Fire TV ›

How Does the Continue Watching Row Work?

The Continue Watching row on your home screen helps you find your recently watched shows from Prime Video and supported third-party apps.

The Continue Watching row syncs across your compatible Fire TV devices and reflects the viewing activity of the profile you’re using. Compatibility varies across Fire TV devices.

Note: This feature isn’t available on Kids profiles.

When you open a supported app, a message appears on-screen about personalizing your Fire TV. To turn on this feature for all supported apps, select Accept. You can also turn on this feature by going to Manage Sharing from Apps in your Fire TV’s Privacy Settings.

Tip: You can manage your privacy settings at any time by following the steps in Manage Sharing of Viewing Information from Apps on Fire TV.

While this feature is on, supported third-party apps share your viewing and content information with Amazon. Shared information includes:

  • Watching activity

  • Watchlist

  • Recordings

  • Purchases For more help, go to:

  • Remove Movies and Shows from Continue Watching on Fire TV Was this information helpful?

Learn to Use Alexa with Fire TV

Perform specific actions, and watch and listen to content on your Fire TV device with Alexa.

Note: Alexa features and services may vary by country.

Compatible devices allow you to use your voice to activate Alexa.

Using Your Voice Remote

To interact with Alexa, hold down the Alexa Voice button on your remote and talk to Alexa. You can say things like:

  • “Open [app name].”
  • “Find [movie title].”
  • “Search for action movies.”
  • “Look for racing game apps.”
  • “Play some study music.” Alexa gives helpful information about topics related to your viewing or listening content and can also do things like control playback.

Many features open in a separate display on your TV screen. To return to the previous screen, press the Back button or Home button on your Fire TV remote.

Control Fire TV Devices with a Compatible Alexa-enabled Device

You can link a compatible Alexa-enabled device to your Fire TV for more voice control options. Linking your devices lets you use your Alexa device to do things like search for content or control playback on your Fire TV. Use the Alexa app to link your devices.

Some Fire TV devices have Alexa built-in for hands-free voice control. For the best experience, make sure that there’s nothing blocking the Alexa microphones on your device.

Manage Alexa Features and Privacy

To manage settings for most Alexa features, use the Alexa app on your compatible mobile device.

Fire TV devices with hands-free Alexa come equipped with a microphone off button. When you press the Microphone On/Off button, the power to the microphones disconnects and a dedicated red light turns on.

After the microphones are off, your device can’t record and stream audio to the cloud, even when you say the wake word. Your device still responds to requests you make through your Voice Remote.

To manage parental consent for Alexa and other Amazon kid services, visit the Manage Parental Consent page.

For more information, visit the Alexa and Alexa Device FAQs page.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Set Up Alexa Home Theater on Your Fire TV

To create a cinematic surround sound experience through Alexa Home Theater, pair your Echo speakers and an optional subwoofer with your Fire TV device.

  • Alexa Home Theater Supported Configurations
  • Basic requirements
  • Video guide to setup your Alexa Home Theater
  • How to set up your Alexa Home Theater
  • You’re Set Up, What’s Next?
  • Troubleshoot setup issues
  • Play Audio from Your Fire TV on Your Echo Devices
Alexa Home Theater Supported Configurations

You can create Alexa Home Theater by pairing up to five Echo speakers and one optional subwoofer with the following Fire TV and Echo device combinations. Pairing mixed Echo speaker configurations is not supported.

  • Fire TV devices:
    • Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)
    • Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation)
    • Fire TV Stick 4K (2nd Generation)
    • Fire TV Stick 4K Plus
  • Compatible Echo devices:
    • Echo Studio (2025 release)
    • Echo Dot Max
    • Echo Sub Some Fire TV devices support up to two Echo speakers of the same model and a subwoofer . Pairing mixed Echo speaker configurations is not supported. To check Fire TV device compatibility with the Echo speakers, go to Alexa Home Theater Compatibility with Fire TV Devices.

Back to top

Basic requirements

To start, have the following set up ready:

  • Set up your Fire TV device. Visit Set Up Your Fire TV for more information.
  • Set up your Echo devices. For more guidance, go to Set Up Your Echo.
  • Note: Consider saving your Wi-Fi password to Amazon for automatic registration for any new devices. For more details, go to Saving Your Network Passwords to Amazon FAQs.
  • To set up Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC, make sure to plug your Fire TV device into HDMI ARC port. For more guidance, visit Initial Set Up for Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC on Compatible Fire TV Device. Back to top
Video guide to setup your Alexa Home Theater

Back to top

How to set up your Alexa Home Theater

To set up Alexa Home Theater on your Fire TV:

Note: If you have purchased an Alexa Home Theater bundle, you can follow the on-screen instructions to set up your home theater once you complete the Fire TV setup. Otherwise, follow the steps below.

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Display & Sounds.
  • Select Alexa Home Theater.
  • Select Create Alexa Home Theater.
  • Select the compatible Echo speakers. Optionally, you can add a subwoofer.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to configure your system:
    • Select at least two Echo speakers and press Next to calibrate when using:
      • Echo Studio (2025 release)
      • Echo Dot Max
    • For other Echo speakers and configurations, select Next to confirm the placement of the speakers.
  • When the setup is complete, your Alexa Home Theater is ready for use. To exit setup, select either Home or Watch Preview. Back to top
You’re Set Up, What’s Next?

To optimize your Alexa Home Theater experience, try following:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Display & Sounds.
  • Select Alexa Home Theater:
    • Select Audio Output:
      • Select Home Theater to play and control audio through your Echo devices.
      • Select Television to control Alexa Home Theater through your television. Use this option for gaming or latency sensitive use cases.
    • Select Lip Sync Tuning to reduce any audio lags. If your TV supports HDMI ARC, you can set up Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC to play audio from your TV and other HDMI sources (like a game console) play through your Echo speakers. To learn more, visit Initial Set Up for Alexa Home Theater with HDMI ARC on Compatible Fire TV Sticks.

Back to top

Troubleshoot setup issues

To troubleshoot setup issues with Alexa Home Theater, try the following:

  • Confirm that the software on all devices is up to date:
    • Echo device: Ask Alexa to “Check for software updates” to install the latest software version.
    • Fire TV device: Go to Update the Software on Your Fire TV.
  • Confirm that the Echo speakers are in the same room as your TV and connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • If your Echo speaker doesn’t appear on the device selection screen, select Rescan to search for available devices.
  • If your Echo speaker is grayed out on the device selection screen, make sure to select Echo speakers of the same model.
  • If your Echo Sub doesn’t appear on the device selection screen, try the following:
    • If your Echo Sub is already paired with another Echo speaker, it doesn’t appear during the setup. Unpair any existing connections before adding your Echo Sub to your home theater system.
    • Restart your Echo Sub. Unplug it from power, wait for 30 seconds, then plug it back in. A small LED next to the power cable should blink orange.
    • Go to the Alexa App and follow Set Up Your Echo Sub.
  • If your Echo Sub displays an updating software message, try the following:
    • When you register Echo Sub on your account through Alexa App, device software will automatically update. It may take 30 minutes or up to 24 hours.
    • Wait for software updates to complete, and then try to set up your Alexa Home Theater with your Echo Sub again.
  • If you experience an issue calibrating your system, try the following:
    • Plug in your Echo speakers and unmute the microphone on all speakers.
    • Check your Echo speakers and subwoofer placement:
      • Place your Echo speakers around the listening area, at eye level when you’re at your desired seating position.
      • If you have two or fewer speakers, place them in front of the room on the left and right side of the TV.
      • Place your Echo Sub on the floor, next to the TV.
      • Avoid placing your speakers next to noise sources (fans, heaters, air purifiers).
    • Don’t obstruct your speakers or place them in enclosed spaces.
    • Make sure you set your TV’s audio output to TV speakers. Turn up the volume, and then verify that sound is coming out of the speakers.
    • For larger rooms, consider placing your rear speakers closer to the listening area.
    • Ensure a quiet environment during the calibration process for the best results.
    • If the issue persists, restart your speakers and Fire TV device. Then try to set up Alexa Home Theater again.
  • If you experience issues with the quality of the audio:
    • Play audio from different streaming services to ensure that the issue isn’t provider specific.
    • Recreate your Alexa Home Theater:
      • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
      • Select Display & Sounds.
      • Select Alexa Home Theater.
      • Select Edit Alexa Home Theater.
      • Select Unpair and confirm.
      • To set up again and recalibrate your system, select Create Alexa Home Theater. Back to top

Set Up Alexa Two-Way Video Calling on Your Fire TV Device

To make video calls, connect a compatible webcam to your Fire TV device.

Alexa Two-Way video calling is supported on these devices:

  • Amazon Ember Artline TVs (2026 Release)
  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series TVs (2024 Release)
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series
  • Fire TV Omni Series
  • Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)
  • Fire TV Cube (2nd Generation) Note: The webcam is not included with the device and must be purchased separately.

To make video calls, your webcam needs:

  • A USB 2.0 connection cable
  • At least 720p resolution
  • At least 30 frames per second, uncompressed Note: If you have a Fire TV Cube (2nd Generation), you also need a USB 2.0 to micro USB adapter.

Webcams with 1080p resolution and 60-to-90 degree field of vision from 8.5 feet (3 m) are recommended.

To make video calls:

  • Plug a compatible webcam into the USB port on your Fire TV device.
    • If you want to use Ethernet, make sure to use an adapter that has a port for USB and Ethernet.
  • Complete setup for Alexa Calling and Messaging in the Alexa app.
  • To make a call, say, “Call [contact’s] Echo.” Important: The video on Fire TV Cube is off by default. To turn it on for video calling, make a call, and say, “Video on.” You can also press the menu button on your remote and activate the video. When you end the call, your video turns off automatically.

For more help, go to:

  • Alexa Calling and Messaging Was this information helpful?

Troubleshoot Hearing Aid and Device Connectivity with Fire TV

Try these troubleshooting steps if you can’t pair your Bluetooth hearing aids or have issues with audio quality or with syncing.

Note: Compatible Starkey hearing aids, Widex hearing aids, and Cochlear hearing devices are supported on:

  • Fire TV Cube (2nd Generation)

  • Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)

  • Amazon Ember Artline TV (2026 Release)

  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)

  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series

  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)

  • Fire TV Omni Series

  • Fire TV 4-Series

  • Amazon Ember 4-Series and Fire TV 4-Series (2025 Release)

  • Fire TV 2-Series

  • Amazon Ember 2-Series and Fire TV 2-Series (2025 Release) To troubleshoot issues with your hearing aids:

  • Disconnect your hearing aids from other Bluetooth devices. You can’t pair multiple devices to hearing aids when connected to your Fire TV device.

  • Make sure that your hearing aids are in pairing mode. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions.

  • Fully charge your hearing aids and make sure to turn them on.

  • Make sure that you’re within 10 ft (3 m) of your Fire TV device and have line of sight.

  • Restart your hearing aids following the manufacturer’s instructions.

  • Try to connect your Fire TV device over the 5 GHz Wi-Fi.

  • If paired, disconnect your hearing aids from the Fire TV device:

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Accessibility .
    • Select Hearing Aids and choose your hearing aids.
    • Select Disconnect Hearing Aids.

  • Try to connect your hearing aids to the Fire TV device again:

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Accessibility .
    • Select Hearing Aids.
    • Select Connect. For more help, go to:

  • Accessibility Features for Fire TV Was this information helpful?

Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV

Learn how to use your compatible Alexa devices to control certain features on your Fire TV.

Just tell your Alexa device what you want to do, and Alexa completes the action directly on your Fire TV–no remote needed.

Note: Some voice commands are only available in select languages.

Compatible Devices

You can find your compatible Alexa devices when you link your Fire TV in the Alexa app.

This feature requires both the latest Fire TV device software update and the latest version of the Alexa app. Echo Show devices don’t support all features.

Link Your Devices

You can find steps to link your devices on Link Your Fire TV and Alexa Device.

Note:

  • You can link multiple Alexa devices to the same Fire TV.
  • To link your Alexa and Fire TV devices, you must register them to the same account.
Control Your Fire TV

Once you’ve completed the linking process, this table lists common features that you can control on your Fire TV using Alexa devices:

To do this on your Fire TV…

Say this to your Alexa device…

Play a movie or TV show:

Alexa can play content from Prime Video and other supported apps installed on your Fire TV.

“Watch [title].”

“Play [title].

“Play [title] on [app].”

Search for movies and TV shows:

Alexa can find movies and TV shows from Prime Video and supported installed apps.

“Search for [title].”

“Find [title / genre].”

“Show me [tv shows / movies] with [actor].”

“Show me new [tv shows / movies].”

“Search for free [tv shows / movies].

Play music:

Alexa can play music from your connected audio providers.

“Play [song / album / artist].”

“Play the latest episode of my podcast.”

“Play relaxing music.”

Navigate search results:

Alexa can navigate through search results and select items by voice.

“Scroll [direction].”

“Select #3.”

“Play #6.”

“Go back.”

Browse Fire TV:

You can use Alexa to navigate through the page and select items.

“Go Home.”

“Show more.”

“Scroll down.”

“Select [row number].”

“Go to my video library.”

Watch and browse content on video details page:

You can use Alexa to control playback and get details on Movie and TV show detail pages.

“Play this movie.”

“Watch trailer.”

“Add this to my Watchlist.”

“Show me [episodes/seasons].”

Open and search within apps:

You can use Alexa to open a previously installed supported app and search for movies and TV shows by voice.

“Open app.”

“Find [title / genre].”

“Show me [movies / TV shows]”

“Find [actor] movies.”

Browse within apps:

You can use Alexa to browse within supported apps by voice.

“Select.”

“Scroll [right / left / up / down].”

“Move [right / left / up / down].”

Control playback:

Alexa can control playback for movies and TV shows from Prime Video. Alexa can also control playback for supported installed apps.

“Play.”

“Pause.”

“Stop.”

“Resume.”

“Rewind [timeframe].”

“Fast-forward [timeframe].”

“Go back [timeframe].”

“Jump forward [timeframe].”

“Next / Next Episode.”

“Watch from beginning.”

Live TV Controls:

For supported apps that feature live TV access, you can use Alexa to change channels or control playback for on-demand programming.

You can also use Alexa to navigate to the Channel Guide and the Live tab.

“Go to [channel / network] on [app].”

“Watch [channel / network].”

“Go to Channel Guide.”

“Go to Live.”

Alexa Requests:

Check the response on Fire TV when you make an Alexa request.

“Show me the weather.”

“Show me my To Do List.”

“Show me songs by [artist].”

“Show me restaurants nearby.”

“Show me the [device name] camera.”

“Show me the nursery camera.”

Note: You may need to clarify that you’d like to stream on a Fire TV device by adding, “on Fire TV” to the end of your request.

Watch Live TV on Fire TV

You can watch live TV on supported apps and browse what’s airing from the Fire TV home screen.

Note: Some apps require a paid subscription.

To watch live TV on your device:

  • Download apps that offer live TV content from the app store.

  • Note: If you have a Fire TV Smart TV, you can connect a live TV source (like a digital antenna) to your device. To learn more, visit Connect a Live TV Source to Your Fire TV Smart TV.

  • Scan for channels:

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Live TV .
    • Select Channel Scan.
    • Follow the on-screen instructions.

  • Choose a show that you’d like to watch. To browse what’s currently airing, go to the On Now row on your home screen or use the Guide button on your remote.

  • You can also go to Live from your home screen. You can customize or favorite channels on your Fire TV. To add a favorite or manage channels on your Live TV:

  • While watching a channel, select the Left or Guide button on your remote to open Channel Guide.

  • Select the Menu button on your remote.

  • Select Add to Favorite Channels or Add & Manage Channels to customize your channel preferences. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Watch Video in 4K Ultra HD on Your Fire TV Device

Watch Video in 4K Ultra HD on Your Fire TV Device

Compatible Fire TV devices automatically detect if your equipment can stream videos in 4K Ultra HD.

Tip: When you connect your Fire TV to a compatible Ultra HD TV, your home screen typically includes “4K Ultra HD” rows with popular titles.

To watch 4K Ultra HD on Your Fire TV, you need:

  • A high-speed internet connection of at least 15 Mbps. Some video apps (for example, Netflix) recommend at least 20 Mbps.

  • An Ultra HD TV with at least one HDMI input that supports HDCP 2.2 content protection standards.

  • Devices that support HDCP 2.2, including all the devices in your home theater setup (such as AV receivers and soundbars).

  • The resolution of your TV configured to 4K, HDR, or FHD. To find the resolution options, check your TV’s picture or input settings and follow the manufacturer’s instructions if needed. To check if your TV supports HDCP 2.2:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • Select Display.

  • Select Video Resolution.

  • Set your video resolution to Auto. A notification displays if HDCP 2.2 isn’t detected for your Fire TV’s HDMI connection. Tip: Some HDMI ports on your Ultra HD TV may not support HDCP 2.2. Ports labeled “Mobile High-Definition Link” (MHL), “HDCP 2.2,” “UHD,” or “4K” typically support HDCP 2.2. The user guide or product packaging for your TV may have more information.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

What Is Equipment Control with Fire TV?

Equipment control lets you control several functions of compatible devices like TVs, A/V receivers, and soundbars.

To control your connected equipment after setup:

Use Your Compatible Fire TV Remote

Pair a Fire TV remote that has volume and power buttons and an Alexa Voice button to your Fire TV. You can use the buttons on your remote to do things like turn your devices on or off or change the volume. You can also press the Alexa Voice button on your remote and use voice commands. Say things like, “Turn up the volume,” or “Turn off the TV.”

Use Your Fire TV Cube

Use the built-in microphone in Fire TV Cube to ask Alexa to do things like turn your devices on or off or change the volume. You can also link a compatible Alexa device with your Fire TV Cube and use your Alexa device to control your equipment.

Use Your Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote

Pair a Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote with your compatible Fire TV Smart TV. You can use the buttons on your remote to do things like turn your devices on or off or change the volume. You can also press the microphone button on your remote and use voice commands. Say things like, “Turn up the volume,” or “Turn off the TV.”

Use Hands-Free Voice Control

This information applies to:

  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)
  • Amazon Ember Artline TVs (2026 Release)
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series
  • Fire TV Omni Series Use the built-in microphone on the TV to ask Alexa to do things like turn your devices on or off or change the volume. You can also use Alexa to control your connected equipment.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

What Is the Fire TV Ambient Experience?

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Device Features on Fire TV ›

What Is the Fire TV Ambient Experience?

The Fire TV Ambient Experience transforms a TV into an Alexa-powered smart display when not streaming.

Note: The Fire TV Ambient Experience isn’t available on all Fire TV devices. To check if Fire TV Ambient Experience is available on your device:

  • Select Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Display & Sounds.
  • If available, the Ambient Experience option appears in the menu. The following table lists some of the Ambient Experience features:

Feature

Description

Display curated art collections as backgrounds.

Choose backgrounds from curated art collections. You can also use your own personal Amazon Photos.

Display Interactive Art.

Note: This feature is only available on the following devices:

  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Amazon Ember Artline TVs (2026 Release) Display artwork that you can interact with through movement. Choose from select interactive backgrounds.

Display the time and weather.

Quickly check the time and weather for your location.

Listen to audio in the background.

While enjoying background art, you can play music, podcasts, and audiobooks from providers such as Amazon Music, Audible, and Spotify.

Note: Some services require a paid subscription.

Play audio.

If audio is playing when Ambient Experience is active, a Now Playing indicator appears on the screen. You can use the remote to pause the music or say, “Pause music.”

To open the full-screen audio experience, select the audio player with the remote. To return to the Ambient Experience, say, “Return to Ambient,” or short-press the power button.

Activate and Deactivate the Ambient Experience

You can activate the Ambient Experience in several ways:

  • Alexa Voice button: Short press the Alexa Voice button on the remote to open the Alexa Shortcuts Panel. Select the Ambient tile to start the Ambient Experience.

  • Home button: Press and hold the Home button on the remote to open the Quick Settings menu. Select the Ambient tile to start the Ambient Experience.

  • Voice: Say, “Go to Ambient Experience.”

  • Schedule or Routine: Set up Routines for Ambient Experience in the Alexa mobile app. The Ambient Experience Advanced Settings include the ability to set the hours when Ambient Experience is available.

  • Idle timeout: Ambient Experience replaces the default screensaver experience and starts after the screensaver advertisements.

  • Fire TV Main Menu: On devices with the New Fire TV Experience, you can select Ambient from the Fire TV menu.

  • Note: To learn more about the new layout, visit Navigate the New Fire TV Experience Ambient Experience deactivates after:

  • You press the Home button .

  • You press and hold the Alexa Voice button and give a voice command like, “Go Home” or “Open Prime Video.”

  • 15 minutes of inactivity on Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation or after a few minutes of no user presence detected in room.

  • A routine deactivates it.

Adjust Start and Timeout for Ambient Experience

You can adjust when Ambient Experience starts and how long it stays active.

Note: The Ambient Experience timeout setting is only available on Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation).

If you haven’t set a duration, the Ambient Experience starts after 5 minutes of inactivity and times out after a few minutes of no motion detected in the room.

To adjust start and timeout from Ambient Experience screen:

  • Press the Menu button on your remote.

  • Select Ambient Preferences.

  • Select Advanced Settings.

  • Select:

    • Ambient Experience Start to adjust how long the device must be inactive before the Ambient Experience launches automatically.
    • Ambient Experience Timeout to adjust how long the device must be inactive before the Ambient Experience times out.

  • Select the new duration. To adjust start and timeout from Fire TV Home screen:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • Select Ambient Experience.

  • Select Ambient Preferences.

  • Select Advanced Settings.

  • Select:

    • Ambient Experience Start to adjust how long the device must be inactive before the Ambient Experience launches automatically.
    • Ambient Experience Timeout to adjust how long the device must be inactive before the Ambient Experience times out.

  • Select the new duration. Important: Ambient Experience may increase the energy consumption of your Fire TV device. You can turn off this feature at any time from the Settings menu. Go to Display & Sounds, and then Ambient Experience.

What Is the New Fire TV Search?

The new Fire TV search allows you to interact with Alexa using natural voice commands on some Fire TV devices.

Note: The new Fire TV search is available in English and isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

You can use the new Fire TV search feature by first pressing and holding down the Alexa Voice button on your voice remote. Then speak your command.

The new Fire TV search makes it easier to find shows and movies you’re interested in watching. Instead of navigating through menus or typing, you can use natural voice commands with Alexa to search. You can also describe a plot or share quotes from a movie or TV show, and Alexa finds similar entertainment options based on what you say.

Alexa offers personalized recommendations by learning from your preferences. The search results pull content from various entertainment apps.

Examples of commands:

  • “Show me movies about cold war spies.”
  • “Find cozy British mystery shows.”
  • “Show legal dramas.”
  • “What’s that show about a New York railroad tycoon?”
  • “What’s that alternate history space race show?”
  • “What are some thrillers with romance storylines?” Was this information helpful?

About Fire TV Recovery Mode

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

About Fire TV Recovery Mode

What to do if the Device Recovery Mode screen appears on your Fire TV.

Note: Device Recovery Mode isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

What is Device Recovery Mode?

Your Fire TV device enters device recovery mode when it encounters a critical error that it can’t resolve. An on-screen message appears on your Fire TV and provides options for you to recover your device:

  • To attempt recovery, select the option to restart your device.
  • If the issue persists after restarting, select the option to reset your device to factory settings.
  • Important: Factory resetting your device removes your account information and downloaded content.
Remote Troubleshooting

If your paired remote doesn’t work in device recovery mode, try a different Fire TV remote. To connect another remote:

  • Reset the remote:
    • Press and hold the Left , Menu , and Back buttons at the same time for 12 seconds.
    • Release the buttons. Your remote resets within 5 seconds.
  • Pair the remote to your Fire TV:
    • Bring the remote within 10 feet (3 m) of your Fire TV device.
    • Within 10 seconds, short-press the following buttons in the order listed:
      • Right
      • Back
      • Play/Pause
    • Tip: If you miss the 10 second window, or press the wrong buttons, wait a few seconds and then try again.
  • If you still can’t use your remote in recovery mode, or you don’t have another Fire TV remote:
    • Restart your Fire TV by unplugging it from power for three seconds.
    • Try these steps again after your Fire TV power on. To reconnect a remote to its original Fire TV device:
  • Restart your Fire TV by unplugging the device or through Settings .
  • When the home screen appears, press and hold the Home button for 10 seconds.
Use Your TV’s Physical Buttons to Navigate Recovery Mode

If your remote isn’t working, you can navigate recovery mode using the physical buttons on your Fire TV.

For Fire TV Smart TVs with volume buttons:

  • Short press the volume buttons to move through the recovery menu options.

  • Short press the power button to select or confirm the highlighted option. For Fire TV Smart TVs without volume buttons:

  • Short press the power button to move between the recovery menu options.

  • Long press the power button to select or confirm the highlighted option. For Fire TV Cubes:

  • Short press the volume buttons to move through the recovery menu options.

  • Short press the Action button to select or confirm the highlighted option. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Can’t Cast Apps to Fire TV

Follow these tips if you can’t cast a supported app to your Fire TV.

  • Connect your mobile device and Fire TV to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Note: To cast Prime Video content, sign in to the mobile app with the Amazon account that you use for your Fire TV.
  • Restart your Fire TV and your mobile device.
  • Restart your modem and router:
    • Unplug your modem and router and then wait 1 minute.
    • Plug in your modem first and wait for the lights to turn on and for it to connect to the internet (about 1 minute).
    • Plug in your router and wait for the lights to turn on and for it to connect to the internet (about 1 minute).
  • Clear the app’s cache on both your Fire TV and mobile device.
  • For help with clearing the app’s cache on your Fire TV, visit Clear App Data and Cache on Fire TV.
  • Update the software on your Fire TV and your mobile device.
  • To learn how to update the software on your Fire TV, follow the instructions in Update the Software on Your Fire TV.

Can’t Screen Mirror on Fire TV Devices

To resolve most issues with screen mirroring, make sure that your device and Fire TV are compatible.

  • The following devices don’t support screen mirroring:

    • iOS and macOS
    • Tip: If you have a Fire TV Smart TV, follow the steps in Use AirPlay on Your Fire TV Smart TV to mirror or cast content.
    • Android devices older than Android OS 4.2 (Jelly Bean)
    • Android devices that don’t support Miracast
    • Windows devices that don’t support Wireless Display (WiDi)

  • Check if your Fire TV can screen mirror.

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Enable Display Mirroring.
    • Note: If the option doesn’t appear, then screen mirroring isn’t compatible with your Fire TV.

  • Connect your Fire TV and the device that you want to mirror to the same Wi-Fi network.

  • Move your devices within 30 ft (10 m) of each other. For more help, go to:

  • Cast Apps to Fire TV

  • Screen Mirror Your Device to Fire TV For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Fire TV Keeps Restarting

If your Fire TV keeps turning on and off, check the power source and try updating the software.

Note: Use the power cable or adapter that came with your Fire TV device.

To stop your Fire TV from continuously rebooting, try the following steps:

  • Unplug the power cable from your device or wall outlet for several seconds, and then plug it back in.
  • If possible, connect the power cable to a different wall outlet.
  • If you can access your Fire TV settings, check for a software update:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select About.
    • Select Check for System Update.
  • Confirm that your TV is HDCP compliant.
  • Review the video-cable section of your TV’s user manual.
  • Try connecting your Fire TV device to a different HDMI port on your TV. If the issue persists, reset your Fire TV device to factory settings.

For more help, go to:

Fire TV Screen is Frozen

To resolve startup issues, restart your device or check the device connections.

Other common solutions:

  • For HDMI hubs, try plugging the Fire TV device directly into the TV instead.
  • Confirm that your TV is HDCP-compliant by reviewing the video-cable section of your TV owner’s manual.
  • If possible try using a different TV. If the issue persists, reset your Fire TV device to factory settings.

Fix a Blank TV Screen on Fire TV Devices

Use the following tips to help get your blank or unresponsive screen up and running.

Note: When you start or stop streaming in 4K Ultra HD, your TV screen may flicker or turn black for a few seconds.

  • Restart your Fire TV device.

  • Use the connection equipment that came with your device.

  • Confirm that any A/V receivers or sound bars connected to your Fire TV are on the correct input. You can also connect your Fire TV device directly to your TV.

  • Disconnect your Fire TV from the HDMI port then plug it back in.

  • Try replacing your HDMI cable or HDMI hub (not included) with a new one.

  • Use a High-Speed HDMI cable (not included) for streaming titles in 4K Ultra HD.

  • Match your remote’s source or input button to the HDMI port that your Fire TV is plugged into.

  • Turn HDMI-CEC Device Control off and then on again:

    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select HDMI-CEC Device Control to turn it off and then on again.

  • Cycle the available resolutions on your Fire TV device by pressing and holding the Up button and the Rewind button together for five seconds. Allow your device to cycle through all available resolutions. For more help, go to:

  • Restart Your Fire TV Device

  • Reset Your Fire TV Device to Factory Settings Was this information helpful?

A factory reset of your device removes all downloaded content including in-app purchases.

To factory reset your Fire TV device, follow these steps.

    • On the TV screen, choose to continue or cancel the factory reset.

Troubleshoot Fire TV Low Power Notification

Troubleshoot Fire TV Low Power Notification

If you see a notification about insufficient USB power on your Fire TV screen, follow these instructions.

Note: If you see the low power screen before your device turns on, connect the power cable to a power outlet.

When your Fire TV device detects insufficient power from your TV’s USB port, it displays an on-screen notification with the following options:

  • Got it - Continue your session.
    • The notification continues to appear each time you turn on your device.
  • Ask me Later – Snooze the notification. You can acknowledge or snooze the notification to continue using your device, but it will reappear until you resolve the power issue.

To resolve the low power issue, try the following:

  • Try a different USB port.

  • Use a 5W (5V, 1A or equivalent) power adapter and a longer USB power cable.

  • Plug the power cable into your TV’s USB 3.0 port (if available).

  • Use a power adapter.

  • Connect your Fire TV’s power cable to a power adapter and then plug the adapter into a power outlet. If you don’t have a power adapter or cable, below are our Amazon recommended power adapter and cable options:

  • Right Angle USB-C Power Cable (5ft / 1.5m) for Fire TV Stick HD For more help, contact Amazon Customer Service.

Unable to Update Your Fire TV Device

Your Fire TV update fails or your update doesn’t complete.

  • Check that your Fire TV device is connected to the Internet. Go to Settings , and then select Network . Press Play/Pause on your remote to test your connection.
  • If your device has connectivity issues, restart your home networks devices, such as your modem or router.
  • If you have a Fire TV media streaming device, unplug your Fire TV device. Wait one minute and then plug your device back in.
  • Confirm that your Fire TV device has enough available storage to download the update (at least 500 MB):
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select About.
    • Select Storage
  • Tip: To increase your available storage, uninstall apps from your Fire TV device. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Alexa Isn’t Responding on Your Fire TV Cube

Try these quick fixes to get Alexa to respond on Fire TV Cube.

Try these steps if the device doesn’t light up:

  • Make sure that your device hears you: take it out of any enclosed spaces.

  • Check if the device has power.

  • Press the Action button then say your request. Try these steps if the device lights up, but Alexa doesn’t respond:

  • Say, “I can’t hear you.” Alexa then routes responses to Fire TV Cube instead of a powered off TV or soundbar.

  • Turn up the volume on Fire TV Cube with the + button.

  • Check what Alexa heard by reviewing the voice history in the Alexa app: if necessary, repeat using slightly different words. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.
