Control Your Set-Top Box on Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)

After you set up equipment control, you can use Alexa voice commands to do things like switch in puts or go to specific channels.

The set-top box and Fire TV Cube need to be within line of sight of each other and should be connected with a high-speed HDMI cable rated at 18 Gbps or higher.

For a list of supported set-top box providers, go to Supported Set-Top Box Providers on Fire TV Cube. If you’re connecting your set-top box directly to your Fire TV Cube, go to Use Your Fire TV Cube to Control a Set-Top Box Connected to Your TV.

To set up equipment control for devices connected to your Fire TV Cube’s HDMI IN input:

  • Go to Inputs from your Fire TV menu.
  • Highlight the HDMI tile.
  • Press the Menu button on your Fire TV remote and select Change Device Name.
  • Select Cable or Satellite, depending on your setup.
  • Choose your TV provider, or select Provider not listed.
  • Your Fire TV Cube will test the connection with your set-top box.
  • To complete setup, follow the on-screen instructions. Note: If you experience issues completing setup, please make sure that your Fire TV Cube is in the line of sight of your TV and your set-top box. You may need to turn off HDMI control on your set-top box. Please refer to your set-top box user manuals or call your provider to learn how to turn off HDMI control from your set-top box settings.

IR Extension Cables with Fire TV Cube

Use a supported IR extension cable to control equipment that’s inside a closed cabinet or out of sight of your Fire TV Cube.

Your Fire TV Cube uses an internal IR blaster to control entertainment, such as set-top boxes or AV receivers. Your Fire TV Cube can control your equipment as long as the devices aren’t out of sight.

If the equipment that you want to control is in a cabinet or otherwise obstructed, consider using an IR extension cable. IR extension cables let you emit IR signals to locations your Fire TV Cube can’t reach.

Your Fire TV Cube supports most IR extension cables, as long as the cable:

  • Is an IR transmitter
  • Connects using a 3.5mm jack An IR blaster style cable is recommended for the best experience.

To use an IR extension cable, plug the cable into the IR port on the back of your Fire TV Cube. Then, place the IR emitter on the same shelf as the devices you want to control. If you have devices on multiple shelves, place the IR emitter on the lowest shelf.

Note: After placing the IR emitter, set your Fire TV Cube to use its internal blaster:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment.
  • Select Advanced Settings.
  • Select Volume & Power Buttons.
  • Select Fire TV Cube.

Learn about Fire TV Cube

Fire TV Cube combines Alexa and infrared technology for hands-free control of your entertainment system.

Fire TV Cube devices have:

Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation) also features dedicated USB and HDMI IN ports.

Find information about devices compatible with Fire TV Cube on the product detail page.

Learn to Use Alexa on Your Fire TV Cube

Perform specific actions, watch and listen to content, and control devices with Alexa. Use your wake word or press and hold the Voice button on your remote to talk to Alexa.

To control certain functions of devices connected to your Fire TV Cube (like an A/V receiver or sound bar) with Alexa, first set them up in the Fire TV device settings.

Note: The voice button on the Fire TV remote doesn’t support voice navigation commands or making onscreen selections with your voice.

You can adjust the volume on your Fire TV Cube with the volume buttons on top of the device, or say, “Volume [1-10].”

Manage Alexa Features

Use the Alexa app on your compatible mobile device to set and manage settings for most Alexa features. To deactivate the microphones on your Fire TV Cube, press the Mute button on top of the device and it lights up red.

These Alexa features aren’t available on Fire TV Cube at this time:

  • Video Drop In
  • Drop In from devices not registered to your account
  • Support for Bluetooth connections with external sources (like your mobile phone)
  • Voice support for Bluetooth connections
  • Third-party smart home devices without a hub Note: While Announcements and Messaging can use the Fire TV Cube internal speaker, Calling and Drop In use the connected external speaker (like the TV or sound bar).

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Reset Your Fire TV Cube

If your Fire TV Cube is unresponsive, or you want to erase your device settings, press and hold the Volume Down and Mute buttons until the light flashes blue (about 40 seconds).

Tip: Having trouble with your Fire TV? Restart your device first to try to resolve the problem. Just unplug the power adapter and then plug it back in.

Your account information and downloaded content are deleted during a factory reset. To reset your device using Settings, follow these steps:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
  • Select My Fire TV.
  • Select Reset to Factory Defaults.

Super Resolution on Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)

Super Resolution makes lower resolution (lower than 4K) videos sharper and clearer on 4K resolution or higher televisions.

Super Resolution on Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation) makes lower resolution videos look better on higher resolution televisions. Unlike traditional linear upscaling, Super Resolution enhances the details of the image to make it sharper. Super Resolution upscales all video content, such as streaming apps or video from devices connected to the HDMI-In port.

Note: If you’re viewing 4K resolution (or higher) content there won’t be a difference in quality.

Super Resolution is activated by default. To change your Super Resolution settings:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
  • Choose Display & Sounds.
  • Select Display.
  • Choose Super Resolution.
  • Switch between ON and OFF. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Unfreeze Your TV Screen on Fire TV Cube

Find a fix for your blank or frozen TV Screen with Fire TV Cube.

If the issue persists, check your equipment and connections:

  • Restart your Fire TV Cube.
  • Use the power adapter and connection equipment that came with your device.
  • Verify that your TV is on and set to the correct HDMI input channel.
  • Make sure that connected devices (A/V receiver or soundbar) are turned on.
  • Confirm that your TV is HDCP-compliant. Review the video-cable section of the TV owner’s manual.
  • Be sure that the HDMI cable is fully connected to both your TV and Fire TV Cube.
  • Use a High-Speed HDMI cable.
  • Try replacing your HDMI cable or HDMI hub with a new one.
  • Check your TV for firmware updates. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

  • Fire TV Stick (1st Generation) Fire TV Profiles personalize certain features on the home screen for each profile on your device. For example:

  • Viewing history

  • Watch progress

  • Amazon Music app You can also customize the apps and channels on the main menu and some device settings, like language and accessibility.

You share app subscriptions, rentals, and content purchased on your Amazon account with the other profiles on your device. You can have a total of six profiles on your Fire TV. Up to four can be Amazon Kids profiles.

To learn more about kid profiles, go to What is Amazon Kids on Fire TV Devices?.

On the Amazon Music app, you can listen to personalized music based on the selected Fire TV profile.

Fire TV Recast Help

Fire TV Recast Not Recording

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

More Fire TV Devices ›

Fire TV Recast Help ›

Fire TV Recast Not Recording

Recording issues can happen when there are internet connectivity issues, recording conflicts, or issues with your antenna connection.

Recordings can fail for a number of reasons:

  • Loss of connectivity between Fire TV Recast and your home network.
    • Visit Update the Wi-Fi Settings for Your Fire TV Recast for more information.
  • Loss of power due to a power outage or an unplugged power cable.
  • Issues with antenna connection.
    • Connect your antenna securely to your Fire TV Recast.
  • Transmitter interference affecting channel reception or quality in your area.
  • Tuner is already in use for live playback.
    • For more information, visit How Many Programs Can I Watch or Record at Once?.
  • Recording conflicts. If you have several recordings scheduled at the same time, the lowest priority show doesn’t get recorded. To manage your recording priority settings:
    • Go to the My Stuff or DVR from the Fire TV menu.
    • Select DVR Manager.
    • Select Recording Priority. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Fire TV Recast Not Showing on Fire TV

Fire TV Recast Help ›

Fire TV Recast Not Showing on Fire TV

Fire TV is missing Fire TV Recast content in the channel guide, settings, or DVR.

Try these tips:

  • Restart your Fire TV and your Fire TV Recast.
  • Register your Fire TV and Fire TV Recast & Blaster app to the same Amazon account. To register your Fire TV to a different account:
    • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
    • Select Account & Profile Settings .
    • Select Amazon Account.
    • Select Deregister.
  • Note: You can only have one Fire TV Recast registered to your Amazon account.
  • Connect your Amazon devices to the same network. Don’t connect your Fire TV Recast to a guest network. For help with connecting Fire TV Recast to Wi-Fi, visit Update the Wi-Fi Settings for Your Fire TV Recast.
  • Update the software for your Fire TV. For more information, visit Update the Software on Your Fire TV.
  • Try unpairing and then pairing your Fire TV Recast and Fire TV device again. For help with pairing your devices, visit Pair Your Viewing Device with Fire TV Recast.
  • Verify that the devices have an active network connection. The light on the Fire TV Recast is orange when it has no network connection. When Fire TV Recast is online, the light is a solid white or green. Use the Fire TV Recast & Blaster app to check your connection:
    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV Recast & Blaster app.
    • Select Fire TV Recast.
    • Select your device.
    • Select Network. If the network status shows as offline, restart your devices.
  • Restart your routers and other hardware.
  • If your Wi-Fi signal is weak, move your Fire TV Recast closer to your router, or switch to an Ethernet connection. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

How Many Programs Can I Watch or Record at Once?

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

More Fire TV Devices ›

Fire TV Recast Help ›

How Many Programs Can I Watch or Record at Once?

The number of programs you can record or watch at once depends on which Fire TV Recast model you have.

Fire TV Recast has two models: 500 GB with 2 tuners, and 1000 GB with 4 tuners. If you’re watching Fire TV Recast content or recording a channel, each of these actions uses a tuner.

With a 2-tuner Fire TV Recast, you can:

  • Record up to 2 programs at once.

  • Watch up to 1 live and 1 recorded program on different devices, while recording another.

  • Watch up to 2 recorded programs on different devices, while recording 2 programs in the background.

  • Watch up to 2 live programs on different devices at once. With a 4-tuner Fire TV Recast, you can:

  • Record up to 4 programs at once.

  • Watch up to 1 live and 1 recorded program on different devices, while recording up to 3 other programs in the background.

  • Watch up to 2 recorded programs on different devices, while recording up to 4 programs in the background.

  • Watch up to 2 live programs on different devices while recording up to 2 other programs in the background. Note: No matter how many tuners you have, you can’t watch Fire TV Recast content on more than two devices at once.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

How to Expand Your Fire TV Recast Storage

Connect a compatible external hard drive to your Fire TV Recast to expand your available storage.

Note: Fire TV Recast doesn’t support using external storage to transfer or back up recordings. When using an external hard drive, you can’t choose whether your recording gets stored in the external hard drive or internal storage.

Fire TV Recast is compatible with the following external hard drives:

  • Seagate Fast SSD 250 GB

  • Toshiba Canvio for Desktop 3 TB

  • WD 2 TB Elements Portable External Hard Drive - USB 3.0 To expand your Fire TV Recast storage:

  • Plug your compatible external hard drive into the USB port on the back of your Fire TV Recast. Your device should detect your hard drive automatically.

  • When prompted, choose whether you’d like to format the hard drive. Formatting erases any existing files on the hard drive. If the prompt doesn’t appear, you can add your hard drive manually:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Live TV , and then Sync Sources.

  • Select Fire TV Recast, and then Add External Storage. Tip: Fire TV Recast reboots whenever you unplug your external storage. Try not to unplug your external storage when a recording is in process.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

How to Record Live TV with Fire TV Recast

How to Record Live TV with Fire TV Recast

Use your Fire TV Recast to record Live TV and watch it later.

Note: You can only record over-the-air live TV channels available through the antenna that’s connected to your Fire TV Recast.

You can schedule a recording up to 14 days before an episode airs. Fire TV Recast automatically schedules recordings of series episodes as they become available.

To record live TV on your Fire TV device:

  • Choose the show that you want to record from the channel guide or from the On Now row on the Home screen.
  • Press the Menu button on your remote. To record in the Fire TV app , select the three dots next to your chosen program.
  • Note: The Fire TV app doesn’t support scheduling future recordings.
  • Select Record. You can choose to record either a single episode or the entire series. When recording a single episode, Fire TV Recast starts recording from the point at which you tuned in. The number of programs you can record or watch at once depends on which Fire TV Recast model you have. For more information, visit How Many Programs Can I Watch or Record at Once?

You can manage the default recording options in your Fire TV settings:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
  • Go to Live TV .
  • Select Sync Sources, and then select Fire TV Recast.
  • Go to Default Recording Options. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Manage Your Fire TV Recast Recordings

To watch, delete, or protect your recordings, go to the DVR or My Stuff tab on your Fire TV.

To manage your Fire TV Recast recordings on Fire TV:

  • Go to the DVR or My Stuff tab on your Fire TV.
  • Go to the My Recordings row to find your recordings. Fire TV Recast automatically deletes programs when its storage space is about 95% full. You can prevent programs from being automatically deleted by protecting the program.

To protect or delete a recording, go to Recording Options:

  • Highlight the recording on the My Recordings row.
  • Press the Menu button on your Fire TV remote.
  • Select Recording Options. Note: Deleting a recording is permanent. You can’t recover deleted recordings.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Scan for TV Channels for Fire TV Recast

In the Fire TV Recast & Blaster app, select Settings. Select, Fire TV Recast, and then Channel Management. Then, choose Channel Scan.

Note: Your location, your antenna connection, and its placement determine which stations you get with Fire TV Recast.

To scan for channels on a Fire TV device:

Set Up Fire TV Recast

To complete setup, connect a digital antenna to your Fire TV Recast and follow the instructions in the Fire TV Recast & Blaster app.

To use Fire TV Recast, you need:

  • A digital HDTV antenna.
  • A compatible Fire TV device.
  • Note: Fire TV Recast is not compatible with Fire TV Stick 4K Select.
  • Access to the Fire TV Recast & Blaster app on a mobile device. Make sure that each device is on the same network and registered to the same Amazon account. You can register one Fire TV Recast per Amazon account.

To set up your Fire TV Recast:

  • Connect a digital antenna to your Fire TV Recast. For best performance, place your antenna as high up in your home as possible. Try placing it against a window or outward facing wall that’s away from nearby towers or buildings.
  • Plug your Fire TV Recast and power adapter into a power outlet.
  • Note: Your Fire TV Recast and antenna don’t connect directly to your TV, so you can place it anywhere in your home. Keep your Fire TV Recast indoors in a cool, dry place with proper ventilation.
  • Open the Fire TV Recast & Blaster app and sign in to your Amazon account.
  • Select Set Up New Device, then Set Up a Fire TV Recast.
  • Follow the app instructions to connect to the Internet and complete device registration.
  • Find your available channels and channel guide in the Live tab or DVR tab at the top of your Fire TV home screen. Note:

Amazon collects information relating to your use of over-the-air TV content which may include the name of the channel watched, the name of the program watched, and the duration.

This helps us improve our services and personalize your experience. We will handle this information in accordance with the Amazon Privacy Notice available at www.amazon.com/privacy.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Use Alexa to Control Fire TV Recast

Use Alexa voice commands to record, access, and manage Fire TV Recast content on compatible devices.

You can ask Alexa to control your Fire TV Recast in a number of ways:

“Record [title]. “

Note: Asking Alexa to record a TV show will record the entire series.

“Delete [title].”

“Cancel my recording of [title].”

“Show me the channel guide.”

“Tune to [channel name].”

“How full is my DVR?”

“Show my recordings.”

“Rewind [timeframe].”

“Fast forward [timeframe].”

“Pause.”

“Play.”

Tip: You can also use Alexa devices linked with your Fire TV for requests that don’t require video playback. To learn more, go to Link Your Fire TV and Alexa Device.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Weak or No Signal with Fire TV Recast

Channel scan isn’t picking up channels or there are weak signal error messages with Fire TV Recast.

Common solutions:

  • Reposition or reinstall your digital antenna to improve reception (not on concrete).
  • Connect the antenna directly to Fire TV Recast, not your TV.
  • Restart the Fire TV Recast.
  • Restart the paired viewing devices.
  • Check available stations for your area with the FCC’s DTV Reception Maps (https://www.fcc.gov/media/engineering/dtvmaps). For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Find Your Alexa Voice Remote Pro

Can’t find your Alexa Voice Remote Pro? Ask Alexa to help locate the missing remote, or use the Fire TV mobile app.

To be able to use the remote finder feature:

  • Pair Alexa Voice Remote Pro with a compatible Fire TV or Echo Show device.
  • Make sure to register your Alexa device and Fire TV or Echo Show to the same account.
  • Make sure to keep your Alexa Voice Remote Pro within 30 ft (10 m) of the paired Fire TV or Echo Show.
  • Turn on your paired Fire TV or Echo Show.
    • Fire TV Smart TVs: Activate the setting Voice Commands When TV Screen is Off to use the feature while the TV screen is off.
    • Fire TV Sticks: Make sure to connect the power cable to a dedicated power source. Use a compatible USB power adapter and cable (5V, 1A, or equivalent).
    • Echo Show: Make sure to connect the power cable to an outlet using the provided power adapter. To use the remote finder feature:
  • Connect your Fire TV app to the same Fire TV or Echo Show as your Alexa Voice Remote Pro.
  • Say “Find my remote” to any Amazon device with Alexa, the Alexa app, or the Fire TV app.
    • You can also press the Remote Finder icon in the Fire TV app’s Remote tab.
    • Note: The Remote Finder icon isn’t available if using an Echo Show device with your Alexa Voice Remote Pro. Alexa Voice Remote Pro rings for up to five minutes, or until you press one of its buttons. It can take up to 30 seconds for the ringing to start.

Fire TV Remote Batteries Are Draining Fast

Try these troubleshooting steps if the batteries in your Fire TV remote are draining too quickly.

  • Make sure that you’re using alkaline AAA batteries for best performance and optimal battery life.
  • Remove the batteries from your remote and wait 30 seconds.
  • Put the batteries back in your remote.
  • Press and hold the Home button. Note: If the issue persists, replace the batteries in your remote with new alkaline AAA batteries.

Learn About Fire TV App

Use your Fire TV app to search and manage your favorite shows, movies, and more.

You can use your Fire TV app to browse, discover, and manage content directly from your mobile device.

To search and manage content from your Fire TV app, open the Fire TV app on your mobile phone and then sign-in using your Amazon account.

Note: The Fire TV app is compatible with the following operating systems and devices:

Feature

Description

Remote

Remote control functionality. When paired with your Fire TV, use the directional pad to navigate and select content on your Fire TV.

Search

Browse Fire TV content, view content details, and open selected content on your connected Fire TV device.

Select content to view detailed information about shows and movies, including options to add to your watchlist, like or dislike content, or open the content on your Fire TV.

Profiles

Select and manage profiles to personalize your Fire TV experience.

My Stuff

Add content to the watchlist from detail pages, view and manage content from your watchlist. Sync your watchlist across all your Fire TV devices within your profile.

Pair Another Fire TV Remote

Learn how to pair an additional remote or set up a replacement remote for your Fire TV device.

Note:

  • Not all remotes are compatible with every Fire TV device. To check remote compatibility, go to Amazon Fire TV and Alexa Devices Compatible with Fire TV Remotes.

  • You can use the Fire TV app to pair remotes to your Fire TV device. To learn more, go to Use the Fire TV App to Pair Your Remote.

  • To pair remotes with Echo Show devices, go to Pair a Fire TV Remote with Your Compatible Echo Show. To pair your new remote with your original remote:

  • Using your current remote, go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.

  • Select Controllers & Bluetooth Devices.

  • Select Amazon Fire TV Remotes.

  • Select Add New Remote.

  • Insert batteries in your new remote. Your remote should appear in the list.

  • Note: If the remote doesn’t appear, press and hold the Home button for 10 seconds. To pair your new remote without your original remote:

  • Restart your Fire TV device by unplugging it from power.

  • Plug in your Fire TV and wait for the on-screen remote detection error message.

  • Insert the included batteries into your new remote.

  • Your remote should pair with your Fire TV device. Note: If your remote doesn’t pair, press and hold the Home button for 10 seconds.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Pair Your Fire TV Remote

Pair Your Fire TV Remote

Try these troubleshooting steps if you can’t connect to your Fire TV Remote during initial set up.

Your remote pairs automatically when you insert the batteries and turn on your TV. You see a confirmation message in the lower-right corner of your screen when successful. If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, or a “Pairing failed” message appears:

  • Make sure that your remote is within 10 feet (3 m) of your Fire TV device.
  • Press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • Remove the batteries from your remote and wait 30 seconds. Put the batteries back in and then press and hold the Home button again.
  • Try using a new pair of alkaline batteries. Once the new batteries are in your remote, press and hold the Home button again.
  • Reset your Fire TV remote:
    • Press and hold the Left button , Menu button , and Back button at the same time.
    • Hold them for 12 seconds.
    • Press and hold the Home button again.
  • If the issue persists, unplug your Fire TV device, wait five seconds, and then plug it back in. Note: If you have seven controllers paired, remove one before attempting to pair another.

Alternatively, use the Fire TV app to pair your remote. Download the Fire TV app on your mobile device and follow the steps in Use the Fire TV App to Pair Your Remote.

For more help, go to:

Remote Finder Not Working on Alexa Voice Remote Pro

If your Alexa Voice Remote Pro isn’t ringing or Alexa doesn’t understand your voice command, try these troubleshooting steps.

If the remote finder feature isn’t working with your Alexa Voice Remote Pro, try these steps:

  • Restart your Fire TV or Echo Show by unplugging it from the power source for one minute before plugging it back in.

  • Make sure to connect your Fire TV Stick’s power cable to a dedicated power source.

  • Use a compatible USB power adapter and cable (5V, 1A, or equivalent).

  • Make sure the batteries in the remote are good.

    • For best performance, use alkaline batteries.
    • If one of the batteries is bad, replace both batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

  • Make sure you’re using the correct voice command: “Find my remote.”

  • If you’re using the Fire TV app to find your remote, connect the app to the same device as your remote.

  • Note: For Echo Shows, the Fire TV app only supports the “Find my remote” voice command.

  • If you have multiple Alexa Voice Remote Pro remotes, use the correct name for the remote you’re trying to find.

  • You can access and manage the Alexa Voice Remote Pro names in the Alexa app. The names appear under All Devices.

  • Unpair and then pair your Alexa Voice Remote Pro with your Fire TV or Echo Show device. For more help, go to:

  • Find Your Alexa Voice Remote Pro

Replace the Batteries in Your Fire TV Remote

Open the back cover of the remote to insert or replace batteries.

Note: Some models have a latch instead.

For models without a latch:

  • Turn over the remote and put one thumb on the arrow at the bottom of the battery cover.

  • Put your other thumb at the top of the remote above the battery cover.

  • Hold the top of the remote tightly. Push down the battery cover by applying pressure with the thumb that’s on the bottom of the battery cover.

  • Slide the door down halfway and roll off the cover from the remote battery casing.

  • Insert new AAA alkaline batteries and slide the cover up until you hear a click to close the cover. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page. For models with a latch:

  • Press directly on the arrow icon to release the latch; and the battery compartment opens.

  • Turn over the remote and put one thumb on the arrow indicator at the top of the battery cover.

  • Hold the remote firmly. Push down the battery cover by applying pressure with the thumb on the arrow indicator that’s on top of the battery cover.

  • Slide the door down halfway and roll off the cover from the remote battery casing.

  • Insert new AAA alkaline batteries and slide the cover up until you hear a click to close the cover. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Reset Your Fire TV Remote

Reset Your Fire TV Remote

If your remote isn’t working, try resetting it.

To reset most Fire TV remotes:
  • Unplug your Fire TV from the power supply and HDMI input, then wait 60 seconds.
  • Press and hold the Left button , Menu button , and Back button at the same time. Hold them for 12 seconds.
  • Release the buttons and wait five seconds.
  • Remove the batteries from your remote.
  • Plug in your Fire TV and wait for the on-screen remote detection error message.
  • Put the batteries back in your remote.
  • Press the Home button . The LED indicator blinks blue when your remote pairs successfully. If it’s not paired, press the Home button for 10 seconds.

Note: Not all remotes have an LED indicator light.

To reset the Basic Edition Remote:
  • Press and hold the Home button . At the same time, press the Menu button three times.
  • Release the Home button .
  • Press the Menu button nine times.
  • Remove the batteries from your remote.
  • Unplug your Fire TV from the power supply and HDMI input, then wait 60 seconds.
  • Put the batteries back in your remote, and then plug in your Fire TV.
  • Once the Home screen appears, press and hold the Home button for 40 seconds.
  • Wait 60 seconds for setup to complete.
To reset the Alexa Voice Remote (1st Generation):
  • Unplug your Fire TV from the power supply and HDMI input, then wait 60 seconds.
  • Press and hold the Left button and Menu button at the same time. Hold them for 12 seconds.
  • Release the buttons and wait five seconds.
  • Remove the batteries from your remote.
  • Plug in your Fire TV and wait for the on-screen remote detection error message.
  • Put the batteries back in your remote.
  • Press the Home button on the remote. Your remote should be paired now. If your remote hasn’t paired, press the Home button for 10 seconds.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Troubleshoot the Alexa Voice Remote Pro Customizable Buttons

Troubleshoot the Alexa Voice Remote Pro Customizable Buttons

Having trouble assigning shortcuts or using the customizable buttons on your Alexa Voice Remote Pro? Follow these troubleshooting steps to help resolve some common issues.

Can’t Program Either Button

If the on-screen panel to select shortcuts doesn’t appear on your Fire TV or Echo Show:

  • Make sure that your device isn’t in a child profile.
  • Try pressing and holding the customizable button for up to 10 seconds.
  • Make sure that the Alexa Voice Remote Pro is paired with the correct device.
  • Restart your device, and then try assigning the shortcut again.
    • To restart your Fire TV, unplug it from the power source for one minute before plugging it back in.
    • To restart your Echo Show, unplug the power adapter from the device or the outlet and then plug it back in.
  • Try setting up the shortcut in the remote options in the Fire TV Settings.
  • Note: For Echo Show devices, you can find Fire TV Settings in your Echo Show Settings.
Shortcut Button Not Working

If a shortcut isn’t working when you press an assigned button:

  • Reassign the shortcut. Press and hold the button for five seconds, then choose an option from the on-screen panel.
  • If the shortcut is an Alexa command that’s not working, try giving the command directly to your device. If the direct command works, reassign the button with the newly given command.
Can’t Program Specific Shortcuts

If you can’t program a specific shortcut (such as an app, voice command, a specific screen):

  • Check the on-screen panel for what recent voice command is displayed. If only “popular” commands are displayed, confirm that the correct voice command was initiated on your device.
  • Confirm that the app is installed on your device. Only installed apps can be assigned to a button.
    • If the app is installed, make sure it launches successfully and opens on your device.
  • Make sure that the shortcut to navigate to a specific screen on the device is supported on all devices. For example, a shortcut to navigate to an Input switching screen is only supported on certain Fire TV devices.
  • Restart your device, and then try assigning the shortcut again.
    • To restart your Fire TV, unplug it from the power source for one minute before plugging it back in.
    • To restart your Echo Show, unplug the power adapter from the device or the outlet and then plug it back in. For more help, go to:
  • Use the Customizable Buttons on Alexa Voice Remote Pro Was this information helpful?

Troubleshoot Your Fire TV Remote

If your Fire TV remote isn’t working or isn’t responding with your Fire TV device, try these troubleshooting steps.

You can use the troubleshooting mode on compatible remotes to help identify what’s causing the issue. When in troubleshooting mode, the LED on your remote changes color based on the problem.

Note: Not all remotes have an LED light. To check if your remote support troubleshooting mode, press the Alexa Voice button on your remote. If the LED at the top of the remote flashes, troubleshooting mode is available.

If your remote responds or supports troubleshooting mode:

  • Press the Rewind and Right buttons at the same time for three seconds to activate the troubleshooting mode.
  • Press the Menu button . The LED turns green to show that your remote is now in troubleshooting mode.
  • Press any button on your remote. The LED flashes with a specific color to help you identify the issue.
    • Red (slow blinking) – Low battery. Replace the batteries in your remote. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.
    • Red (fast blinking) – There’s a problem with your remote. Try to reset your Fire TV remote.
    • Orange – The remote isn’t paired with your Fire TV. Restart your Fire TV device and wait until “Cannot detect your remote” appears on-screen. Then, pair your Fire TV remote again by pressing and holding the Home button on the remote for 10 seconds. If you still can’t pair your remote, go to Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote help page.
    • White - Make sure that the Fire TV device is on. If the problem persists, restart your Fire TV device.
    • Blue – No issue with the remote. Try to restart your Fire TV device.
  • To deactivate the troubleshooting mode:
    • Press the Play/Pause and Up buttons at the same time for three seconds.
    • Then, press the Menu button to turn off troubleshooting mode.
    • Next, remove the batteries and place them back into the remote. For more help, go to:
  • Volume, Power, or Mute Buttons Not Working on Fire TV Remote
  • Reset Your Fire TV Remote
  • Replace the Batteries in Your Fire TV Remote

Use the Customizable Buttons on Your Alexa Voice Remote Pro

The customizable buttons on your remote are shortcuts to do things like quickly access a favorite app, give an Alexa voice command, and more.

To be able to use the customizable buttons:

  • Alexa Voice Remote Pro must be paired with a compatible device.
  • Alexa Voice Remote Pro must be within 30 ft (10 m) of the paired device.
  • The paired device must be on.
    • Fire TV Smart TVs: Activate the setting Voice Commands when TV Screen is Off to use the feature while the TV screen is off.
    • Fire TV Sticks: Make sure that the power cable is connected to an outlet with the provided power adapter, and not to a USB port on the TV. This lets the customizable buttons work while the TV is off.
    • Echo Shows: Make sure that the power cable is connected to the device and the power adapter is connected to an outlet. Note: The customizable buttons shortcuts aren’t available in Child profiles.

To set up the customizable button shortcuts on Alexa Voice Remote Pro:

Note: For Echo Show devices, you can find Fire TV Settings in your Echo Show Settings.

  • Press and hold the desired customizable button (labeled 1 and 2) for five seconds. You can also go to your remote in the Fire TV Settings and select the desired button.
  • A personalized side panel appears on-screen. The panel shows suggested actions based on your recent activity, and shortcuts for your last three voice commands.
  • Select a suggested app, Alexa voice command, or More Actions in the side panel. For More Actions, select the category and choose a shortcut from the on-screen list. An on-screen notification confirms that the new shortcut has been created.

To change the assigned shortcut, repeat these steps with the button that you want to update.

Volume or Power Controls Not Working in Fire TV App

Try these steps if the volume or power controls in your Fire TV app aren’t working.

Note:

  • Not all TVs support the CEC protocol required to use this feature.

  • This feature isn’t available for all Fire TV devices. If your Fire TV supports this feature, your Fire TV app displays the option to set up volume and power controls. If you can’t use the volume or power controls in your Fire TV app, try the following:

  • Turn on HDMI CEC in your TV’s settings.

  • To learn how to manage HDMI CEC settings on common TV brands, visit

  • Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV

  • Check if you can change the TV’s volume or power with your Fire TV remote. If you can’t, follow the instructions in Volume, Power, or Mute Buttons Not Working on Fire TV Remote.

  • If you use an external speaker, check if you can change the speaker’s volume or power with your Fire TV remote. If you can’t, set up equipment control for your speaker under Settings > Equipment Control on your Fire TV. If the problem continues after turning on CEC, your TV may not support the required CEC protocol.

What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)?

What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)?

Learn about the button layout on the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release).

Text Description of the Button Layout

Hold the remote with the large circular button towards your TV and the smooth end towards yourself.

Starting at the top left and moving to the right is the Power button and a small hole for the microphone.

Below the microphone is the Alexa Voice button, which you can press to make Alexa voice commands. Below the Alexa Voice button is the Navigation Ring. Navigate your Fire TV by pressing up, down, left, or right on the ring. In the center of the ring is the Select button.

Next is a row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Back, Home, and Menu. Home has a raised dot.

Next is another row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Rewind, Play/Pause, and Fast Forward.

Next is another row of three buttons, where the center button is a vertical bar. From left to right, they are: Mute, Volume Up and Down, and the Guide button.

Finally, there are two rows with two App buttons each. Each button launches a preset app on your Fire TV. The preset apps may vary.

For more help, go to:

  • Accessibility Features for Fire TV Was this information helpful?

Next is a row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Back, Home, and Menu. Home has a raised dot.

Next is another row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Rewind, Play/Pause, and Fast Forward.

Next is another row of three buttons, where the center button is a vertical bar. From left to right, they are: Mute, Volume Up and Down, and the Guide button.

Finally, there are two rows with two App buttons each. Each button launches a preset app on your Fire TV. The preset apps may vary.

For more help, go to:

  • Accessibility Features for Fire TV Was this information helpful?

What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced?

Learn about the button layout on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced.

Text Description of the Button Layout

Hold the remote with the large circular button towards your TV and the smooth end towards yourself.

Starting at the top left and moving to the right is the Power, a small hole for the microphone, and then the LED indicator.

Below the microphone is the Alexa Voice button, which you can press to make Alexa voice commands. Below the Alexa Voice button is the Navigation Ring. Navigate your Fire TV by pressing up, down, left, or right on the ring. In the center of the ring is the Select button.

Next is a row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Back, Home, and Menu. Home has a raised dot.

Next is another row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Rewind, Play/Pause, and Fast Forward.

Next is a set of vertical bar buttons on the left side and right side with one button between them. The left bar is Volume Up and Down and the right bar is Channel Up and Down. The button in between is the Guide button.

Next is a row of three buttons. From left to right, they are: Mute, Settings, and Recents.

Finally, there are two rows with two App buttons each. Each button launches a preset app on your Fire TV. The preset apps may vary.

Attach the Support Base to Your Fire TV Smart TV

Safely attach the base to your Fire TV Smart TV.

This information applies to:

  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series
  • Fire TV Omni Series
  • Fire TV 4-Series

  • Fire TV 2-Series
  • Amazon Ember 2-Series and Fire TV 2-Series (2025 Release) Warning: Never place your Fire TV Smart TV in an unstable location. The TV may slide or fall causing serious injury or damage. Assembly takes two people.

To attach the base to your Fire TV Smart TV:

  • Remove the accessories from the box.
  • Leave the plastic bag on the TV.
  • Lift the TV from either side, without touching the screen.
  • Place your Fire TV Smart TV face down on a large, flat surface.
  • Cut the plastic bag along the bottom.
  • Attach the double-legged support base to the TV using the included screws. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Dolby Vision or High Dynamic Range Not Working on Fire TV Smart TV

Check your cable connections and verify which video formats the content supports.

  • Check if the content supports Dolby Vision, 4K, or HDR.
  • If the content comes from a connected device:
    • Connect the device with an HDMI cable.
    • Restart the connected device.
    • Set the source device to output Dolby Vision, 4K, or HDR.
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds, and then select Picture Settings.
    • Select the HDMI input that your device connects to, and then select HDMI Input Mode.
    • Change the input mode to Auto or Mode 2 (2.0).
  • Try to restart your Fire TV Smart TV:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select Restart.
  • Make sure that the app is up to date:
    • Go to the Appstore and then search for the app.
    • An option to update shows if there’s an available update for the app.
  • Reset your Fire TV Smart TV:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select Reset to Factory Defaults.

Fire TV Smart TV Audio Settings

You can manage your sound settings directly from the Display & Sounds menu.

To access your Fire TV Smart TV sound and audio output settings, go to Settings and then Display & Sounds.

Sound Settings

The following table lists the sound settings and their descriptions:

Option

Description

Sound Mode

Select from a range of sound modes such as Standard, Movie, Music and more.

Reset

Reset your sound settings to the default factory settings.

Bass, Treble, Balance

Adjust the bass, treble, and balance of your TV speakers.

Advanced Settings

Adjust the settings for Dialog Clarity, TruVolume, and DTS Virtual:X.

Audio Output Options

The following table lists the audio output options and their descriptions:

Option

Description

TV Speakers

Turn on or off the built-in TV speakers.

Audio output jack

Select how to control the volume when using the 3.5mm audio output on the back of the TV.

You can choose from the following options:

  • Fixed: Select to control the volume using only your connected device.
  • Variable: Select to control the volume using both your connected device and your Fire TV remote. Digital Audio Format

Select an audio format for the HDMI ARC and optical output:

  • PCM: Passes uncompressed audio to the HDMI ARC or optical output.
  • Dolby Digital: Passes Dolby Digital Audio to the HDMI ARC or optical output.
  • Passthrough: Passes through the signal from the audio or source without changing the audio format type. Your TV defaults to supporting 5.1 channel digital output. Select Passthrough to support a max of 7.1 channels.
  • Auto: Automatically selects the best audio format for the HDMI ARC and optical output based on the connected device or output. AC4 Dialog Enhancer

Increase the quality and clarity of the dialogue.

Bluetooth Audio Sync

Sync the video and audio on your Bluetooth audio device.

Fire TV Smart TV Has Video but No Audio

To resolve audio issues, check your audio output settings and restart your Fire TV.

To troubleshoot issues with your audio, follow these steps:

  • Make sure that your TV isn’t muted. Press the Volume Up button on your Fire TV remote to increase the volume.
  • If you use your TV speakers for sound, turn on your TV speakers:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Audio Output.
    • Check that the TV Speakers option shows as On.
  • If you use an external speaker for sound:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Display & Sounds.
    • Select Audio Output and make the following changes:
      • TV Speakers: OFF
      • ARC MODE: Auto
      • Digital Audio Format: Auto
  • Restart your Fire TV Smart TV in one of the following ways:
    • Press and hold the Play/Pause and Select buttons together for 3-5 seconds.
    • Unplug the power cord from your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet for at least 30 seconds, and then plug it back in. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Fire TV Smart TV Is Unresponsive

Fire TV Smart TVs Help ›

Fire TV Smart TV Is Unresponsive

Use these tips to help get your Fire TV Smart TV back up and running.

  • Replace the batteries in your remote. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.
  • Follow the instructions in Use Your Mobile Device Like a Fire TV Remote to try controlling your TV with the Fire TV app.
  • Use the power cable that came with your Fire TV Smart TV.
  • Restart your Fire TV Smart TV in one of the following ways:
    • Press and hold the Play/Pause and Select buttons together for 3-5 seconds.
    • Unplug the power cord from your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet for at least 30 seconds, and then plug it back in.
  • Connect the power cable to a different power outlet.
  • Reset your Fire TV Smart TV to factory settings:
    • Press and hold the Back button and Right button together for 10 seconds.
    • Select the on-screen option to continue with the factory reset.
  • If you can’t reset your Fire TV Smart TV using your remote, try resetting from recovery mode:
    • Unplug the power cable from your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet.
    • Press and hold the physical power button that’s located on the TV. Keep holding the power button while performing the following steps:
      • Plug the power cord back into your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet.
      • Wait for the Fire TV logo to appear on the TV screen.
    • Release the power button.
    • Use your remote to select the factory reset option within the recovery mode menu.

Fix Picture Issues on Fire TV Smart TV

To resolve picture issues such as lines on the screen or blurry images, try restarting your device.

To troubleshoot picture issues, follow these steps:

  • Check that your Fire TV Smart TV software is up to date:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select About.
    • Select Check for System Update.
  • Try to restart your Fire TV Smart TV:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select Restart.
  • Your Fire TV Smart TV turns off and then back on while restarting.
  • Change the picture modes or other picture settings on your Fire TV Smart TV:
    • Press and hold the Home button or the Settings button on your Fire TV remote until the Quick Settings menu appears.
    • Select Picture, then select Picture Mode.
    • Try different picture modes like Vivid, Standard, Energy Saving, Sport, Game, Film Maker Mode, Movie Bright, and Movie Dark.
    • Note: Picture mode options vary across Fire TV devices.
    • Try different individual picture settings to check their effect on the image. Picture Reset always returns the settings to their starting point for that picture mode.
  • Try to reset your Fire TV Smart TV:
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV or Device & Software.
    • Select Reset to Factory Defaults. For more help, go to:

How to Return a Amazon Ember or Fire TV Smart TV to Amazon

There are special instructions to consider when you return a Fire TV Smart TV.

Note: This information applies to Amazon Ember or Fire TV Smart TVs developed and manufactured by Amazon.

You can replace your eligible Fire TV smart TV under warranty or return within 30 days of delivery. Use our Online Returns Center page to generate your return label and get detailed information on how to return your device.

To return your TV:

  • Visit the Factory reset your Fire TV device page for reset instructions.

  • Note: If your device doesn’t work, visit the Deregister Your Device page to remove it from your Amazon account.

  • Go to Your Orders page to display your recent orders.

  • Find the Fire TV order and select Return or Replace Items.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to create return label.

  • Use the original box and packaging to return the device.

  • Note: If you’re expecting a replacement, you can use the replacement box to return the original TV.

  • If you print the label, cover the original label on the box with your new label. Cross out any other shipping labels on the box.

  • Follow the instructions sent to your email to learn about the pick up or drop off return methods available which vary based on device size. Important: When returning the device, include all accessories that came with the device, such as:

  • TV legs

  • Wall Mount Kit (Amazon Ember Artline TV only)

  • Frame (Amazon Ember Artline TV only)

  • Note:

    • If you are returning the Ember Artline TV frame, please return it separately from the TV and do not ship in the same box.
    • If you are requesting replacement for Amazon Ember Artline TV, make sure to ship only the TV and all in-box accessories. Retain your TV frame to use with your replacement TV.

  • All power cables and adapters

  • Fire TV remote

  • Fire TV IR cable (not included with all TVs) For more help, go to:

  • Reset Your Fire TV Device to Factory Settings

  • Repackage Your Amazon Device Returns

  • Deregister Your Device

  • Select Restart.
  • Your Fire TV Smart TV turns off and then back on. If these steps don’t work, go to Reset Fire TV Smart TV to Factory Settings.

Safety Guidelines for Using a Wall Mount with Fire TV Smart TV

Keep these safety precautions in mind when mounting your device.

Note: This information applies to Fire TV Smart TV developed and manufactured by Amazon.

Warning: If you mount this TV on a wall, follow the instructions exactly as set out in the instructions provided with the wall mount (sold separately). This process requires two people.

To ensure safe installation, follow these safety precautions:

  • Check that the wall can support the weight of the TV set and wall mount assembly.

  • Follow the mounting instructions provided with the wall mount.

  • The TV set must be installed on a vertical wall.

  • Only use screws that are suitable for the wall’s material.

  • Ensure no one can trip over the TV cables. Where to place your TV:

  • Don’t place the TV on an unstable surface.

  • Place the TV somewhere with good ventilation.

  • Don’t use the TV near damp or cold areas.

  • To protect the TV from overheating, keep it away from direct sunlight.

  • Don’t expose the TV to dripping or splashing liquids. Don’t place objects filled with liquid on or near the TV. For more help, go to:

  • Set Up Your Fire TV Smart TV

  • Clean Your Fire TV Smart TV Screen

  • Attach the Support Base to Your Fire TV Smart TV Was this information helpful?

Set Up Alexa Home Theater on Your Fire TV Smart TV

To have audio from your TV and other HDMI sources (like a game console) play through your Echo speakers, set up Alexa Home Theater.

Alexa Home Theater isn’t available on all Fire TV Smart TVs. To check if Alexa Home Theater is available on your Fire TV Smart TV:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • If available, the Alexa Home Theater option appears in the menu. Before you get started:

  • Turn on Wi-Fi on your Fire TV even if your device connects to the network with an Ethernet cable. Wi-Fi is required for this feature to work.

  • Make sure that your devices are in sync by enabling Alexa Anytime on your Fire TV. Enabling this setting may increase your TV’s power consumption.

  • Devices in your speaker group should be in the same room as your TV and connected to the same Wi-Fi network. To set up Alexa Home Theater on your Fire TV Smart TV:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • Select Alexa Home Theater.

  • Select Create Alexa Home Theater.

  • Select Begin Setup.

  • When prompted, select up to two compatible Echo devices to be your speakers. You can also add an optional Echo Sub.

  • Confirm the placement of the speakers.

  • Select the option to continue. When using Alexa Home Theater, audio from your TV plays through your Echo speakers instead of the speakers configured with your TV.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Set Up Your Fire TV Smart TV

Set up and register your device to use Alexa, access the full Amazon Appstore, and receive Fire TV software updates.

  • Plug the power cord into an outlet.
  • Put batteries in your Fire TV remote.
  • Turn on your TV using the Power button on your Fire TV remote.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • Activate the Voice Commands When TV Screen is Off feature.
  • To set up Wi-Fi, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Note: If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code. To download apps and games, add a default payment method. Go to Your Payments.

Stop Fire TV Smart TV from Rebooting

Try these troubleshooting steps if your Fire TV Smart TV is continuously rebooting.

If your Fire TV Smart TV keeps rebooting:

  • Unplug the power cord from your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet for at least 30 seconds.
  • Plug the power cord back in.
  • If the issue persists, try to reset your Fire TV Smart TV to its factory settings:
    • Press and hold the Back button and Right button on your remote together for 10 seconds.
    • On the TV screen, choose to confirm or cancel the factory reset.
  • If you can’t reset your Fire TV Smart TV using your remote, try to reset from recovery mode:
    • Unplug the power cord from your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet.
    • Press and hold the physical power button on the TV.
    • While still holding the power button, plug the power cord back into your Fire TV Smart TV or wall outlet.
    • Wait for the Fire TV logo to appear on the TV screen, and then release the power button. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

Use Gaming Features on Your Fire TV Smart TV

Improve your gaming experience on Fire TV Smart TV by using Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) and Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM).

Note: VRR and ALLM aren’t available under all Fire TV Smart TVs. To check if VRR and ALLM are available on your Fire TV Smart TV:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Picture.

  • Select Input Settings.

  • Select Game. VRR and ALLM work with compatible gaming devices to enhance your gaming experience.

  • VRR: Allows your TV to synchronize its refresh rate with your gaming device for smoother viewing. This reduces stutter and screen tearing, giving you a more fluid visual experience. Depending on the device, VRR supports up to 144 Hz.

  • Note: Higher refresh rates depend on your game and the output settings of your connected gaming device.

  • ALLM: Allows your gaming device to switch your TV automatically to its low-lag game mode, giving you a more responsive gaming experience. VRR and ALLM features are activated by default for supported HDMI inputs. If you notice screen tearing, stuttering, or increased input lag while gaming, ensure that Game mode, VRR, and ALLM are activated:

  • Turn on your gaming device.

  • Switch to the appropriate HDMI input on your Fire TV.

  • Note: For compatible Fire TV Smart TVs, use HDMI 1 or 2 to activate the 120 Hz or 144 Hz refresh rate at 4K or UHD resolution.

  • Press and hold the Home button on your Fire TV remote to open the Quick Settings.

  • Select Picture.

    • Select Picture Mode.
      • Select Game.
    • Select Input Settings.
      • Select HDMI.
        • Select Input Mode.
        • Select Auto or Gaming.
      • Select Game.
        • Make sure VRR and ALLM are set to ON. Note: If issue persists, check that your gaming console’s VRR and ALLM settings are also properly configured.

Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV Smart TV

Use compatible Alexa devices to do things like control the volume on your Fire TV Smart TV or turn it on and off.

Note: A few things to keep in mind:

  • Fire TV Smart TVs don’t respond to voice commands while powered off or in standby mode. For Fire TV Omni TVs, turn on Alexa Anytime in Settings to give voice commands when your TV screen is off or in standby mode.
  • If Alexa Announcements are on for your Fire TV Smart TV, Announcements play even if your device is in standby mode. You can manage Announcement settings in the Alexa app. For Fire TV Omni TVs, you can also manage Announcements from your device Settings.
  • Some Alexa voice commands are only available in select languages.
  • For voice commands to browse content or control video playback, go to Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV. To control more features and settings on your Fire TV Smart TV, link your Alexa device and Fire TV Smart TV in the Alexa app.

To turn off the microphones on your Fire TV Omni TVs, slide the Microphone On/Off switch on the bottom of the TV. When muted, it lights up red.

Use voice commands like these examples below to control the volume on your Fire TV Smart TV, switch input channels, and browse live TV.

Input switching and power:

  • “Turn Fire TV [on/off].”

  • Tip: To use this voice command, select Turn on TV with Alexa in your Fire TV settings.

  • “Turn [up/down] the volume on Fire TV.”

  • “Switch to [input].” Browse Live TV:

  • “Open TV guide.”

  • “Go to [channel / network].”

  • “Change to [channel / network].” Change sound and picture settings:

  • “Set the picture mode to dynamic.”

  • “Mute Fire TV.

  • “Change the sound mode to sports.”

  • “Increase [Treble/Midrange/Bass].”

  • “Decrease [Treble/Midrange/Bass].”

  • “Reset the equalizer.” For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

For more help, go to:

What is Drop In on Your Amazon Ember or Fire TV Smart TV?

Drop In is a feature that lets you connect instantly to supported Alexa devices.

This information applies to:

  • Amazon Ember Artline TV (2026 Release)
  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series
  • Fire TV Omni Series Use Drop In to open an instant conversation between your devices or with your Alexa contacts. To use Drop In with your TV, give access to friends and family in the Alexa app.

Few things to consider when using Drop In on your TV:

  • When you receive a Drop In, your TV plays an incoming Drop In tone and the active call begins.
  • If a compatible web cam is connected, your video is visible after the frosted window appears.
  • If your TV is off when you get a Drop In, it turns on to start the Drop In.
  • If your TV is turned off during a Drop In, the Drop In ends.
  • If a compatible web cam is connected, the camera is automatically activated for Drop In.
Alexa Anytime

When activated, Alexa Anytime allows you to give voice commands and use features, such as smart home and communications, when your TV screen is off.

Note: Your TV will automatically turn on during certain actions, such as when you make or receive a call, drop in, or announcements.

Audio Not Playing on Fire TV Soundbars

Check your device connections and connect the soundbar to your TV’s HDMI ARC or eARC port.

To troubleshoot audio issues:

  • Disconnect the HDMI cable from your TV and the soundbar.

  • Unplug the soundbar power cable from the power source for 30 seconds.

  • Reconnect the HDMI cable and the power cable and try playing audio again. To learn how to manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on common TV brands, visit Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.

  • Disconnect all other devices connected to your TV and then connect the soundbar again before connecting the other devices. If the issue persists:

  • Set the HDMI CEC function on your TV to On.

  • Set the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to Soundbar or Audio. For further troubleshooting, refer to your TV’s manual.

Can’t Pair Fire TV Soundbar Plus Speakers

Try these steps if either a blinking amber light or no light appears on the back of your subwoofer or surround speakers.

This information applies to the following devices:

  • Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer

  • Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer and Surround Speakers The subwoofer and surround speakers connect automatically to your soundbar. To manually connect, follow these steps:

  • Place your subwoofer and surround speakers (if you purchased the surround speakers) in the same room as your soundbar, within at least 10 meters.

  • Unplug the power cables from the power outlet for three seconds, and then plug them back in.

  • Factory reset the soundbar.

    • Press and hold the power button on your soundbar for 10 seconds.
    • Wait until the soundbar turns off and then back on.

  • Press the connect button on the back of the speaker that you need to connect.

  • Note: If you need to reconnect both the subwoofer and the speaker set, connect the Subwoofer first, then the Left speaker, and finally the Right speaker. When the speakers connect to your soundbar, a white LED appears on their connect buttons.

Change the Audio Settings on Fire TV Soundbars

Use the remote that came with your soundbar to adjust the bass, equalizer and surround sound settings.

This information applies to the following devices:

  • Fire TV Soundbar
  • Fire TV Soundbar Plus Series You can use your soundbar remote to change the audio settings listed in the table below.

Note: For Fire TV Soundbar Plus, you can also adjust the sound settings within Display & Sounds on compatible Fire TV devices. Visit Control Fire TV Soundbar Plus Sound Settings on Fire TV for more information.

Audio Setting

Description

Equalizer Mode

To cycle through the equalizer modes on your soundbar, press the EQ button on your remote.

You can choose between Movie, Music, or Dialogue to match the sound experience you want.

Bass

To cycle through your soundbar’s bass levels, press the BASS button on your remote.

You can choose between low, medium, or high bass levels to fit your preference.

Surround Effect

Press the Surround Effect button on your soundbar remote to turn surround sound on or off.

Input

Press the Input button to change inputs on your soundbar.

Treble

Note: This setting is only available for Fire TV Soundbar Plus.

To cycle through your soundbar’s trebel levels, press the TREBLE button on your remote.

Dialogue Enhancer

Note: This setting is only available for Fire TV Soundbar Plus.

Press the DIALOG button on your soundbar remote to adjust the dialog clarity.

You can also long press DIALOG to turn on or off DTS TruVolume.

Surround Speakers

Note: This setting is only available for the Fire TV Soundbar Plus Series with subwoofer and surround speakers.

Adjust the volume and balance of your surround speakers:

  • Press the L and R buttons on the soundbar remote to adjust the left and right speaker balance.
    • Pressing L shifts the balance to the left, while pressing R shifts the balance to the right.
  • Use the – SURR + buttons to adjust the surround speaker volume.

Fire TV Remote Not Working with Fire TV Soundbar

If your Fire TV remote isn’t working to control your soundbar, set up equipment control on your Fire TV.

Before getting started, locate your Fire TV and Fire TV Soundbar remotes.

Fire TV devices automatically detect compatible equipment and provide on-screen instructions to add them.

If your Fire TV device doesn’t detect your soundbar, or you’re using an optical cable, set up equipment control in your Fire TV settings:

Note: To use your TV remote with your soundbar outside of the Fire TV experience, connect the soundbar to your TV’s HDMI ARC input.

  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment.
  • Select Add Equipment, and then select Soundbar. For supported devices, visit Compatible Devices for Fire TV and Alexa Equipment Control.

How to Wall Mount Fire TV Soundbar Plus

Fire TV Soundbar Help ›

How to Wall Mount Fire TV Soundbar Plus

For the optimal sound experience, position the soundbar close to ear level when seated for viewing.

Before getting started, you’ll need:

  • The included wall mounting template, anchors, screws, and brackets.
  • An electric drill with a 5/16” drill bit and a Phillips #2 driver bit.
  • A hammer
  • A level or level app
  • Wall-safe tape Important: Don’t drill holes into electrical wiring or piping.

To mount your soundbar to the wall:

  • Use a level to tape the included template to the wall under your TV.

  • When using the anchors, drill holes where the template indicates ‘MARK HERE’. Remove the template and then tap the anchors into the holes.

  • Note: The included anchors and screws are recommended to use with drywall. When using the anchors, don’t drill into studs.

  • Insert the included screws into the brackets and then screw them into the anchors.

  • Position the soundbar on the brackets. Carefully align the soundbar screw holes on the brackets and the bottom of the soundbar.

  • Fasten the soundbar screws until the soundbar is secure. For more help, go to:

  • How to Set Up Fire TV Soundbar Plus

  • How to Wall Mount Fire TV Soundbar Was this information helpful?

Restart Fire TV Soundbars

To solve most intermittent issues, restart your soundbar.

To restart your soundbar:

  • Press the power button on your Fire TV Soundbar or on the included remote.
  • White LED lights on your soundbar flash three times while powering off.
  • Press the power button again.
  • White LED lights turn on and then off again while powering on. You can also unplug the power cable for three seconds, then plug it back in.

For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

What is DTS Virtual:X or DTS:X on Fire TV Soundbars?

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

More Fire TV Devices ›

Fire TV Soundbar Help ›

What is DTS Virtual:X or DTS:X on Fire TV Soundbars?

With Dolby Atmos and DTS audio technology, you get an immersive multi-dimensional sound experience similar to how we hear sound in our daily lives.

On Fire TV Soundbars, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, and DTS Virtual:X improve your audio experience while watching movies, shows, and listening to music.

Dolby Atmos features clear dialogue and 3D sound that moves around you. It adds overhead and surround channels to make the audio feel more lifelike and spacious. Similarly, DTS:X delivers multi-dimensional audio for lifelike sound.

Note: The Fire TV Soundbar (2-channel) doesn’t support DTS:X. The soundbar features DTS Virtual:X to improve your audio experience.

DTS Virtual:X is an immersive audio format from DTS that brings three-dimensional, cinema-quality audio to your TV. DTS Virtual:X simulates a 3D sound experience without the need for overhead or surround speakers.

To get started, connect your Fire TV Soundbar directly to your TV’s HDMI ARC or eARC port and start listening to music and watching your favorite shows. No additional set-up required.

Automatic Content Recognition

Find more solutions

Fire TV Terms & Conditions ›

Automatic Content Recognition

  1. What is automatic content recognition?

When Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) is enabled, Amazon uses ACR to understand which shows, movies, and advertisements you watch on your Fire TV smart TV through connected devices, such as a cable set-top-box. To do this, Amazon creates a digital fingerprint of the content you watch on your TV from encoded audio or pixel samples of the content. Amazon then uses ACR to match the fingerprint to content in a database of movies, TV shows, and ads. The fingerprints are discarded if they do not match content in the database. For example, a fingerprint from a home video will not match content that is in the database and will be discarded.

  1. What data does Amazon collect with ACR?

When ACR is enabled, Amazon collects viewing data about content you view on your Fire TV smart TV through connected devices. Viewing data includes information such as the networks, channels, advertisements, and programs watched. This data may be combined with other personal information, such as account and device identifiers.

  1. How is my viewing experience improved?

When you enable ACR on your Fire TV smart TV, Amazon collects data about what you view on your TV to improve products and services to create a better viewing experience, starting with fewer repetitive ads on Fire TV. In the future, we may use this data to help you discover more content to watch and more ways to watch. For example, we may recommend similar shows and movies to what you have watched on TV or show you new apps or subscription services that have content you may like.

  1. What do you mean by fewer repetitive ads?

We use the viewing data collected by ACR to determine the ads you were shown while viewing content on your Fire TV smart TV through your connected devices. For example, if ACR determines that you have already seen the same ad multiple times while watching TV through the cable provider set-top-box, Amazon may not show the same ad on your Fire TV when you watch Freevee, Prime Video, or when third-party apps use Amazon’s ad network to display ads. Not all ads on this device are displayed by Amazon, and we won’t be able to reduce repetition for those ads.

  1. If I enable ACR on one device, is it enabled for all of my devices?

No. Enabling ACR on one device won’t enable the setting on your other Fire TV devices.

  1. If I turn off ACR, how does it affect my Fire TV features?

Turning off ACR will not change the basic functionality of your device or whether you see ads, though those ads may be more repetitious.

  1. How do I manage my ACR preferences?

You can change your ACR preferences on your Fire TV device by visiting Settings → Preferences → Privacy Settings → Automatic Content Recognition.

  1. Where can I learn more about other privacy settings on Fire TV?

You can learn more about other privacy settings here.

Cloud App FAQs for Vega Fire TV Devices

Find more solutions

Fire TV Terms & Conditions ›

Cloud App FAQs for Vega Fire TV Devices

What are cloud apps?

On Vega Fire TV devices, some apps are now run as cloud apps. Instead of running only on your device like other apps, cloud apps are installed and run on servers in the Amazon cloud, and the app experience is streamed to your device. When a cloud app is installed, the app’s icon appears on your device. When you start the app, software on your device connects to the Amazon cloud and provides the streamed app experience on your TV or other display.

You can tell which apps are cloud apps in two ways.

  • In the Appstore: View an app’s description page. For cloud apps, you’ll see the text “Amazon cloud-hosted app.”
  • On your device: Go to Settings > Applications > Manage Installed Apps, and select an app. For cloud apps, you’ll see the text “This app runs and stores its data in the Amazon cloud.”
Where do cloud apps use and store app data?

Apps typically use and store data, like login information, on your device. Cloud apps also use and store data, but because a cloud app runs on a server in the Amazon cloud, the app data is used and stored on an Amazon server. To learn more about how app developers use your personal data, please review the app developer’s privacy policy.

How is my cloud app data protected in Amazon’s cloud?

Cloud app data is encrypted with a key unique to your device and your Amazon account.

How do I delete my cloud app data from the Amazon cloud?

You can delete your cloud app data from the Amazon cloud for each app or for all cloud apps as follows:

  • For one cloud app: Go to Settings > Applications > Manage Installed Apps, and select an app. Select Clear App Data or Uninstall to delete cloud app data for that app.
  • For all cloud apps: Reset your device to factory settings by navigating to Settings > My Fire TV and selecting Reset to Factory Defaults. Factory resetting your device removes your account information and downloaded content.
What if a developer releases an on-device version of a cloud app?

If you’ve installed a cloud app and a newer version of this app is available for on-device installation, we’ll automatically replace the cloud app with the updated version on your device. You won’t have to do anything to install the app on your device, and you can always manage your apps, including what apps are installed on your device or in the cloud, by navigating to Settings > Applications > Manage Installed Apps. The availability of cloud apps, ability to use cloud apps, and availability of content within cloud apps varies by your country of residence and the location of the device.

What is the internet speed required to use cloud apps?

While cloud app streaming technology can adapt to a wide range of internet speeds and network conditions, we recommend an internet speed of at least 8 Mbps to enjoy the best cloud app experience.

Find Your Fire TV Serial Number

Your Fire TV’s serial number helps Amazon provide device support and warranty services when you need assistance.

Your Fire TV device serial number is a unique set of 16 letters and numbers. Try the following methods to find your Fire TV’s serial number:

  • Check Device Settings
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select My Fire TV.
    • Select About.
    • Look for “Serial Number” in the device information.
  • Check Original Packaging
    • Find a label with a barcode on the device packaging.
    • Check the label for the device serial number (DSN).
  • Scan QR Code
  • This option applies to the following devices:
    • Fire TV Stick 4K Select
    • Fire TV Stick HD (2nd Generation)
    • Disconnect your Fire TV Stick from your TV.
    • If you use an HDMI extender, remove the extender from your Fire TV Stick.
    • Locate your Fire TV Stick’s HDMI connector.
    • Scan the QR code with your smartphone’s camera or QR code scanner app.
  • Check Device Summary
    • Go to Manage Your Devices.
    • Select Fire TV, and then select your Fire TV device.
    • Look for “Serial number” within the Device Summary section.

How to Play Games on Fire TV

Go to Games on Fire TV to find compatible Amazon Appstore games on your Fire TV device. You can also find your Amazon Luna games.

You can access Games on Fire TV devices running Fire OS 5 or higher. To check the latest software versions for Fire TV devices, visit Fire TV Device and Accessory Software Updates.

Note: You can’t access Games on Fire TV from a Kids profile.

To play Games on Fire TV:

  • Go to Games on your Fire TV Home screen.
    • If your Fire TV doesn’t have a Games menu option, go to Find to access your games.
  • Select the game that you want to play.
  • Select Get to download the game.
    • To purchase the game, select the Shopping Cart and follow the on-screen instructions to complete the purchase.
    • To play the game with Amazon Luna, select Play with Amazon Luna and follow the on-screen prompts.
    • Note: Some games require a subscription. Turning on parental controls prevents Twitch content from appearing in Games on Fire TV.

Settings Menu

The Settings menu has the following options, displayed as tiles:

The Settings menu comes with a search bar to quickly find few popular settings.

  • If you don’t find a specific setting through the search bar, select the applicable tile to view all settings. Profiles - Choose from the profiles on your device, edit a profile, or create a new one.

Network - Connect your Fire TV to the internet and manage your network settings.

Display & Sounds - Adjust the screensaver, set the video resolution, change the audio output, or manage display mirroring, HDMI CEC settings, and more.

Applications - Manage the settings for the Appstore and the apps installed on your Fire TV.

Equipment Control - Manage how your Fire TV device interacts with your connected equipment. You can add and manage devices such as compatible A/V receivers or soundbars.

  • To learn more about Equipment Control, visit the What is Equipment Control with Fire TV? page. Controllers & Bluetooth Devices - Add and remove compatible remotes, game controllers, and Bluetooth devices.

Preferences - Manage Parental Controls, access your notification and privacy settings, or change the language and time displayed on your Fire TV.

My Fire TV or Device & Software - Update the software on your Fire TV and display available storage.

You can also perform device functions like restart, sleep, and reset to factory defaults.

Accessibility - Turn on accessibility features such as:

  • Explore Your Remote
  • VoiceView
  • High Contrast Text
  • Closed Captions To learn more, visit Accessibility Features for Fire TV.

Account & Profile Settings - Manage the registered account on your Fire TV. You can also select Sync Amazon Content to refresh the content on your Fire TV.
