Navigate the New Fire TV Experience

Learn how to navigate the new Fire TV home screen, main menu, and settings menu.

The new Fire TV Experience is available on the following devices:

  • Fire TV Stick 4K (2nd Generation)

  • Fire TV Stick 4K Plus

  • Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2nd Generation)

  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release, newest model)

  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release, newest model)

  • Amazon Ember 4-Series and Fire TV 4-Series (2025 Release, newest model)

  • Amazon Ember 2-Series and Fire TV 2-Series To learn how to navigate other Fire TV devices, visit this Help page instead: Navigate the Fire TV Home Screen

  • Fire TV Home Screen

  • Main Menu

  • Settings Menu

Fire TV Home Screen

The categories on your Fire TV Home screen help you navigate your Fire TV experience.

Availability for some of the categories may vary across countries and devices.

Search - Your search and discovery tool for Fire TV content. You can:

  • Quickly locate movies and TV shows across multiple streaming services.
  • Find and download apps.
  • Discover new entertainment.
  • Find a personalized collection of music and podcasts. Home - Your central hub for finding your apps and recently watched content.

Movies - Explore movies that are available through your Fire TV.

Press and hold the Home button on your remote to access key settings and features without leaving playback.

TV Shows - Watch your favorite TV shows.

Live TV - Watch live TV channels from supported apps or access content from your active subscriptions.

  • Live TV may require active subscriptions to supported streaming services. News - Stay updated on the latest news.

Long-press the Select button to find more options for the content on your Fire TV. You can do things like add a movie or tv show to your Watchlist, uninstall an app, reorder your Apps row, and more.

Back to top

Main Menu

Open your Fire TV’s main menu to find more features, access your saved content, and manage your device settings. You can use the Menu button on your remote or navigate to the menu icon on the side of your Fire TV.

Fire TV Profiles - Choose from the profiles on your device, edit a profile, or create a new one.

Inputs - Access the Input menu on your Fire TV.

Movies & TV - Browse and watch movies and TV shows.

Appstore - Explore apps and games that you can download on your Fire TV.

Games - Discover and play games directly on your Fire TV.

My Stuff - A personal hub for your saved and recorded content on Fire TV.

Art & Photos - Explore art and photo collections to display them on your Fire TV screen. You can explore the following categories and set them as your Fire TV screensaver:

  • Curated art photography collections
  • Your Amazon Photos collections
  • Create AI Art with Alexa
  • Motion Art
  • Interactive Art scenes that respond to your presence and movement Settings - Manage your Fire TV device settings.

Smart Home - Control your smart home devices.

Ambient - Activate your Fire TV’s Ambient Experience. Ambient Experience displays curated art, personal photos while your Fire TV is idle.

You can also activate the Ambient Experience by pressing the Alexa button on your remote.

Back to top

Settings Menu

Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu to manage your device settings.

You can also access Settings by asking Alexa, “Go to Settings.”

Network - Connect your Fire TV to the internet and manage your network settings.

Display & Sounds - Adjust the screensaver, set the video resolution, change the audio output, or manage display mirroring, HDMI CEC settings, and more.

Applications - Manage the settings for the Appstore and the apps installed on your Fire TV.

Equipment Control - Manage how your Fire TV device interacts with your connected equipment. You can add and manage devices such as compatible A/V receivers or soundbars.

Controllers & Bluetooth Devices - Add and remove compatible remotes, game controllers, and Bluetooth devices.

Preferences - Manage parental controls, access your notification and privacy settings, or change the language and time displayed on your Fire TV.

My Fire TV or Device & Software - Update the software on your Fire TV and display available storage. You can also perform device functions like restart, sleep, and reset to factory defaults.

Accessibility - Turn on accessibility features to enhance your Fire TV experience:

  • VoiceView: Speaks on-screen text out loud as you navigate menu options and setting.
  • High Contrast Text: Improves text readability for users with low vision.
  • Closed Captions: Display subtitles for users who are deaf or hard of hearing. To learn more, visit Accessibility Features for Fire TV.

Account & Profile Settings - Manage the registered account and the profiles on your Fire TV. You can also select Sync Amazon Content to refresh the content on your Fire TV.

Watch Prime Video on Your Fire TV

Access Prime Video content from the home screen, through search, or from the Prime Video app.

There are several ways to access Prime Video content on your Fire TV:

Home Screen

Browse Prime Video content from the recommendations on your Fire TV home screen. You can scroll up or down the home screen to access different content categories.

Search

You can search for content from your Fire TV home screen. Go to Find and then Search to get started. You can also use a remote with Alexa Voice button to search by voice.

Your search results display content from Prime Video as well as other supported providers, such as:

  • Prime Video add-on subscriptions
  • Streaming services with subscriptions.
  • Streaming services with free ad-supported content. Videos included with Prime Video have the Watch Now with Prime option.
Prime Video App

Open the Prime Video app to access videos included with your Amazon Prime or Prime Video membership. You can browse for content on the home screen or from Find . You can also use a remote with Alexa Voice button to search by voice.

You can also cast Prime Video content to your Fire TV using a mobile device. To learn more, visit Cast Apps to Fire TV.

What Is Code-Based Linking on Fire TV?

Code-based linking lets you use your mobile phone or computer to quickly register a Fire TV device to your Amazon account.

The following Fire TV devices don’t support code-based linking:

  • Fire TV Recast You can set up a new Fire TV device by signing in on the device itself, or by visiting the amazon.com/code page. On this site you can:

  • Sign in to an existing Amazon account and then enter the code displayed on your device.

  • Create a new Amazon account and then enter the code displayed on your device. For more information on how to set up Fire TV devices, go to Set Up Your Fire TV.

What Types of Subscriptions Are Available on Fire TV?

Get Started with Fire TV ›

What Types of Subscriptions Are Available on Fire TV?

Subscriptions let you access additional content from Prime Video and other streaming services. Learn more about the types of subscriptions supported on your Fire TV.

Prime Video (included with Amazon Prime membership)

As a Prime member, you can watch movies and TV shows from the Prime Video catalog at no extra cost. Eligible titles have “ Included with Prime” in the video description.

Prime Video Add-On Subscriptions

Prime Video add-on subscriptions are additional, paid subscriptions that let you access content from third-party networks and streaming services. You can pay for the subscriptions you want and cancel anytime from your Amazon account.

Note: Only Amazon Prime members can subscribe to Prime Video add-on subscriptions.

Amazon Appstore Subscriptions

Amazon Appstore subscriptions are paid subscriptions that let you access content from third-party networks and streaming services.

To get started, download the app for the service you’d like to watch and then select the option to begin your subscription.

You can change, update, cancel, or turn off auto-renewals for these subscriptions in your Amazon account. Follow the steps in the Manage Your Appstore Subscriptions from the Website page.

Other Streaming Services

If you have an existing subscription with a third-party network or streaming service, you may be able to watch that content on your Fire TV.

Download the app for the service that you’d like to watch, if available, and then sign in using your login information for that service.

Pair Your Amazon Luna Controller to Your Fire TV

After setting up your Luna Controller, you can pair it to your Fire TV device with Bluetooth and use it as a remote.

  • Power on your Luna Controller.
  • Put your Luna Controller in Bluetooth pairing mode by holding the Action and B buttons for 3 seconds (until there’s a pulsing white light).
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV to pair your Luna Controller:
    • Select Controllers and Bluetooth Devices.
    • Choose Game Controllers.
    • Select Add New Game Controller.
    • When your Luna Controller appears in the list of devices, select it and wait for pairing to complete. When you exit the Luna app, your Luna Controller automatically switches to Bluetooth mode, letting you control your Fire TV device with your Luna Controller. The Luna button LED indicator changes from purple to white to show the change in connection type.

You can also use the Luna Controller app to pair your Luna Controller with Bluetooth. Check out Manage Your Luna Controller Bluetooth Connections Using the Luna Controller App for more information.

Note: For the best gaming experience, your Luna Controller automatically switches to Cloud Direct mode when playing games on Luna.

Use Alexa on an Amazon Luna Controller Paired With Fire TV

After pairing your Luna Controller with a compatible Fire TV device, you can use Alexa voice commands and control your Fire TV device with your controller.

To talk to Alexa when your Luna Controller is connected to Fire TV:

  • Bluetooth: Press and hold the Microphone button and ask Alexa things like, “What’s the weather?”

  • Cloud Direct: When playing games through Luna, your Luna Controller switches automatically to Cloud Direct mode. Press and hold the Microphone button and ask Alexa things like “Play Control.” Note: Although Alexa on Luna Controller is supported only on Fire TV devices, Alexa may wake on your Android devices if:

  • Alexa is your default voice assistant on your Android device.

  • You long press the Luna button when your Luna Controller is paired to your Android device with Bluetooth. To learn how to disable this functionality, contact your device manufacturer for instructions.

Deregister Your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in

If you no longer wish to use the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in, or want to use it with a different account, you can deregister it from your Amazon account by going into the Account & Profile Settings section of the device settings and selecting Deregister.

  • Click Devices.
  • Select your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in.
  • Select Deregister.
  • Once you deregister, you’re prompted to register again to connect the device to a different Amazon account.

Find Purchased Content on the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in

Access your purchased or rented video content in the Library tab of the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in Home screen. Find your apps and games in the Appstore under the Find tab.

Purchased content is saved to your Amazon account. This includes movies, TV shows, apps, games, and music. You can access your purchased content on any Fire TV device registered to your account.

On the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in, your purchased movies and TV shows are in the Library. You can find all your downloaded Prime Video titles, along with any movies or TV shows you’ve added to your Watchlist.

Access your purchased music, playlists, and the Amazon Music library by opening the Music app on your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in.

You can listen to personalized music experience on the Amazon Music app based on the selected Fire TV profile.

Note: The Amazon Music app isn’t available with BMW vehicles.

In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in Console Integration

In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in integrates with the center console display to provide device management options from the front seat.

Console integration isn’t available for the following vehicles:

  • Ford Expedition

  • Lincoln Navigator

  • BMW: i7 Series, and 7 Series With the center console display in the front seat, you have control over the two rear-seat screens. You can:

  • Set the content that is playing on either screen. You can have both screens playing separate content or the same content at the same time.

  • Control the content. You can pause, rewind, and fast-forward what is playing on either screen.

  • Control the volume. Each screen can listen individually with headphones or you can listen as a group and have the sound come through the vehicle speakers.

In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in Won’t Connect to Wi-Fi

Try these troubleshooting steps if you can’t connect to Wi-Fi, your videos are buffering, or the “Home is Currently Unavailable” message appear.

Note: The In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in for BMW vehicles doesn’t support Wi-fi. The device is connected directly to your vehicle’s mobile network.

If you’re having connectivity problems, the network status tool can help identify and fix them. To use the network status tool:

  • Go to Settings .

  • Select Network .

  • Press Play/Pause on your remote.

  • Follow the recommended steps. If the connection issue persists try the following:

  • Confirm that you’re using a Wi-Fi password and not an Amazon account password.

  • If safe to do so, turn off your vehicle for ten minutes and turn it back on.

  • Check your surroundings. Some geographical features can block network reception.

  • Contact the network service provider.

Set Up Your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in

Power on your vehicle and follow the on-screen instructions to complete your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in setup.

If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, reset your password.

Forgot Your Password

For Jeep, Chrysler, Ford, Lincoln vehicles:

  • Put batteries in your Fire TV remotes.

  • Power on your vehicle.

  • Pair your remote by pressing the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to connect to Wi-Fi and download the latest software update.

  • Note: If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.

  • Sign in with your Amazon account. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.

  • Follow the on-screen prompts to download popular apps and complete the setup process. For BMW vehicles:

  • Turn on the touchscreen door controller.

  • Press the Fold down button to fold down the theatre screen.

  • Sign in with your Amazon account. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.

  • Follow the on-screen prompts to download popular apps and complete the setup process. To download apps and games, add a default payment method. Go to Your Payments.

Turn on Parental Screen Lock on Your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in

To lock the backseat screens so that they don’t respond to touch or the remote, turn on the parental lock screen.

Parental Screen Lock isn’t available for the following vehicles:

  • Ford Expedition

  • Lincoln Navigator

  • BMW: i7 Series, and 7 Series To lock the rear seat screens:

  • On the front seat screen, select Media.

  • Select Rear Seat.

  • Select the Lock icon under the desired screen or select Lock All to lock all screens. The rear screens won’t respond to touch or the remote while the screen is locked. Content that is currently playing continues to play.

You can follow the same steps to unlock a specific screen or unlock all screens.

Unable to Update In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in Device Software

Your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in update fails or your update doesn’t complete.

  • Check that your Fire TV device is connected to the internet.

    • For Jeep, Chrysler, Ford, Lincoln vehicles: Go to Settings , and then select Network . Press Play/Pause on your remote to test your connection.
    • For BMW vehicles: The In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in for BMW vehicles doesn’t support Wi-fi. The device is connected directly to your vehicle’s mobile network.

  • If your device has connectivity issues, turn off your vehicle for ten minutes and then start it again.

  • Confirm that your Fire TV device has enough available storage to download the update (at least 500 MB). Go to Settings , and then select My Fire TV. Select About, and then Storage. To provide more available storage, uninstall apps by going to Settings on your device. For more help, go to:

  • In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in Won’t Connect to Wi-Fi

Use Alexa with the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in

Use the Voice Remote with Alexa to do things like search for content and control video playback on your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in.

Alexa isn’t available for the following vehicles:

  • BMW: i7 Series, and 7 Series Once you’ve paired your Voice Remote with Alexa with your In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in, press the microphone button on the remote to give commands. You can have Alexa do things like:

  • Search for movies and TV shows

  • Play specific movies or TV shows

  • Control media, such as play/pause and adjusting the volume

  • Play music playlists You can find examples of Alexa commands by visiting the Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV page.

Some vehicles also feature an Alexa button on the steering wheel. This is separate from the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in, and this button doesn’t interact with the In-Car Entertainment with Fire TV built-in.

Network Issues on Fire TV

Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Network Issues on Fire TV ›

Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi

Try this troubleshooting if you can’t connect to Wi-Fi, your videos buffer, or the message “Unable to Connect” appears.

If you can’t connect to Wi-Fi while setting up your Fire TV, go to Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi

Follow these steps to fix Wi-Fi connection issues with your Fire TV device.

  • Check Network Status
  • Restart Your Fire TV and Reset Your Wi-Fi Connection
  • Restart Your Modem and Router
  • Factory Reset Your Fire TV
  • Tips to prevent future Wi-Fi Issues
Check Network Status
  • From the Unable to Connect error message, select Network Diagnostics.
    • Check your Wi-Fi connection status.
    • Tip: On compatible devices, you can also select Run Speed Test or Advanced for detailed connection information.
  • Follow the on-screen recommendations to restore your connection. Note: Fire TV devices include an on-device network status tool to help diagnose and troubleshoot connectivity issues. You can access this tool from Fire TV Settings. Open Settings , select Network , and press Play/Pause on your remote. To learn more, go to What is the Fire TV Network Status Tool?
Restart Your Fire TV and Reset Your Wi-Fi Connection
  • Unplug your Fire TV from power, wait for 10 seconds, then plug it back in.
  • If you still can’t connect, or your network name doesn’t appear, reset your Wi-Fi connection by following these steps:
    • Go to Settings.
    • Select Network .
    • Select Wi-Fi and turn it off, then back on.
  • If it still doesn’t work, follow these steps to Forget your Wi-Fi network, then reconnect:
    • Go to Settings and Select Network.
    • Find your network name.
    • Press the Menu button, then Select / OK button to forget the network.
    • Re-enter your Wi-Fi password to reconnect. If you can’t find your password, go to Locate Your Wi-Fi Password for more help.
Restart Your Modem and Router

  • Unplug your modem and router and then wait 1 minute.

  • Plug in your modem first and wait ~1 minute for the lights to turn on and for it to connect to the internet.

  • Plug in your router and wait ~1 minute for the lights to turn on and for it to connect to the internet. Tip:

  • If possible, move your Fire TV and router closer for a stronger signal.

  • If multiple devices on your network have gone offline, you may have a network outage. Go to Troubleshooting Network Outage for more information.

Factory Reset Your Fire TV

If none of the above steps work, reset your Fire TV to factory settings. For steps, go to Reset Your Fire TV Device to Factory Settings for Fire TV and Reset Fire TV Smart TV to Factory Settings for Fire TV Smart TV.

Tips to prevent future Wi-Fi Issues

Optimize your Wi-Fi

Fire TV devices with Wi-Fi 6E support 6-GHz band connections, offering faster speeds, increased bandwidth, and lower latency. To get the best performance from your Fire TV device, consider upgrading to Wi-Fi 6E or higher capable router. For larger homes, consider mesh routers for whole-home coverage.

Additionally, configure your router to use the same network name (SSID) for the 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz bands. This allows your Fire TV to automatically connect to the best-performing band based on signal strength.

For more help, go to:

  • Restart Your Fire TV Device
  • Fire TV Isn’t Turning ON
  • Amazon Fire TV forum Was this information helpful?

What is the Fire TV Network Status Tool?

What is the Fire TV Network Status Tool?

The Network Status tool helps you identify and troubleshoot network connectivity issues on your Fire TV device.

You can use the Network Status tool by going to Settings and then Network on your device.

Note: To access the Network Status Tool during connectivity issue, select Network Diagnostics on Unable to connect error screen.

The Network Status tool lets you check things like:

  • The network connection status, which is the connection between your Fire TV and router.

  • The internet connection status, which is the connection between your router and the internet.

  • A recommendation section with connectivity status and information on how to fix specific connectivity issues observed by your Fire TV. Some compatible Fire TV devices have additional options, such as:

  • The results of network download speed tests.

  • An Advanced button, which shows detailed network information including data usage.

  • A Run Speed Test button, with the option to run the speed test again. For more help, go to:

  • Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi Was this information helpful?

Safety and Compliance for Fire TV Devices

Safety and Compliance Information

Find more solutions

Fire TV Terms & Conditions ›

Safety and Compliance for Fire TV Devices ›

Safety and Compliance Information

Safety and Compliance Information

Use Responsibly. Read all instructions and safety information before use.

FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

Maintaining Your Amazon Fire TV and Fire TV Stick

Do not use your Amazon Fire TV or Fire TV Stick (collectively “Amazon Fire TV Devices”) or their accessories near sinks or other wet locations. Take care not to spill any food or liquid on your Amazon Fire TV Devices and do not put any object filled with a liquid, such as a vase, on or near your Amazon Fire TV Devices. If your device does get wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device to dry completely before plugging it in again. Do not attempt to dry your Amazon Fire TV Devices with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or hair dryer.

Only handle your Amazon Fire TV Devices with clean hands. Clean your Amazon Fire TV Devices only with a soft cloth that is slightly damp with water and a touch of rubbing alcohol; be careful not to wipe it with anything abrasive or to use any harsh chemicals. Don’t expose your Amazon Fire TV Devices to steam, extreme heat or cold. For example, do not install your Amazon Fire TV Devices near any heat sources such as space heaters, heater vents, radiators, stoves, or other things that produce heat.

Use of third party accessories may impact your Amazon Fire TV Devices’ performance. In limited circumstances, use of third party accessories may void your Amazon Fire TV Devices’ limited warranty. Read all safety instructions for any accessories before using with your Amazon Fire TV Devices.

Your Amazon Fire TV Devices do not have an on/off button. If you wish to stop power from flowing into your device, unplug the power adapter. Only use the included power adapter with your Amazon Fire TV Devices. Do not force the power adapter into a power outlet. If the power adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately. Do not plug multiple electric devices into the same wall socket. Overloading a socket can cause it to overheat and may result in a fire.

Your Amazon Fire TV Devices may get hot during normal use. If you find the device has become hot to the touch, unplug power and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.

Batteries

This product contains alkaline. The remotes for your Amazon Fire TV Devices require batteries for use. Only use new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. Do not open, disassemble, puncture, cut, bend, shred or heat the batteries and do not allow metal objects to touch the battery terminals on the remote as they can become hot and cause burns. Remove all batteries if they are worn out or before storing your remote for an extended period of time. Dispose of all batteries in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and do not dispose of batteries by throwing them into a fire. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

Servicing Your Device

If your device needs service, please contact Amazon Customer Support. Contact details can be found at amazon.com.

Faulty service may void the warranty.

Other Safety Considerations

  • A small percentage of people may be susceptible to blackouts or seizures (even if they have never had one before) when exposed to flashing lights or light patterns, such as when watching video or playing games. If you have experienced seizures or blackouts or have a family history of such occurrences, you should consult a doctor before watching videos or playing games.
  • Engaging in repetitive motions such as pressing buttons or playing some games may cause you to experience occasional discomfort in your hands, arms, shoulders, neck, or other parts of your body.
  • Discontinue use of your device and consult a physician if you experience headaches, blackouts, seizures, convulsion, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, involuntary movement, disorientation, or other discomfort. To reduce risk of these symptoms avoid prolonged use, watch your television from a far distance and in a well-lit room, and take frequent breaks.
  • Handle your Amazon Fire TV Devices with care. Your Amazon Fire TV Devices may have pointed edges which can lead to scratches, cuts, or other physical injury.
  • Do not touch your Amazon Fire TV Devices or any wires connected to your Amazon Fire TV Devices during a lightning storm.
  • Small parts contained in your device and its accessories may present a choking hazard to small children.
  • The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that television should be avoided for infants and children under age 2. Using Your Amazon Fire TV Devices Around Other Electronic Devices

Amazon Fire TV Devices generate, use, and can radiate radio frequency (RF) energy and, if not used in accordance with its instructions, may cause interference to radio communications and electronic equipment. External RF signals may affect improperly installed or inadequately shielded electronic operating systems, entertainment systems, and personal medical devices. While most modern electronic equipment is shielded from external RF signals, if in doubt, check with the manufacturer. For personal medical devices (such as pacemakers and hearing aids), consult with your physician or the manufacturer to determine if they are adequately shielded from external RF signals.

There are some places where RF signals could constitute a hazard, such as health care facilities, and construction sites. If you are not sure, look around for signs indicating that two-way radios or mobile phones should be turned off.

The devices DV83YW, LY73PR, CL1130 and LDC9WZ, W87CUN should be installed and operated with at least 20cm between the radiator and your body.

FCC Compliance Statement (USA)

The Amazon Fire TV Devices and related accessories like the remote and the adapter (the “Products”) comply with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation of each Product is subject to the following two conditions: (1) such Product may not cause harmful interference, and (2) such Product must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

Note: The Products have been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device or external switching power supply, pursuant to part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference in a residential installation. The Products generate, use and can radiate radio frequency energy and, if not installed and used in accordance with the instructions, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. However, there is no guarantee that interference will not occur in a particular installation. If a Product does cause harmful interference to radio or television reception, which can be determined by unplugging and plugging in the Product, the user is encouraged to try to correct the interference by one or more of the following measures:

  • Reorient or relocate the receiving antenna.
  • Increase the separation between the equipment and receiver.
  • Connect the equipment into an outlet on a circuit different from that to which the receiver is connected.
  • Consult the dealer or an experienced radio/TV technician for help. Changes or modifications to a Product by the user that are not expressly approved by the party responsible for compliance could make the Product no longer comply with the FCC Rules.

The Products meet the FCC Radio Frequency Emission Guidelines and are certified with the FCC. Information on these Products is on file with the FCC and can be found by inputting such Product’s FCC ID (which can be found on the back of the Amazon Fire TV Device or in the battery compartment of the remote) into the FCC ID Search form available at transition.fcc.gov/oet/ea/fccid.

Information Regarding Exposure to Radio Frequency Energy

The output power of the radio technology used in the Products is below the radio frequency exposure limits set by the FCC. Nevertheless, it is advised to use the Products in such a manner that minimizes the potential for human contact during normal operation.

RF Exposure Compliance

In order to protect human health, these devices meet the thresholds for exposure of the general public to electromagnetic fields according to Council Recommendation 1999/519/EC. DV83YW, LY73PR, CL1130, LDC9WZ, and W87CUN should be installed and operated with a minimum distance of 20 cm between the radiator and your body.

WATCH FOR SMALL PARTS Your device, its accessories, and batteries may present a choking hazard to small children. Keep them out of reach of small children.

WARNING: Never place a television set in an unstable location. A television set may fall, causing serious personal injury or death. Many injuries, particularly to children, can be avoided by taking simple precautions such as:

  • Only using furniture that can safely support the television set.
  • Routing cords and cables connected to the television so they cannot be tripped over, pulled, or grabbed.
  • Not placing the television set on tall furniture (for example, cupboards or bookcases) without anchoring both the furniture and television set to a suitable support.
  • Not placing the television set on cloth or other materials that may be located between the television set and supporting furniture.
  • Educating children about the dangers of climbing on furniture to reach the television set or its controls. If you are keeping and relocating an existing television set, the same considerations as above should be applied.
  • Not placing items that might tempt children to climb, such as toys and remote controls, on top of the television set and supporting furniture Please refer to the information on the exterior back enclosure for electrical and safety information before installing or operating the device.

Television:

  • Do not install this device in a confined or built-in space such as a bookcase or similar unit unless proper ventilation is provided. The ventilation should not be impeded by covering the ventilation openings with items such as newspaper, tablecloths, curtains, etc. Keep a minimum distance of 10 cm around all edges of the display for sufficient ventilation.
  • To reduce the risk of fire or electric shock, do not expose this device to rain or moisture. The device should not be exposed to dripping or splashing and objects filled with liquids, such as vases, should not be placed on the device.
  • Do not block or cover the ventilation openings on the back cover.
  • Do not push objects of any kind into this unit through the cabinet slots as they could touch the current carrying parts or short-circuit parts, resulting in fire, electric shock, or damage to the unit.
  • Do not touch the screen surface with fingers as this may scratch or mar the TV screen.
  • Do not impact the TV screen with hard pressure as this may damage the TV screen severely.
  • Refer all servicing to qualified service personnel. Servicing is required when the device has been damaged in any way, such as power-supply cord or plug is damaged, liquid has been spilled or objects have fallen into the device, the device has been exposed to rain or moisture, does not operate normally, or has been dropped.
  • Power cord and Plug:
  • To disconnect your TV from power, you must unplug the power cord from the electrical outlet. The power cord must remain readily operable.
  • Unplug the TV set under the following conditions:
    • If the set will not be used for a long period of time.
    • If the power cord or the power outlet/plug is damaged.
    • If the TV, power cord, or power outlet/plug has been exposed to liquid or moisture.
    • If the set has been subject to impact, dropped, or otherwise damaged.
    • When not in use and during movement, please take care of the power cordset, e.g. tie up the power cordset with cable tie. It should be free from sharp edges and the like that can cause abrasion of the power cordset. When put into use again, make sure the power cordset is not damaged.
    • Unplug this product during lightning storms.
  • Do not allow anything to rest on or roll over the power cord and the signal cable.
  • Protect the power cord and the signal cable from being trampled.
  • Do not overload the power cord or the power outlet beyond their capacity, since this can result in fire or electric shock.
  • Do not expose the power cord and the signal cable to moisture.
  • Only use the provided plug with an appropriate outlet. If the provided plug does not fit into your outlet, do not force the plug into the outlet.
  • Protect the power cord from being walked on or pinched. Particularly near the plug and the point where it exits the product.
  • Be sure to plug in the power cord until it is firmly seated. When unplugging the power cord from the outlet, always pull on the power cord’s plug. Never unplug it by pulling on the power cord. Do not touch the power cord with wet hands.
  • Only use attachments/accessories included with the device.
BATTERY SAFETY

The battery (battery or batteries or battery pack) should not be exposed to excessive heat such as sunshine, fire or the like.

CAUTION: There is a danger of an explosion if you replace the batteries used in the remote with the wrong type of battery. Replace only with the same or equivalent type.

This device uses batteries. There may be environmental regulations that require you to dispose of these batteries properly. Please contact your local authorities for disposal or recycling information.

Hanging the TV Set on the Wall

WARNING: If you mount this TV on a wall, follow the instructions exactly as set out in the instructions provided with the wall mount. If it is not correctly mounted, the TV may slide or fall and cause serious injury to a child or adult and serious damage to the TV.

This operation requires two people.

To ensure a safe installation, observe the following safety notes:

  • Do not install while your TV set is turned on. This may result in personal injury from electric shock.
  • Check that the wall can support the weight of the TV set and wall mount assembly.
  • Follow the mounting instructions provided with the wall mount (sold separately).
  • The TV set must be installed on a vertical wall.
  • Make sure to use only screws suitable for the material of the wall.
  • Make sure that the TV set cables are placed so that there is not danger of tripping over them.
  • Your TV has four VESA mounting holes on the back. If you attach a wall-mount bracket to the back of your TV, the bracket must be securely attached using all four holes. If you do not use all four mounting holes, your TV may fall and cause property damage or personal injury. See the documentation that came with your wall mount for complete mounting instructions.
Securing Your TV

WARNING: TV sets that are inappropriately situated on dressers, bookcases, shelves, desks, speakers, chests, carts, etc. may fall over, resulting in injury.

  • Never allow children to climb on or play on the TV set or the furniture on which the TV set is placed.
  • Never place the TV set on furniture that can easily be used as steps, such as a chest of drawers.
  • Always install the TV set where it cannot be pushed, pulled over, or knocked down.
  • Always route power cords and cables connected to the TV set so that they cannot be tripped over, pulled, or grabbed. When a cart is used, use caution when moving the cart/device combination to avoid injury from tip-over.

Maintaining Your Amazon Ember Artline Series

Do not use your Amazon Ember or accessories near sinks or other wet locations. Take care not to spill any food or liquid on your devices and do not put any object filled with a liquid, such as a vase, on or near your devices. If your Amazon Ember does get wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device to dry completely before plugging it in again. If your Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote does get wet, use rubber gloves to remove the batteries and wait for the remote to dry completely before re-inserting the batteries. Do not attempt to dry your devices with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or hair dryer. Do not drop, throw, disassemble, crush, bend, puncture, or paint your Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote

Use Environment:

  • Keep the set away from direct sunlight.

  • Do not use the device in a location with heavy dust. Accumulated dust can cause an electric shock, an electric leakage, or a fire by causing the power cord to generate sparks and heat or by causing insulation to deteriorate.

  • Do not install near any heat sources such as radiators, heat registers, stoves, or other apparatus (including amplifiers) that produce heat.

  • Do not use or install the device in a location where exposure to liquids or moisture may results, such as in a bathroom or near a kitchen sink or other sources of running water. Cleaning:

  • To clean the device, unplug the power cord and dust the device by wiping the screen and the cabinet with a soft, clean cloth or some special liquid cleaner.

  • Do not apply excessive force to the screen when cleaning.

  • Do not use water or other chemical cleaner to clean the screen as this may damage the surface of the TV screen.

  • Do not spray water or any liquid directly onto the TV. Any liquid that goes into the TV may case a failure, fire, or electric shock. IMPORTANT PRODUCT INFORMATION

Use Responsibly. Read all instructions and safety information before use.

FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

STRANGULATION HAZARD

Children have strangled in cords. Keep cords out of reach of children.

Battery Safety

This product contains alkaline batteries. The remote requires batteries for use. Only use new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA-sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. Do not open, disassemble, puncture, cut, bend, shred or heat the batteries and do not allow metal objects to touch the battery terminals on the remote as they can become hot and cause burns. Remove all batteries if they are worn out or before storing your remote for an extended period of time. Dispose of all batteries in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and do not dispose of batteries by throwing them into a fire. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

Maintaining Your Fire TV Cube

Do not use your Fire TV Cube or accessories (collectively referred to as “the device” or “devices”) near sinks or other wet locations. Take care not to spill any food or liquid on your devices and do not put any object filled with a liquid, such as a vase, on or near your devices. If your Fire TV Cube does get wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device to dry completely before plugging it in again. If your Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote does get wet, use rubber gloves to remove the batteries and wait for the remote to dry completely before re-inserting the batteries. Do not attempt to dry your devices with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or hair dryer. Do not drop, throw, disassemble, crush, bend, puncture, or paint your Amazon Fire TV Alexa Voice Remote.

Only handle your devices with clean hands. Clean your devices only with a soft cloth that is slightly damp with water and a touch of rubbing alcohol; be careful not to wipe it with anything abrasive or to use any harsh chemicals. Don’t expose your devices to steam or extreme heat or cold. For example, do not install your device near any heat sources such as space heaters, heater vents, radiators, stoves, or other things that produce heat. Store your Alexa Voice Remote and Fire TV Cube in cool, dust-free areas out of direct sunlight.

Use of third-party accessories may impact your devices’ performance. In limited circumstances, use of third party accessories may void your devices’ limited warranty. Do not expose your device or adapter to liquids. If your device or adapter gets wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device and adapter to dry completely before plugging them in again. Do not attempt to dry your device or adapter with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or a hair dryer. If the device or adapter appear damaged, discontinue use immediately. Use only accessories supplied with the device to power your device. To avoid risk of electric shock, do not touch your device or any wires connected to your device during a lightning storm. Do not force the power adapter into a power outlet. If the power adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately. Do not plug multiple electric devices into the same wall socket. Overloading a socket can cause it to overheat and may result in a fire.

If you wish to turn off your Fire TV Cube, press and hold the “action” button for at least 10 seconds. To turn your Fire TV Cube back on, press the “action” button. If you wish to stop power from flowing into your device, unplug the power adapter.

Other Safety Considerations

  • A small percentage of people may be susceptible to blackouts or seizures (even if they have never had one before) when exposed to flashing lights or light patterns, such as when watching video or playing games.   • Engaging in repetitive motions such as pressing buttons or playing some games may cause you to experience occasional discomfort in your hands, arms, shoulders, neck, or other parts of your body.
  • Discontinue use of your device and consult a physician if you experience headaches, blackouts, seizures, convulsion, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, involuntary movement, disorientation, or other discomfort.   • Handle your device and its accessories with care. Your device or its accessories may have pointed edges which can lead to scratches, cuts, or other physical injury.
  • Small parts contained in your device and its accessories may present a choking hazard to small children.
  • The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that television should be avoided for infants and children under age 2.
  • Your device is shipped with an AC adapter. Your Fire TV Cube device should only be powered using the AC adapter included with the device.
  • If the adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately.

  • Your Fire TV Cube may get hot during normal use. To reduce the effect of the warming, place your Fire TV Cube on a heat resistant surface. If you find the device has become hot to the touch, unplug power and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.
  • Install your power adapter into an easily accessible socket-outlet located near the equipment that will be plugged into, or powered by, the adapter.
  • When this device is plugged into an electrical socket-outlet, unplugging this device will disconnect it from the AC mains supply. Only plug this device into an easily accessible socket-outlet. WARNING: Never place a television set in an unstable location. A television set may fall, causing serious personal injury or death. Many injuries, particularly to children, can be avoided by taking simple precautions such as:

  • Only using furniture that can safely support the television set.

  • Routing cords and cables connected to the television so they cannot be tripped over, pulled, or grabbed.

  • Not placing the television set on tall furniture (for example, cupboards or bookcases) without anchoring both the furniture and television set to a suitable support.

  • Not placing the television set on cloth or other materials that may be located between the television set and supporting furniture.

Television:

  • Do not install this device in a confined or built-in space such as a book case or similar unit unless proper ventilation is provided. The ventilation should not be impeded by covering the ventilation openings with items such as newspaper, table-cloths, curtains, etc. Keep a minimum distance of 10 cm around all edges of the display for sufficient ventilation.

  • To reduce the risk of fire or electric shock, do not expose this device to rain or moisture. The device should not be exposed to dripping or splashing and objects filled with liquids, such as vases, should not be placed on the device.

  • Do not block or cover the ventilation openings on the back cover.

  • Do not push objects of any kind into this unit through the cabinet slots as they could touch the current carrying parts or short-circuit parts, resulting in fire, electric shock, or damage to the unit.

  • Do not touch the screen surface with fingers as this may scratch or mar the TV screen.

  • Do not impact the TV screen with hard pressure as this may damage the TV screen severely.

  • Refer all servicing to qualified service personnel. Servicing is required when the device has been damaged in any way, such as power-supply cord or plug is damaged, liquid has been spilled or objects have fallen into the device, the device has been exposed to rain or moisture, does not operate normally, or has been dropped. Power cord and Plug:

  • To disconnect your TV from power, you must unplug the power cord from the electrical outlet. The power cord must remain readily operable.

  • Unplug the TV set under the following conditions:

    • If the set will not be used for a long period of time.
    • If the power cord or the power outlet/plug is damaged.
    • If the TV, power cord, or power outlet/plug has been exposed to liquid or moisture.
    • If the set has been subject to impact, dropped, or otherwise damaged.
    • When not in use and during movement, please take care of the power cordset, e.g. tie up the power cordset with cable tie. It should be free from sharp edges and the like that can cause abrasion of the power cordset. When put into use again, make sure the power cordset is not damaged.
    • Unplug this product during lightning storms.

  • Do not allow anything to rest on or roll over the power cord and the signal cable.

  • Protect the power cord and the signal cable from being trampled.

  • Do not overload the power cord or the power outlet beyond their capacity, since this can result in fire or electric shock.

  • Do not expose the power cord and the signal cable to moisture.

  • Only use the provided plug with an appropriate outlet. If the provided plug does not fit into your outlet, do not force the plug into the outlet.

  • Protect the power cord from being walked on or pinched. Particularly near the plug and the point where it exits the product.

  • Be sure to plug in the power cord until it is firmly seated. When unplugging the power cord from the outlet, always pull on the power cord’s plug. Never unplug it by pulling on the power cord. Do not touch the power cord with wet hands.

  • Only use attachments/accessories included with the device. BATTERY SAFETY

This device contains alkaline batteries. The remote requires batteries for use. Only use new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA-sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. Do not open, disassemble, puncture, cut, bend, shred or heat the batteries and do not allow metal objects to touch the battery terminals on the remote as they can become hot and cause burns. Remove all batteries if they are worn out or before storing your remote for an extended period of time. Dispose of all batteries in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and do not dispose of batteries by throwing them into a fire. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

WARNING: Never place a television set in an unstable location. A television set may fall, causing serious personal injury or death. Many injuries, particularly to children, can be avoided by taking simple precautions such as:

  • Only using furniture that can safely support the television set.
  • Routing cords and cables connected to the television so they cannot be tripped over, pulled, or grabbed.
  • Not placing the television set on tall furniture (for example, cupboards or bookcases) without anchoring both the furniture and television set to a suitable support.
  • Not placing the television set on cloth or other materials that may be located between the television set and supporting furniture.
  • Educating children about the dangers of climbing on furniture to reach the television set or its controls. If you are keeping and relocating an existing television set, the same considerations as above should be applied.

Television:

  • Do not install this device in a confined or built-in space such as a book case or similar unit unless proper ventilation is provided. The ventilation should not be impeded by covering the ventilation openings with items such as newspaper, table-cloths, curtains, etc. Keep a minimum distance of 10 cm around all edges of the display for sufficient ventilation.

  • To reduce the risk of fire or electric shock, do not expose this device to rain or moisture. The device should not be exposed to dripping or splashing and objects filled with liquids, such as vases, should not be placed on the device.

  • Do not push objects of any kind into this unit through the cabinet slots as they could touch the current carrying parts or short-circuit parts, resulting in fire, electric shock, or damage to the unit.

  • Do not impact the TV screen with hard pressure as this may damage the TV screen severely.

  • To disconnect your TV from power, you must unplug the power cord from the electrical outlet. The power cord must remain readily operable.

  • Unplug the TV set under the following conditions:

    • If the set will not be used for a long period of time.
    • If the power cord or the power outlet/plug is damaged.
    • If the TV, power cord, or power outlet/plug has been exposed to liquid or moisture.
    • If the set has been subject to impact, dropped, or otherwise damaged.
    • When not in use and during movement, please take care of the power cordset, e.g. tie up the power cordset with cable tie. It should be free from sharp edges and the like that can cause abrasion of the power cordset. When put into use again, make sure the power cordset is not damaged.
    • Unplug this product during lightning storms.

  • Do not allow anything to rest on or roll over the power cord and the signal cable.

  • Protect the power cord and the signal cable from being trampled.

  • Do not overload the power cord or the power outlet beyond their capacity, since this can result in fire or electric shock.

  • Do not expose the power cord and the signal cable to moisture.

  • Only use the provided plug with an appropriate outlet. If the provided plug does not fit into your outlet, do not force the plug into the outlet.

  • Protect the power cord from being walked on or pinched. Particularly near the plug and the point where it exits the product.

  • Be sure to plug in the power cord until it is firmly seated. When unplugging the power cord from the outlet, always pull on the power cord’s plug. Never unplug it by pulling on the power cord. Do not touch the power cord with wet hands.

  • Only use attachments/accessories included with the device.

Safety and Compliance Information for Fire TV Stick 4K

IMPORTANT PRODUCT INFORMATION

Safety and Compliance Information

READ ALL SAFETY INFORMATION BEFORE USING THE DEVICE. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

Watch for Small Parts

Your device, its accessories, and batteries may present a choking hazard to small children. Keep them out of reach of small children.

BATTERY SAFETY

HANDLE WITH CARE. This product contains alkaline batteries. The remote requires batteries for use. Only use new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA-sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. Do not open, disassemble, puncture, cut, bend, shred, or heat the batteries and do not allow metal objects to touch the battery terminals on the remote as they can become hot and cause burns. Remove all batteries if they are worn out or before storing your remote for an extended period of time. Dispose of all batteries in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and do not dispose of batteries by throwing them into a fire. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

Maintaining Your Fire TV Stick 4K

Refer to the Safety & Compliance section on amazon.com for additional information.

Do not expose your device or adapter to liquids. If your device or adapter gets wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device and adapter to dry completely before plugging them in again. Do not attempt to dry your device or adapter with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or a hair dryer. If the device or adapter appear damaged, discontinue use immediately. Use only accessories supplied with the device to power your device.

Only handle your devices with clean hands. Clean your devices only with a soft cloth that is slightly damp with water and a touch of rubbing alcohol; be careful not to wipe it with anything abrasive or to use any harsh chemicals. Don’t expose your devices to steam or extreme heat or cold. For example, do not install your device near any heat sources such as space heaters, heater vents, radiators, stoves, or other things that produce heat. Store your Fire TV Stick 4K in cool, dust-free areas out of direct sunlight.

Use of third-party accessories may impact your devices’ performance. In limited circumstances, use of third-party accessories may void your devices’ limited warranty. In addition, use of incompatible third-party accessories may lead to damage to device or the accessory. Read all safety instructions for any accessories before using with your Fire TV Stick 4K.

Your Fire TV Stick 4K may get hot during normal use. To reduce the effect of the warming, place your Fire TV Stick 4K on a heat resistant surface. If you find the device has become hot to the touch, unplug power and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.

Servicing Your Device

If your device needs service, please contact Amazon Customer Support. Contact details can be found at amazon.com.

Faulty service may void the warranty.

Other Safety Considerations

  • A small percentage of people may be susceptible to blackouts or seizures (even if they have never had one before) when exposed to flashing lights or light patterns, such as when watching video or playing games. If you have experienced seizures or blackouts or have a family history of such occurrences, you should consult a doctor before watching videos or playing games.
  • Engaging in repetitive motions such as pressing buttons or playing some games may cause you to experience occasional discomfort in your hands, arms, shoulders, neck, or other parts of your body.
  • Discontinue use of your device and consult a physician if you experience headaches, blackouts, seizures, convulsion, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, involuntary movement, disorientation, or other discomfort. To reduce risk of these symptoms, avoid prolonged use, watch your television from a far distance and in a well-lit room, and take frequent breaks.
  • Handle your device and its accessories with care. Your device and its accessories may have pointed edges which can lead to scratches, cuts, or other physical injury.
  • Do not touch your Fire TV Stick 4K or any wires connected to your Fire TV Stick 4K during a lightning storm.
  • The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that television should be avoided for infants and children under 2 years of age.
  • Your device is shipped with an AC adapter. Your device should only be powered using the AC adapter and USB cable included with the device.
  • Do not expose adapter or cable to liquids.
  • If the adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately.
  • Power adapter designed only for use with Fire TV Stick 4K.

Safety and Compliance Information for Fire TV Stick HD

Safety Information

Use Responsibly. Read all instructions and safety information before use.

FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

Watch for Small Parts

Your device, its accessories, and batteries may present a choking hazard to small children. Keep them out of reach of small children.

Maintaining Your Fire TV Stick HD

Do not use your Fire TV Stick HD or Alexa Voice Remote (collectively referred to as “device” or “devices”) near sinks or other wet locations. Take care not to spill any food or liquid on your devices and do not put any object filled with a liquid, such as a vase, on or near your devices. If your Fire TV Stick HD does get wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device to dry completely before plugging it in again. If your Alexa Voice Remote does get wet, use rubber gloves to remove the batteries and wait for the remote to dry completely before re-inserting the batteries. Do not attempt to dry your devices with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or hair dryer. Do not drop, throw, disassemble, crush, bend, puncture, or paint your Alexa Voice Remote.

Only handle your devices with clean hands. Clean your devices only with a soft cloth that is slightly damp with water and a touch of rubbing alcohol; be careful not to wipe it with anything abrasive or to use any harsh chemicals. Don’t expose your devices to steam, extreme heat or cold. For example, do not install your device near any heat sources such as space heaters, heater vents, radiators, stoves, or other things that produce heat. Store devices in a cool, dust-free areas out of direct sunlight.

Use of third party accessories may impact your devices’ performance. In limited circumstances, use of third party accessories may void your devices’ limited warranty. In addition, use of incompatible third-party accessories may lead to damage to device or the accessory. Read all safety instructions for any accessories before using with your Fire TV Stick HD.

Do not expose your device or adapter to liquids. If your device or adapter gets wet, carefully unplug all cables without getting your hands wet and wait for the device and adapter to dry completely before plugging them in again. Do not attempt to dry your device or adapter with an external heat source, such as a microwave oven or a hair dryer. If the device or adapter appear damaged, discontinue use immediately. Use only accessories supplied with the device to power your device. To avoid risk of electric shock, do not touch your device or any wires connected to your device during a lightning storm.

Your Fire TV Stick HD does not have an on/off button. If you wish to stop power from flowing into your Fire TV Stick HD, unplug the power adapter. Only use the included power adapter with your device. Do not force the power adapter into a power outlet. If the power adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately. Do not plug multiple electric devices into the same wall socket. Overloading a socket can cause it to overheat and may result in a fire. Your device may get hot during normal use. If you find the Fire TV Stick HD has become hot to the touch, unplug it from the power supply and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.

Battery Safety

This product contains alkaline batteries. The remote for your Fire TV Stick HD requires batteries for use. Only use new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. Do not open, disassemble, puncture, cut, bend, shred or heat the batteries and do not allow metal objects to touch the battery terminals on the remote as they can become hot and cause burns. Remove all batteries if they are worn out or before storing your remote for an extended period of time. Dispose of all batteries in accordance with applicable laws and regulations and do not dispose of batteries by throwing them into a fire. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

Servicing Your Device

If your device needs service, please contact Amazon Customer Support. Contact details can be found at www.amazon.com/devicesupport.

Faulty service may void the warranty.

Other Safety Considerations

  • A small percentage of people may be susceptible to blackouts or seizures (even if they have never had one before) when exposed to flashing lights or light patterns, such as when watching video or playing games. If you have experienced seizures or blackouts or have a family history of such occurrences, you should consult a doctor before watching videos or playing games.
  • Engaging in repetitive motions such as pressing buttons or playing some games may cause you to experience occasional discomfort in your hands, arms, shoulders, neck, or other parts of your body.
  • Discontinue use of your device and consult a physician if you experience headaches, blackouts, seizures, convulsion, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, involuntary movement, disorientation, or other discomfort. To reduce risk of these symptoms avoid prolonged use, watch your television from a far distance and in a well-lit room, and take frequent breaks.
  • Handle your device and its accessories with care. Your device and its accessories may have pointed edges which can lead to scratches, cuts, or other physical injury.
  • Small parts contained in your device and its accessories may present a choking hazard to small children.
  • The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that television should be avoided for infants and children under 2 years of age.
  • Your device is shipped with an AC adapter. Your device should only be powered using the AC adapter and USB cable included with the device.
  • Do not touch your Fire TV Stick HD or any wires connected to your Fire TV Stick HD during a lightning storm.
  • Do not expose adapter or cable to liquids.
  • If the adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately.
  • Power adapter designed only for use with Fire TV Stick HD.
  • Your Fire TV Stick HD may get hot during normal use. To reduce the effect of the warming, place your Fire TV Stick HD on a heat resistant surface. If you find the device has become hot to the touch, unplug power and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.
  • Install your power adapter into an easily accessible socket-outlet located near the equipment that will be plugged into or powered by the adapter. Using Your Fire TV Stick HD and Alexa Voice Remote Around Other Electronic Devices

The Fire TV Stick HD and Alexa Voice Remote generate, use, and can radiate radio frequency (RF) energy and, if not used in accordance with its instructions, may cause interference to radio communications and electronic equipment. External RF signals may affect improperly installed or inadequately shielded electronic operating systems, entertainment systems, and personal medical devices. While most modern electronic equipment is shielded from external RF signals, if in doubt, check with the manufacturer. For personal medical devices (such as pacemakers and hearing aids), consult with your physician or the manufacturer to determine if they are adequately shielded from external RF signals.

FCC Compliance Statement

The device and its related accessories like the adapter (the “Products”) comply with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation is subject to the following two conditions: (1) This device may not cause harmful interference, and (2) This device must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

NOTE: This product has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device, pursuant to part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference in a residential installation. This equipment generates, uses and can radiate radio frequency energy and, if not installed and used in accordance with the instructions, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. However, there is no guarantee that interference will not occur in a particular installation. If this equipment does cause harmful interference to radio or television reception, which can be determined by turning the equipment off and on, the user is encouraged to try to correct the interference by one or more of the following measures:

  • Reorient or relocate the receiving antenna.
  • Increase the separation between the equipment and receiver.
  • Connect the equipment to an outlet on a circuit different from that to which the receiver is connected.
  • Consult the dealer or an experienced radio/TV technician for help. Pursuant to Section 15.21 of the FCC rules, changes or modifications to a Product by the user that are not expressly approved by the party responsible for compliance could void the user’s authority to operate the equipment.

The device meets the FCC Radio Frequency Emission Guidelines. Information on the Product is on file with the FCC and can be found by inputting such Product’s FCC ID (which can be found on the device) into the FCC ID Search form available at transition.fcc.gov/oet/ea/fccid.

The party responsible for FCC compliance is Amazon.com Services LLC, 410 Terry Ave North, Seattle, WA 98109 USA. If you wish to contact Amazon visit www.amazon.com/devicesupport, select United States, click Help and Troubleshooting, then scroll to the bottom of the page and under the Talk to an Associate option, click on Contact Us.

  • Device Name: Fire TV Stick HD and Alexa Voice Remote
  • Model (Fire TV Stick HD): S3L46N
  • Model (Alexa Voice Remote): H69A73, E4GE9R, PA38CA, and PA2M36 Information Regarding Exposure to Radio Frequency Energy

The output power of the radio technology used in the Products is below the radio frequency exposure limits set by the FCC. This device should be installed and operated with a minimum distance of 20 cm between the radiator and your body.

Recycling Your Device Properly

In some areas, the disposal of certain electronic devices and waste batteries is regulated. Make sure you dispose of or recycle your device in accordance with your local laws and regulations. For information about recycling devices, go to www.amazon.com/devicesupport.

How to Set Up Amazon Ember 2-Series & 4-Series (2025)

Set up and register your device to use Alexa, access the full Amazon Appstore, and receive Fire TV software updates.

Note: Due to a recent name update from the Fire TV 4-Series to the Amazon Ember 4-Series, packaging, including the product name, may vary. Device functionality remains the same.

Note: Due to a recent name update from the Fire TV 2-Series to the Amazon Ember 2-Series, packaging, including the product name, may vary. Device functionality remains the same.

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • The Amazon Ember 2-Series or Amazon Ember 4-Series TV and in-box accessories
    • Alexa Voice Remote, power cord, AAA batteries for the remote, 2 TV stand legs, and 4 TV stand screws
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password
    • Don’t have an account? Visit this page: Create an Amazon Account
    • If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password
  • Philips screwdriver and scissors
  • TV wall mounts (sold separately) if you decide to mount the TV on a wall Back to top
Unpack Your TV

To unpack your TV:

  • Carefully unpack the TV and all included accessories from the box. Make sure you remove all parts and accessories before disposing of the box.
  • Lay your TV on a flat surface with the plastic wrap still on the TV.
  • Cut the plastic wrap off of the TV. Back to top
Install Your TV

Important:

  • The installation process requires two people.

  • Make sure your TV is powered off before installation. Installing while your TV is on may put you at risk of electric shock.

  • Make sure to place your TV on a stable surface. An unstable location risks your TV sliding or falling, potentially causing serious injury or damage. To install the TV stand:

  • Screw both TV stand legs into the bottom of the TV. The legs are interchangeable and can be installed on either side. To mount your TV on the wall:

  • Check that the wall can support the weight of the TV set and wall mount assembly.

  • Compatible VESA wall mount patterns:

    • Amazon Ember TV 2-Series (32”, 40”): 100 mm (w) x 100 mm (h)
    • Amazon Ember TV 4-Series (43”, 50”, 55”): 300 mm (w) x 300 mm (h)

  • Compatible screws: Type M6, 12 mm length

  • Follow the mounting instructions provided with the wall mount.

  • Note: Follow the mounting instructions exactly as provided. This will help you avoid any damage or serious injury during the mounting process.

  • Make sure to install the TV on a vertical wall.

  • Only use screws that are suitable for the wall’s material.

  • Make sure no one can trip over the TV cables. Follow these tips to place your TV:

  • Don’t place your TV on an unstable surface.

  • Place your TV somewhere that allows good ventilation.

  • Don’t use your TV near damp or cold areas.

  • Keep your TV away from direct sunlight to protect the TV from overheating.

  • Keep liquids and liquid-filled containers away from your TV. Back to top

Control Buttons and Ports

The Amazon Ember 2-Series and Amazon Ember 4-Series TV has the following buttons, indicators and ports located on the front and back of the device.

On the front of the device:

  • Power button (bottom of the TV) On the back of the device:

  • Power port

  • 4 VESA mount holes and preinstalled screws

  • Optical audio output (S/PDIF) port

  • Ethernet port

  • USB-A ports

  • Antenna/Cable port

  • HDMI 2.1 eARC port

  • HDMI 2.0 port

    • Amazon Ember 2-Series has one HDMI 2.0 port
    • Amzon Ember 4-Series has three HDMI 2.0 ports

  • IR Emitter port

  • Audio out/headphone port Back to top

How to Set Up Your Device
  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Plug in the power cord first into your TV’s power (AC-in) port, and then plug the other end into a power outlet.
  • Note: If the power cord is damaged, don’t connect it to an outlet, as there is a risk of electric shock.
  • (Optional) Connect an external antenna to your TV’s antenna port to watch broadcast TV.
  • Press the Power button on your remote or your TV.
  • Your Fire TV remote should already be paired with your Fire TV.
  • Note: If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • If connecting to a Wi-Fi network, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • If connecting to a router or modem:
    • Connect one end of an Ethernet cable (sold separately) to your TV.
    • Connect the other end to your modem or router.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup. Note: When turning off your TV with the power button on your remote or TV, the device enters standby mode. To completely shut down your TV, unplug the power cord from the outlet.

Back to top

Remote Overview

Your device comes with a remote that you can use to navigate your TV. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content. Use the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to quickly navigate and select apps.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.

Note: For best performance, always replace both dead batteries with new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2V NiMH rechargeable AAA batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

For a text description of the button layout, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced?

Note: Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

Back to top

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try the following suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to the Forgot Your Password page.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds). Visit the Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, visit the Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi During Setup page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If you can’t download apps or games, add a default payment method. Visit the Your Payments page.
  • If your TV has video but no sound, visit the Fire TV Smart TV Has Video but No Audio page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If your TV has no video or sound, visit the Fire TV Smart TV Won’t Turn On page to find more troubleshooting information. Back to top
Accessibility Features on Fire TV

Fire TV devices have a set of features designed to enhance the viewing experience for customers with disabilities. These features include things like closed captions, a screen reader, screen magnifier, and audio descriptions. To learn more, go to Accessibility Features for Fire TV.

Back to top

You’re Set Up, What’s Next?

Once you’ve finished setting up your device, you can explore more features to improve your Fire TV experience. To learn more, go to:

  • Find and download your favorite apps using voice search on your remote
  • Set up equipment control so your Alexa Voice Remote can control the TV’s power and volume Back to top
