Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • The Amazon Ember Omni Mini-LED TV and in-box accessories
    • Alexa Voice Remote, power cord, AAA batteries for the remote, 2 TV stand legs, and 4 TV stand screws
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password
    • Don’t have an account? Visit this page: Create an Amazon Account
    • If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password
  • TV wall mounts (sold separately) if you decide to mount the TV on a wall Back to top
Unpack and Install Your TV

To install the TV stand:

  • Carefully unpack the TV and all included accessories from the box.
  • Note: Make sure you remove all parts and accessories before disposing of the box.
  • Lay your TV on a flat surface with the plastic wrap still on the TV.
  • Cut the plastic wrap off of the TV.
  • Screw both TV stand legs into the bottom of the TV. Use the included TV stand screws and a Phillips screwdriver.
  • Note: Do not use an electric drill to prevent stripping the screw holes. To mount your TV on the wall:

Follow the instructions exactly as set out in the instructions provided with the wall mount (sold separately). This will help you avoid any damage or serious injury during the mounting process. This process requires two people.

  • Carefully unpack the TV and all included accessories from the box.
  • Note: Make sure you remove all parts and accessories before disposing of the box.
  • Lay your TV on a flat surface with the plastic wrap still on the TV.
  • Cut the plastic wrap off of the TV.
  • Compatible VESA wall mount patterns:
    • 55”, 65”, 75” TVs: 400 mm (w) x 300 mm (h)
    • 85” TVs: 500 mm (w) x 200 mm (h)
  • Use the pre-installed screws at the back of the TV to attach a mount:
    • 55”, 65”, 75” TVs: Type M6 x 15 mm screws
    • 85” TV: 500 mm (w) x 200 mm (h) Note: If the mount doesn’t lay flat against the TV, screw in the included mounting spacers first.

Back to top

Control Buttons and Ports

The Amazon Ember Omni Mini-LED TV has the following buttons, indicators and ports located on the front, and on the back of the device:

On the front of the device:

  • Microphones on/off button

  • Microphones

  • Power button

  • Light bar

  • LED Indicators On the back of the device:

  • Power port

  • 4 VESA mount holes and preinstalled screws

  • Optical audio output (S/PDIF) port

  • Ethernet port

  • USB-A ports

  • Antenna/Cable port

  • HDMI 2.1 eARC port

  • HDMI 2.1 port

  • HDMI 2.0 port

  • IR Emitter port

  • Audio out/headphone port Back to top

How to Set Up Your Device

Video guide to set up your device

  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Plug in the power cord into your TV’s power port, then plug the other end into a power outlet.
  • Press the Power button on your remote or TV.
  • Your Fire TV remote should already be paired with your Fire TV.
  • Note: If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • If connecting to a Wi-Fi network, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • If connecting to a router or modem:
    • Connect one end of an Ethernet cable (sold separately) to your TV.
    • Connect the other end to your modem or router.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup. Back to top
Remote Overview

Your device comes with the remote that you can use to browse your Fire TV. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content. Use the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to navigate quickly to select apps.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.

Note: For best performance, always replace dead batteries with new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2V NiMH rechargeable AAA batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

For a text description of the button layout, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced?

Note: Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

Back to top

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try the following suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to the Forgot Your Password page.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds). Visit the Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, visit the Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi During Setup page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If you can’t download apps or games, add a default payment method. Visit the Your Payments page. Back to top
Privacy & Support

You can take control of your privacy settings. Toggle the microphone on/off switch on your device to deactivate microphones whenever you need. In the Alexa app, you have the ability to access, listen to, or delete any voice recordings associated with your account at any time.

For additional options to customize your privacy, visit Alexa Privacy Hub page.

Back to top

Accessibility Features on Fire TV

Fire TV devices have a set of features designed to enhance the viewing experience for customers with disabilities. These features include things like closed captions, a screen reader, screen magnifier, and audio descriptions. To learn more, go to the Accessibility Features for Fire TV page.

Back to top

You’re Set Up, What’s Next?

Once you’ve finished setting up your device, you can explore more features to improve your Fire TV experience. To learn more, go to:

  • Find and download your favorite apps using voice search on your remote
  • Set up equipment control so your Alexa Voice Remote can control the TV’s power and volume Back to top

How to Set Up Fire TV Soundbar

How to Set Up Fire TV Soundbar

Connect the Fire TV Soundbar to an HDMI port on your TV that supports ARC or eARC.

  • Using HDMI (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Using Optical (With a Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube, or Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Using Bluetooth (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Using HDMI (With a Smart TV)
  • Using Optical (With a Smart TV) You can set up your soundbar in several ways:
Using HDMI (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Plug your Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube into a non-ARC HDMI port on your TV.
  • Now that the ARC or eARC port is available, connect the included HDMI cable to your soundbar and the ARC or eARC port on your TV.
  • Set the input on the soundbar to HDMI. To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment and then select your Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube from the list to set them up again.
  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, check the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to make sure the soundbar or audio system is selected.
  • Note: Make sure to configure your TV’s HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC settings correctly. To learn how to manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on common TV brands, visit Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.
  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your Fire TV Soundbar. If your soundbar is connected to your TV’s ARC or eARC input, you can use your TV remote to control the volume and power.
Using Optical (With a Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube, or Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Connect the soundbar to your TV’s optical port using an optical cable (sold separately).
  • Set the input on the soundbar to Optical. To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
  • Select Equipment Control, and then select Manage Equipment.
  • Select Add Equipment.
  • Select Soundbar, and then select Amazon Fire TV Soundbar.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to configure your Fire TV Soundbar for volume and power control with your Fire TV remote.
Using Bluetooth (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)

Tip: To pair your soundbar with other Bluetooth devices, follow the instructions in Pair Bluetooth Devices to Fire TV Soundbars.

  • Disconnect the soundbar’s HDMI or optical cable from your TV.
  • Note: Connecting the soundbar to your TV using both Bluetooth and HDMI may cause connection issues.
  • Press and hold the Bluetooth button on your soundbar or the included remote.
  • Release the button after your soundbar blinks blue and enters discovery mode.
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube.
  • Select Controllers & Bluetooth Devices.
  • Select Other Bluetooth Devices, and then select Add Bluetooth Devices.
  • Select Fire TV Soundbar from the list of available devices.
Using HDMI (With a Smart TV)
  • Plug the included power cable into the back of the soundbar, and then plug the cord into a power outlet.
  • Connect the included HDMI cable to your soundbar and an ARC or eARC supported port on your TV.
  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, check the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to make sure the soundbar or audio system is selected.
  • Note: Make sure to configure your TV’s HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC settings correctly. To learn how to manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on common TV brands, visit Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.
  • Set the input on the soundbar to HDMI. To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your Fire TV Soundbar. If your soundbar is connected to your TV’s ARC or eARC input, you can use your TV remote to control the volume and power.
Using Optical (With a Smart TV)

  • Connect the soundbar to your TV’s optical port using an optical cable (sold separately).

  • Set the input on the soundbar to Optical. To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.

  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, check the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to make sure the soundbar or audio system is selected.

  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your Fire TV Soundbar. For more help, go to:

  • What Do the LEDs Mean on Fire TV Soundbars?

  • How to Wall Mount the Fire TV Soundbar Was this information helpful?

How to Set Up Fire TV Soundbar Plus

How to Set Up Fire TV Soundbar Plus

Connect the Fire TV Soundbar Plus to an HDMI port on your TV that supports ARC or eARC.

With Fire TV Soundbar Plus, you get three full range speakers, two woofers, and three tweeters that push audio in every direction. The soundbar uses Dolby Atmos and DTS:X to create three-dimensional audio with dynamic movement and depth, so the sound surrounds you and syncs with your entertainment. A dedicated center dialogue channel keeps conversations sharp and clear.

For an upgraded home theater experience, create a 5.1-channel system with the Fire TV Soundbar Plus Series subwoofer and surround speakers. The wireless subwoofer provides rich bass and the two surround speakers create a 360-degree listening experience.

  • Position your Soundbar and Speakers
  • Set Up Overview
  • Using HDMI (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Using HDMI (With a Smart TV)
  • Using Optical (With a Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube, or Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Using Optical (With a Non-Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Using Bluetooth
  • Set Up Subwoofer and Surround Speakers
  • Remote Overview
  • Video Guide to Set Up Your Device
Position your Soundbar and Speakers
  • Place your soundbar under your TV or mount it to the wall.
  • Position the soundbar so that it’s ear level from where you watch TV.
  • Place your subwoofer away from corners and at least 12 inches away from the wall.
  • Check the back of your surround speakers for a note marking them as left or right.
  • Place your surround speakers 6-9 feet from where you watch TV and angle them toward you. Position the speakers at ear level or 1-2 feet higher.
  • Tip: For the best sound, place the speakers behind where you sit. Back to top
Set Up Overview

Now that you have your soundbar where you want it, you can set it up in several ways:

  • Using HDMI (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Using HDMI (With a Smart TV)
  • Using Optical (With a Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube, or Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Using Optical (With a Non-Fire TV Smart TV)
  • Using Bluetooth Back to top
Using HDMI (With a Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube)
  • Plug the included power cable into your soundbar power port and then into a power outlet.
  • If your Fire TV Stick or Fire TV Cube connects to an HDMI ARC or eARC port on your TV, connect the HDMI cable to a non-ARC HDMI port.
  • Using the included HDMI cable, connect your soundbar to the ARC or eARC port on your TV.
  • Set the input on the soundbar to HDMI. To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, set the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to Auto.
  • Note: Make sure to configure your TV’s HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC settings correctly. To learn how to manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on common TV brands, visit Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.
  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your soundbar. You can also adjust the sound settings within Display & Sounds on compatible Fire TV devices. Visit Control Fire TV Soundbar Plus Sound Settings on Fire TV for more information.
  • If you purchased the Fire TV Soundbar Plus with a subwoofer or surround speakers, set up your subwoofer and surround speakers. Back to top
Using HDMI (With a Smart TV)
  • Plug the included power cable into your soundbar power port and then into a power outlet.
  • Using the included HDMI cable, connect your soundbar to the ARC or eARC port on your TV.
  • Set the input on the soundbar to HDMI.
    • To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, set the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to Auto.
  • Note: Make sure to configure your TV’s HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC settings correctly. To learn how to manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC setting on common TV brands, visit Manage the HDMI ARC or HDMI CEC Setting on Your TV.
  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your soundbar. You can also adjust the sound settings within Display & Sounds on compatible Fire TV devices. Visit the Control Fire TV Soundbar Plus Sound Settings on Fire TV page for more information.
  • If you purchased the Fire TV Soundbar Plus with a subwoofer or surround speakers, set up your subwoofer and surround speakers. Back to top
Using Optical (With a Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube, or Fire TV Smart TV)

Note: Optical connections don’t support Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, or the Fire TV sound control feature. For more information about the sound control feature, visit the Control Fire TV Soundbar Plus Sound Settings on Fire TV page.

  • Plug the included power cable into your soundbar power port and then into a power outlet.
  • Connect the soundbar to your TV’s optical port using an optical cable (sold separately).
  • Set the input on the soundbar to Optical.
    • To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • Set up equipment control for the soundbar in your Fire TV settings.
    • Go to Settings on your Fire TV.
    • Select Equipment Control, and then select Manage Equipment.
    • Select Add Equipment.
    • Select Soundbar, and then select Amazon Fire TV Soundbar.
    • Follow the on-screen instructions to set up your Fire TV remote to control the soundbar volume and power.
  • Note: You only need to set up equipment control if using an optical cable to connect your soundbar. If using Bluetooth or HDMI to connect your soundbar, you don’t need to set up equipment control.
  • If you purchased the Fire TV Soundbar Plus with a subwoofer or surround speakers, set up your subwoofer and surround speakers. Back to top
Using Optical (With a Non-Fire TV Smart TV)

Note: Optical connections don’t support Dolby Atmos or DTS:X.

  • Plug the included power cable into your soundbar power port and then into a power outlet.
  • Connect the soundbar to your TV’s optical port using an optical cable (sold separately).
  • Set the input on the soundbar to Optical.
    • To change inputs, press the Input button on the soundbar remote or on the soundbar.
  • If audio doesn’t automatically play on the soundbar, set the Speakers or Audio Output setting on your TV to Auto.
  • Use the included remote to adjust the audio settings on your soundbar.
  • If you purchased the Fire TV Soundbar Plus with a subwoofer or surround speakers, set up your subwoofer and surround speakers. Back to top
Using Bluetooth

Note: Bluetooth connections don’t support Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, or the Fire TV sound control feature. For more information about the sound control feature, visit the Control Fire TV Soundbar Plus Sound Settings on Fire TV page.

  • Plug the included power cable into your soundbar power port and then into a power outlet.
  • Disconnect the soundbar’s HDMI or optical cable from your TV.
  • Note: Connecting the soundbar to your TV using both Bluetooth and HDMI may cause connection issues.
  • Press and hold the Bluetooth button on your soundbar or the included remote.
  • Release the button after your soundbar blinks blue and enters discovery mode.
  • Go to the Bluetooth settings on the device you want to pair and connect to your soundbar.
  • If you purchased the Fire TV Soundbar Plus with a subwoofer or surround speakers, set up your subwoofer and surround speakers. Back to top
Set Up Your Subwoofer and Surround Speakers
  • Turn on your Fire TV Soundbar Plus.
  • Plug the included power cables into your subwoofer and speakers (if you purchased the surround speakers), and then into a power outlet. The subwoofer and speakers connect automatically to your soundbar. Once connected, a white LED appears on the Connect button located on the back of the subwoofer and speakers.

If an amber LED appears, visit the Can’t Pair Fire TV Soundbar Plus Speakers page for troubleshooting steps.

Back to top

Remote Overview

Your soundbar comes with a remote that you can use to control the device. Use the remote to control audio settings like bass, treble, and volume. You can use the playback buttons to control audio content.

For Fire TV Plus Soundbars with surround speakers, your remote includes buttons to control the surround balance and volume.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press firmly and slide the cover down. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

    • Alexa Voice Remote, USB cable, power adapter, AAA batteries for the remote, and HDMI extender cable (optional)
  • A TV with an available HDMI port
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password
    • Don’t have an account? You can make one by visiting the Create an Amazon Account page.
  • Note: If you see a password field but don’t have a password for your Amazon account, Create a Temporary Password
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password Back to top
How to set up your device

Video guide to set up your device

  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Connect the USB cable to the power adapter and the Stick.
  • Plug in the Stick to the TV’s HDMI port. Use the HDMI extender cable if it’s difficult to plug the Stick into the TV’s HDMI port.
  • Plug in the power adapter to the wall. Avoid plugging the USB cable directly into the TV.
  • Turn on your TV and switch to the correct HDMI input.
  • Tip: Use the remote that came with your TV to select the HDMI source or input.
  • To set up Wi-Fi, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen questions to set up equipment control for devices like soundbars. Back to top
Remote overview

Your device comes with the Alexa Voice Remote that you can use to browse your Fire TV. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content or the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to navigate quickly to select apps.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press firmly and slide the cover down. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

Back to top

Troubleshoot setup issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try the following suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to Forgot Your Password.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds). For more troubleshooting information, go to Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, you can find more troubleshooting in the Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi During Setup page.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If you can’t download apps or games, add a default payment method to Your Payments. Back to top
Accessibility features on Fire TV

Fire TV devices have a set of features designed to enhance the viewing experience for customers with disabilities. These features include things like closed captions, a screen reader, screen magnifier, and audio descriptions. To learn more, go to the Accessibility Features for Fire TV page.

Back to top

You’re set up, what’s next?

Once you’ve finished setting up your device, you can explore more features to improve your Fire TV experience. Go to:

  • Find and download your favorite apps
  • Set up equipment control so your Alexa Voice Remote can control the TV’s power and volume
  • Pair compatible Echo devices for Alexa Home Theater for a more immersive sound experience
  • Get access to Live TV on supported apps Back to top

How to Use the Silk Web Browser on Fire TV

Launch the Silk app on your Fire TV to browse the internet, watch videos, bookmark sites, and more.

To start using Silk, select Apps from the Fire TV home screen and open the Internet app.

You can move your cursor by using the directional pad on your Fire TV remote. Press the center button to select things like icons or text fields.

Tip: You can also use a connected keyboard to navigate the Silk browser. Use the arrows keys to move your cursor and the Enter key to select things on-screen. Press F to fast forward, R to rewind, M to open the menu, and Esc to go back.

There are several options on the Silk navigation bar to help with browsing or to manage your settings. The following table lists common options and their descriptions:

Option

Description

Address Bar

Select the address bar to enter a web address or search term using the Fire TV keyboard.

Back

Forward

Use the Back arrow and Forward arrow to go back to a previous page or return to the next page.

Refresh

Refresh your current page.

Menu

Manage Silk browser settings, such as your browsing history and passwords.

To learn more about Silk settings, go to What Are the Silk Browser Settings on Fire TV?

Private Browsing

Enter Private Browsing to have any pages you visit removed from your history after you close the private browsing tab. The browser saves any files you download or bookmarks you create.

Note: Your activity might still be visible to your internet service provider or the websites you visit (including websites affiliated with Amazon).

Desktop Sites

Default Sites

Switch between the desktop and mobile layouts for your current page.

Add Bookmark

Add or remove a bookmark on your current page.

What Are the Silk Browser Settings on Fire TV?

You can manage things like your browsing history, passwords, and parental controls from the Silk Settings menu.

To access your settings options, select Menu and then Settings in the Silk browser. The following table displays Silk Browser settings options and their descriptions:

Option

Description

Clear History and Data

Use this option to clear your Silk browsing history, most visited sites, cookies, cached files, and current page.

You can clear the last 24 hours of your browsing history and data or all of it at once.

Peek Row

Use this feature to add Silk shortcuts to your home screen for easy access.

You can add tiles for your bookmarks, most visited pages, and last visited pages to the My Stuff section of your home screen.

Browsing History

Access a list of all the websites that you’ve visited in Silk.

You can do things like return to a previously visited page, delete specific websites from your history, or delete all your browsing history.

Customize the Menu

Choose which rows appear in your Menu . You can also change the order the rows appear in.

Cursor Speed

Change your cursor speed or your scrolling speed.

Calibrate Screen Size

Note: Some Fire TV Smart TVs don’t support this option.

Adjust your Fire TV’s display size so it matches your TV screen.

Settings

Additional settings for your Silk browser. These settings include things like:

  • Passwords
  • Privacy and security
  • Accessibility
  • Parental controls
  • Site settings Send Feedback

Let us know how we can make Silk better for you. Select the issue that you experienced from a list or follow the on-screen instructions to send us an email with your feedback.

Note: We read all feedback carefully but can’t reply to specific comments.

Help and Support

Go to Help and Support to learn more about using the Silk web browser or for troubleshooting tips.

Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen

Use this guided setup for Echo Show to build your Fire TV experience.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

When the Set up your Fire TV experience screen appears on your Echo Show, select Get Started and follow the instructions on the device.

Guided setup helps you create a Fire TV profile. If you have one already, your Fire TV profile page opens when setup finishes.

To postpone Fire TV setup, select Set Up Later. When you’re ready for Fire TV, go to Echo Show settings.

  • Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:

    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.

  • Open Fire TV, then select Repeat Guided Setup.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions. The Fire TV experience is available on these Echo Show devices:

  • Echo Show 15

  • Echo Show 15 (2nd Generation)

  • Echo Show 21 For more help, go to:

Turn On Fire TV Parental Controls on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen

Use settings to restrict access to content types and purchasing through Fire TV.

To turn Fire TV Parental Controls on or off:

  • Say, “Go to Settings,” or go to the device settings on your Echo Show:
    • If you’re using Alexa+, select the Menu icon on your screen, and then select Settings.
    • If you’re using the original Alexa, swipe down from the top of the screen and select Settings.
  • Open Fire TV.
  • Select Preferences.
  • Turn on the switch for Parental Controls.
  • Set a PIN to use each time that you want to turn parental controls on or off. Enter the PIN that you want and select OK.
  • Select the types of controls that you want to turn on or off. For list of compatible devices Echo Show devices, visit Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen.

Note: Set parental controls settings for Fire TV separately from the Echo Show device settings. Each work on different functions and services.

Watch Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen with Touch

Launch and navigate the Fire TV experience on the screen of compatible Echo devices. Use touch on your compatible Echo devices with a screen to launch and navigate the Fire TV experience.

Note: Settings menu items for the Echo Hub and Echo Show 5 (all generations) may vary, and those devices will receive a software update soon.

To launch the Fire TV experience, select the Fire TV button on the home screen, or go to your device settings.

You can also use the Fire TV widget to open some Fire TV services, such as My Watchlist, Recently Watched, and Recent Apps.

Some video services available with Fire TV have limited touchscreen capabilities. Using such services is best with a compatible Fire TV remote. If you don’t have a remote, the Echo Show provides an on-screen virtual remote that works like a physical remote for these services. The virtual remote doesn’t appear when you’re using a physical remote.

For a list of compatible Echo Show devices with Fire TV, visit Set Up Fire TV on Your Compatible Echo Devices with a Screen

Note: Fire TV isn’t available when the Echo Show is in Amazon Kids mode, or when using a kid’s Alexa profile. To allow Fire TV on the device, turn off Amazon Kids in the device settings. Then, turn Amazon Kids back on when you’re done watching Fire TV.

Can’t Create Fire TV and Echo Audio System

If you can’t connect your Fire TV and Echo device, try these steps.

  • Make sure that your Echo and Fire TV devices are compatible with the home theater feature.

  • Make sure that your devices are registered to the same account.

  • Check that your devices are on the same Wi-Fi network and frequency band.

  • Make sure that the Alexa app is up to date.

  • Force close the Alexa app and restart it before trying to create your home theater.

  • Make sure that your devices are on the latest software version. For Echo devices, say “Check for software updates.” For Fire TV, go to Settings > My Fire TV > About > Check for Updates.

  • Restart your devices. For Echo devices, temporarily unplug them from power. For Fire TV, go to Settings > My Fire TV > Restart. Wait a few minutes before playing content. For more help, go to:

  • Alexa Home Theater on Fire TV Stick 4K Max Isn’t Working

  • Download the Alexa App

  • Amazon Devices that Support Fire TV and Echo Device Speaker Systems

  • Force Stop an App on an iOS Device

  • Force Stop an App on an Android Device For more help, try our Echo & Alexa forum.

Can’t Play Your Fire TV Audio on Your Echo Devices

One or more paired Echo speakers not playing sound in home theater mode? Use these suggestions.

  • Verify that your devices are compatible with home theater mode.
  • Verify that your Echo speakers are “online” in the Alexa app.
  • Connect all devices to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Turn up the volume on your speakers.
  • Play a video title from a different streaming media app.
  • Make sure to select the home theater audio option on your Fire TV device to match your activity. When watching video with your Alexa Home Theater, turn off Gaming Audio (default). For gaming, turn on Gaming Audio.
  • Restart devices in your home theater group. For Echo devices, temporarily unplug them from power. For Fire TV, go to Settings > My Fire TV > Restart. Wait a few minutes before playing content.
  • For audio issues with your Fire TV Stick 4K Max, there are additional troubleshooting steps on Alexa Home Theater on Fire TV Stick 4K Max Isn’t Working.. If the issue persists, delete the home theater group in the Alexa app and set it up again.

For more help, go to:

  • Play Audio from Your Fire TV on Your Echo Devices
  • Multi-Room Music is Out of Sync on Your Fire TV Device

Compare Audio Systems on Echo and Fire TV Devices

Discover more about Multi-Room Music, speaker sets, and Alexa Home Theater support for Alexa-enabled devices.

Multi-Room Music
  • Plays music across multiple, compatible Alexa-enabled devices.
  • Devices can be located in different rooms and added to multiple groups.
  • Can include speaker sets and home theater systems.
  • Control audio settings on each device.
Speaker Set (Stereo Pair)
  • Pair two compatible Echo devices for left/right sound during music playback.
  • Add Echo Sub for deeper bass.
  • Devices must be located in the same room.
  • Audio settings, like volume, are common to all devices in the pair.
  • Go here for a list of Compatible Echo Devices for Stereo Pairs.
Home Theater System
  • Pair one or two Echo devices with your Fire TV device for home theater. Optionally, add Echo Sub for additional bass.
  • Supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Digital, and Dolby Digital Plus with Echo Studio.
  • Audio settings, like volume, are common to all devices in the home theater system. Your Fire TV remote controls home theater volume by default, and not TV volume. This is adjustable in Fire TV settings.
  • Devices in a home theater group need to be located in the same room as the television.
  • Go here for a list of Amazon Devices that Support Fire TV and Echo Device Speaker Systems. Tip: Create home theater groups or speaker sets before adding to Multi-Room Music groups.

For more help, go to:

  • Create Speaker Sets with Compatible Echo Devices

Link Your Fire TV and Alexa Device

To link your compatible Alexa-enabled device to your Fire TV, use the Alexa app. You can also say, “Play [movie title] on Fire TV” and confirm that you want your Alexa device to control your Fire TV.

For the devices to pair properly and work together, your Alexa device and Fire TV must be registered to the same account. You can link multiple Alexa devices to the same Fire TV. Not all features are supported on Echo Show devices or for a paired Fire TV Cube.

Tip: Before linking your Alexa-enabled device and Fire TV, check that you have the latest version of the Alexa app.

  • Open the Alexa app .
  • Open More and select Settings .
  • Select TV & Video.
  • Select Fire TV.
  • Select Link Your Alexa Device and follow the on-screen instructions. Note: For information on setting up a home theater with your Fire TV and Alexa devices, go to: Play Audio from Your Fire TV on Your Echo Devices.

Play Audio from Your Fire TV on Your Echo Devices

Play audio on your compatible Echo device from a Fire TV device after setting up a home theater group.

Set up your Fire TV and Echo devices, then check for software updates.

  • Open the Alexa app .

  • Open Devices .

  • Select Plus and scroll to the bottom of the screen.

  • Select Combine speakers.

  • Select Home Theater.

  • Select your compatible Fire TV device.

  • Select up to two compatible Echo devices to use as speakers, along with an optional Echo Sub.

  • Select left and right speakers when using two Echo devices.

  • Name your home theater and assign it to a room in your house.

  • Devices in your speaker group should be in the same room as your television.

  • Follow the directions on your TV to finish the setup. For more help, go to:

About VoiceView for Fire TV

About VoiceView for Fire TV

VoiceView is a screen reader for Fire TV devices. It speaks on-screen text out loud as you navigate menu options and settings. You can also use VoiceView to help you set up your device.

To access the VoiceView User’s Guide, go to: Amazon Fire TV VoiceView User’s Guide

  • Use VoiceView During First-Time Setup
  • Turn on VoiceView in Fire TV Settings
  • VoiceView Controls
  • VoiceView Navigation
  • Review Mode
  • Playback Controls
  • Button Descriptions
  • On-screen Keyboard
  • VoiceView Settings Note: For an accessibility-friendly video overview of this topic, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.
Use VoiceView During First-Time Setup

To get started with VoiceView on your Fire TV Stick with Alexa Voice Remote:

  • First, connect your Fire TV Stick to an HDMI port on your TV, and plug in the power adapter.
  • Then, insert the batteries included with your Alexa Voice Remote. You hear a single tone sound when your remote is ready to pair to your Fire TV stick.
  • Press the Home button on your remote for up to 10 seconds to pair it to your device.
  • When the pairing process is complete, you hear a different, two-tone sound. This indicates that you can now turn on VoiceView.
  • Hold the Back and Menu buttons for 2 seconds to start VoiceView. Note: The Fire TV App is not supported during first-time setup.
Turn on VoiceView in Fire TV Settings

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

To turn on VoiceView:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select VoiceView.
  • Select VoiceView again to turn it on. You hear “VoiceView Ready” when the feature is activated and ready to use. When you turn the feature off, you hear “VoiceView Exiting.”

The first time you turn VoiceView on, a tutorial automatically opens with tips on how to use the feature and locate buttons on your Fire TV remote.

The first screen of the tutorial asks you to confirm that you intended to turn VoiceView on. To confirm, press the Play/Pause button on your remote. You can also skip the tutorial by pressing the Skip/Fast-Forward button .

You can find some additional tips and examples of how you can use VoiceView on your Fire TV device.

VoiceView Controls

The following table outlines the buttons available on your Alexa Voice Remote to control VoiceView.

Buttons

Action

Hold Back and Menu for two seconds

Turn VoiceView on or off

Single press Menu

Hear usage tips and orientation descriptions to help you understand the layout of certain user screens, and learn more about using VoiceView

Double press Menu

Access more options available for your current selection

Press Play/Pause

Stop speech

Hold Play/Pause and press Select or OK

Open the Explore Your Remote activity. Explore Your Remote reads the options of all remote buttons and their descriptions

Hold Play/Pause and press Left or Right

Cycle through Speech Rate or Speech Volume settings

Press Play/Pause and Up or Down

Increase/decrease speech volume or speed

Press Rewind or Fast Forward while VoiceView is speaking

Skip backward or forward through the spoken elements on your Fire TV

VoiceView Navigation

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

While you navigate your Fire TV device, a green box highlights your current on-screen selection or location. VoiceView automatically speaks and/or describes what you’ve selected.

The following table outlines the buttons available on your Alexa Voice Remote to navigate your Fire TV device with VoiceView.

Button

Action

Down

Focus and have VoiceView speak the item below the current selection

Up

Focus and have VoiceView speak the item above the current selection

Left

Focus and have VoiceView speak the item to the left of the current selection

Right

Focus and have VoiceView speak the item to the right of the current selection

Return to the Fire TV Home screen

Select or OK

Select the currently focused element on your Fire TV

Review Mode

In addition to describing selectable navigation options and controls, VoiceView features an enhanced navigation mode, called Review Mode, that you can use to hear descriptions of all on-screen text.

The following table outlines the buttons available on your Alexa Voice Remote to turn on and control Review Mode.

Button

Action

Press Home

Go to the VoiceView Settings

Hold Menu for 3 seconds

Turn Review Mode on or off

Press Menu

Have VoiceView spell out words

Press Up or Down

Highlight other on-screen text, including video details like plot or cast information, customer ratings, headings, lists, and more

Press Left or Right

Move between selectable navigation options

Playback Controls

When VoiceView is speaking, you can still control video playback using the buttons on your Alexa Voice Remote.

The following table outlines the buttons available on your Alexa Voice Remote to control video playback.

Button

Action

Double press Menu

Access more playback options in Prime video, including Watch from Beginning, Subtitles and Captions, and Next Episode (for TV shows)

Play/Pause

Starts and stops media playback

Skip Back/Rewind

Skip back in a movie, TV show, or music

Skip/Fast-Forward

Skip forward in a movie, TV show, or music

Button Descriptions

The following table outlines where to find the Alexa Voice Remote buttons that you can use to control VoiceView.

Button

Description and Location

Back

Left button in the top row of three small buttons

Middle button located on the top row of three small buttons

Left, Right , Up, or Down

The large round ring toward the top of your remote is the directional keypad, which you can use to navigate by pressing the Left, Right, Up and Down keys

Menu

Right button in the top row of three small buttons

Play/Pause

Middle button located on the bottom row of three small buttons

Select or OK

Large round button near the top, inside the directional keypad ring

Skip Back/Rewind

Left button located on the bottom row of three small buttons

Skip/Fast-Forward

Right button located on the bottom row of three small buttons

On-screen keyboard

When the Fire TV on-screen keyboard is open, VoiceView speaks out each character as you select it. Press the Select or OK button on your remote to enter a character.

If you have a Fire TV remote with an Alexa Voice button , you can use your voice to search for content. You can also use your voice to interact with Alexa. Press and hold the Alexa Voice button and say what you’re looking for.

To learn more about what Alexa can do, you can ask “Tell me what you can do” or go to Learn to Use Alexa with Fire TV.

VoiceView Settings

To access and manage VoiceView preferences:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select VoiceView. You can manage the following options:

  • VoiceView - Turn VoiceView on or off.

  • Reading Speed - Adjust the rate of speech speed for the VoiceView voice.

  • Speech Volume - Set a volume level for the VoiceView voice. Speech Volume defaults to 40% of device volume.

  • Sounds Volume - Set the volume level for the feedback sounds that VoiceView uses. Sounds Volume defaults to 40% of device volume.

  • Key Echo - Determine how text characters are echoed back to you while you enter them with the on-screen keyboard. By default, characters are echoed as they are typed to confirm entry. You can change this setting to None, Characters, Words, or both Characters and Words.

  • Punctuation Level - Control which punctuation marks VoiceView reads aloud. For more help, try our Amazon Fire TV forum.

VoiceView

VoiceView is a screen reader that speaks on-screen text out loud as you navigate menu options and settings. Use VoiceView to navigate and set up your device. To switch VoiceView on or off:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select VoiceView.
  • Select VoiceView again to turn it off. The first time you turn on VoiceView, a tutorial provides tips on the feature and how to locate buttons on your Fire TV remote. Currently, VoiceView only works with the Fire TV remotes; VoiceView doesn’t support the Fire TV Remote App.

To learn more, go to About VoiceView for Fire TV.

Back to top

Explore Your Remote

Turn on Explore Your Remote to have the names of your Fire TV remote buttons spoken when you press them.

Note: You need to turn on VoiceView on your Fire TV device to use Explore Your Remote.

To turn on Explore Your Remote:

  • Turn on VoiceView.
    • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
    • Select Accessibility.
    • Select VoiceView.
  • Press and hold the Play/Pause button first, and while holding it, press the Select or OK button . On your remote, Play/Pause is the middle button located on the bottom row of three small buttons. Select or OK button is the large round button near the top, inside the directional keypad ring.
  • Wait until you hear, “Explore Remote.”
  • Press any button on your remote to have the button name spoken. To turn off Explore Your Remote, press and hold the Play/Pause button first, and while holding it, press the Select or OK button again.

Back to top

Closed Captions

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

Turn on closed captions during video playback to display on-screen text for the dialog in movies and TV shows.

Prime Video titles with closed captions typically feature a “CC” symbol in the video details.

Most videos with closed captions include English text, but you can often find other languages available. To access the available languages, open the video details for a movie or TV show and find the Subtitles section.

There are two ways to turn on closed captions: while watching a Prime Video movie or show, or using the device accessibility setting.

While watching a Prime Video movie or show:

  • Start video playback.

  • Press the Menu button on your Fire TV remote to open more playback options.

  • Select Subtitles.

  • Select the Off button under Subtitles. Then select an available language from the options on-screen to turn on Subtitles.

  • Note: Set your preferred text size and display. A sample displays as you change your preferences.

  • Once you’ve made your selections, press the Menu button again to return to playback, and start watching the video with Subtitles. To turn off Subtitles:

  • Press the Menu button during playback.

  • Open Subtitles.

  • Set Subtitles back to Off. Back to top

Alexa Captions

You can turn on Alexa Captions on your Fire TV device to display Alexa’s responses when available.

To turn on Alexa Captions:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility.
  • Select Alexa Caption.
  • Select ON/OFF for the Alexa Caption option. Tip: Use the available options to customize the text style to your preference.

Back to top

Audio Descriptions

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

Audio Descriptions are available for select Prime Video titles and provide narration for compatible movies and TV shows. They describe actions, characters, scene changes, on-screen text, and other visual content.

There are two ways to turn on Audio Descriptions: while watching a movie or show, or using the device accessibility setting.

While watching Prime Video movies and TV shows:

  • Start video playback of a title compatible with Audio Descriptions.

  • Press the Menu button on your Fire TV remote to open more playback options.

  • Note: With VoiceView activated, press the Menu button twice.

  • Select Audio.

  • Under the Audio options, select the audio track with the Audio Descriptions tag.

  • Once you’ve made your selection, the video reloads and resume playback with Audio Descriptions. To turn Audio Descriptions while watching a movie or show:

  • Press the Menu button during playback.

  • Open Audio.

  • Select the audio track with the Audio Descriptions tag. To turn on Audio Descriptions:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select Audio Descriptions.

  • Set Prime Video to ON. To turn off Audio Descriptions:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select Audio Descriptions.

  • Select OFF for Prime Video option. Back to top

Screen Magnifier

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

To turn on Screen Magnifier:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select ON or OFF for the Screen Magnifier option. You can also use the Fire TV remote to manage Screen Magnifier:

  • To turn on or off, hold Back and Fast Forward .

  • To turn on or off zoom, press Menu and Play/Pause .

  • To zoom in, press Menu and Fast Forward .

  • To Zoom out, press Menu and Rewind .

  • To pan in a different direction, press Menu and Up, Down, Left, or Right .

  • To enter the Single Press Magnifier, press and hold Menu for 1 second.

  • Note: A yellow arrow appears on the top left of the TV screen when you activate Single Press Magnifier.

    • To zoom in or out, press Fast Forward or Rewind .
    • To pan in different directions, press Up, Down, Left, or Right .
    • To activate or deactivate zoom, press Play/Pause .
    • To exit Single Press Magnifier, press and hold the Menu for 1 second or press Back or Select . Note: Most video content isn’t compatible with the zoom feature.

Back to top

Adaptive Display

Adaptive Display enlarges text, menus, icons, and other interface elements on your Fire TV Home, Settings, and Profile screens. Unlike Screen Magnifier, everything stays in place and you can navigate normally with your remote, without needing to scroll to find content.

Choose from two levels:

  • Large - Moderate enlargement.

  • Larger - Maximum enlargemen To turn on Adaptive Display:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select Adaptive Display.

  • Choose your preferred level: Large or Larger. Tip: You can also turn on the feature by going to Display & Sounds from the Quick Actions panel or in Settings.

To turn off Adaptive Display:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select Adaptive Display.
  • Select Default. Note: Adaptive Display works alongside other accessibility features like Screen Magnifier, Text Banner, and VoiceView.

Back to top

Text Banner

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

Text Banner displays a white box on the screen with the title of the currently focused item and related text. This feature is especially important for customers with visual impairments and limited vision range. This feature allows you to customize colors, box, and text size.

To access the Text Banner feature:

  • Select Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select Text Banner.
  • To customize the experience, select Font Size & Color or Banner size, Timing, & more.
  • For more details, select Tutorial. To turn Text Banner on or off with your Fire TV remote, press and hold Rewind and Fast Forward for two seconds.

Back to top

High Contrast Text (Experimental Feature)

Note: For an accessibility-friendly video of this feature, visit our Amazon Fire TV Accessibility Help Videos page.

Fire TV devices feature a high contrast text experimental feature, designed to help make text easier to read. It changes most of the text on-screen to black or white and adds a border of the opposite color. To turn High Contrast Text on or off:

  • Select Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select High Contrast Text. Note: High contrast text is currently an experimental feature, and performance varies. If you’re having trouble navigating your device or selecting items, try to turn off this feature.

Back to top

Audio Streaming for Hearing Aids and Devices

Audio Streaming for Hearing Aids and Devices (ASHA) lets you pair your compatible Bluetooth hearing aids directly to your Fire TV device for private listening.

On Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series TVs, you can stream audio to paired hearing aids while others listen through the TV’s built-in speakers. Visit the following help page to learn more: Use Dual Audio on Your Fire TV Smart TV.

Note: Compatible Starkey hearing aids, Widex hearing aids, and Cochlear hearing devices are supported on:

  • Fire TV Cube (2nd Generation)
  • Fire TV Cube (3rd Generation)
  • Amazon Ember Artline TV (2026 Release)
  • Amazon Ember Mini-LED Series and Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series (2024 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni QLED Series
  • Amazon Ember QLED Series and Fire TV Omni QLED Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV Omni Series
  • Fire TV 4-Series
  • Amazon Ember 4-Series and Fire TV 4-Series (2025 Release)
  • Fire TV 2-Series
  • Amazon Ember 2-Series and Fire TV 2-Series (2025 Release) To pair your hearing aids and devices with Fire TV:

Note: “Hearing aids” refers to ASHA-compatible Bluetooth hearing devices like:

  • Hearing aids

  • Cochlear implants

  • Bone-conduction hearing devices Before starting the pairing process with your Fire TV device, follow the manufacturer’s instructions to put your hearing aids in pairing mode. Once your hearing aids are in pairing mode:

  • Select Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select Hearing Aids.

  • Select Add Hearing Aids.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions. Note: If you’re using a right and left hearing aid, you need to pair them both separately.

If you’re having issues with pairing your hearing aids, visit the following help page: Troubleshoot Hearing Aid and Device Connectivity with Fire TV.

To control the volume:

Once you pair your hearing aids, you can control the volume using the volume control buttons available on your remote control. If your remote doesn’t have volume control options:

  • Hold the Home button to access the Quick Settings.

  • Use your remote to increase or decrease the volume bar. You can also adjust the volume from the settings:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Accessibility .

  • Select Hearing Aids and choose your hearing aids.

  • Select Volume. Control the volume using the fast forward and rewind buttons on your remote. Back to top

Auracast Streaming for Bluetooth Low Energy Audio Devices

Auracast streaming lets you pair multiple Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) audio devices to your Fire TV Smart TV for private and multi-user listening experiences.

Note: The following devices support BLE audio:

  • Panasonic W90/W95 Series Fire TV Smart TV
  • Panasonic Z85 Series Fire TV Smart TV
  • Panasonic Z90/Z93/Z95 Series Fire TV Smart TV To pair your BLE compatible Hearing Aids with your Fire TV Smart TV and tune into Auracast, go to Pair BLE or Auracast Headsets to Your Fire TV Smart TV.

Back to top

Preferred Speaking Rate

Note: Preferred Speaking Rate is only available in English.

You can adjust Alexa’s speaking speed to make it more comfortable for you to understand. Simply use voice commands to adjust how fast or slow Alexa talks.

  • To decrease speed, say “Alexa, speak slower.”
  • To increase speed, say “Alexa, speak faster.”
  • To return to normal speed, say, “Alexa, speak at your default rate”. Back to top
Adaptive Listening Mode

Note: Adaptive Listening Mode is only available in English.

Adaptive Listening gives you more time to finish speaking before Alexa responds to you.

To turn on Adaptive Listening for your Fire TV device:

  • Open the Alexa app .
  • Select More .
  • Select Settings .
  • Select Accessibility.
  • Select Adaptive Listening Mode.
  • Select the device or devices where you want to use Adaptive Listening. Back to top
Dialogue Boost Mode

Note: Feature availability varies across Fire TV devices.

The Dialogue Boost feature helps to improve dialogue volume and clarity relative to the background music and effects.

To turn on Dialogue Boost:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Accessibility .
  • Select Dialogue Boost.
  • Choose from a range of levels to match your preferred dialogue volume.
  • Note: The Enhanced or Heightened options boost the dialogue by enhancing low frequency (high pitched) speech. You can also manage Dialogue Boost mode from your Fire TV Display & Sounds settings.

Alexa and Alexa Device FAQs

  • Alexa FAQs
  • Amazon Kids on Alexa and Echo Devices FAQs

Alexa FAQs
1. How do I use Alexa?

Alexa allows you to ask questions and make requests using just your voice. For instance, you can ask Alexa a question, such as “What is the weather today in New York?”, or tell Alexa to do something, like “Add batteries to my shopping list,” or “Play jazz.” When you speak to Alexa, a recording of what you asked Alexa is sent to Amazon’s cloud so we can process and respond to your request. You can access Alexa differently based on the type of device you are using. For example, for “hands free” devices, like the Amazon Echo, you can access Alexa by saying the wake word (e.g., Alexa, Amazon, Computer, Echo, or Ziggy). For other devices, like certain Fire tablets and the Alexa app, you can access Alexa by pressing a button and speaking, or by typing a request to Alexa. You can use Alexa across a range of Amazon devices and services, including to help you shop on Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app, and to search for music on Amazon Music. Certain functionality may not be available across all devices and services where Alexa is available. For example, if you ask Alexa to set a timer while using Amazon.com, you may be routed to Alexa.com or the Alexa app to complete your request. To learn more about Alexa on Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app, visit the Alexa for Shopping FAQs.

2. What is Alexa+?

Alexa+ is the newest version of Alexa with more knowledge, greater capabilities, and many new features. For example, you can ask Alexa almost any question, share files for Alexa to summarize, or ask Alexa to remember something for your later use. Alexa+ is available across all your compatible Alexa-enabled products, including the Alexa app and Alexa.com. Devices not compatible with Alexa+ remain in the original Alexa experience. Alexa+ is currently only available in the English language.

3. Is Alexa recording all my conversations?

No. By default, Alexa-enabled devices are designed to detect only your chosen wake word (e.g., Alexa, Amazon, Computer, Echo, or Ziggy). The device detects the wake word by identifying acoustic patterns that match the wake word. No audio is stored or sent to the cloud unless the device detects the wake word (or Alexa is activated by pressing a button). On certain devices, you can enable features that allow you to interact with Alexa without the wake word. For instance, Follow Up Mode allows you to make follow-up requests to Alexa without having to repeat the wake word and, on compatible devices, interrupt Alexa to make requests. When you join Alexa+, Follow Up Mode will be turned on for your compatible Echo devices and the Alexa app. See the FAQ “How does Follow Up Mode work?” for more information. You can also configure supported Echo devices to detect specific sounds, such as the sound of smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms, and glass breaking. See the FAQs “How does Alexa Emergency Assist work?” and “How do Routines with sound detection work?” for more information.

4. What happens when I speak to Alexa?

When you speak to Alexa, a recording of what you ask Alexa is sent to Amazon’s cloud, where we process your request and other information to respond to you. As part of that processing, we create a text transcript of your request to help Alexa interpret and understand what you said, take any requested actions, and provide a response. For example, when you ask “Alexa, play top hits on Amazon Music,” we use the recording of your request and information from Amazon Music to play top hits.

5. How does Alexa minimize the amount of data sent to the cloud?

Alexa-enabled devices are designed to record as little audio as possible and minimize the amount of background noise streamed to the cloud. By default, Alexa-enabled devices only stream audio to the cloud if the wake word is detected (or Alexa is activated by pressing a button). When an Alexa-enabled device detects the wake word and begins streaming audio to the cloud, Alexa performs a “cloud verification” of the wake word using the more powerful processing capabilities of the cloud to double-check the audio to confirm detection of the wake word. If the cloud verification does not also detect the wake word, Alexa stops processing the audio and ends the audio stream to the cloud. See the FAQ “How does Follow Up Mode work?” for more information about how audio is processed for a feature that allows you to interact with Alexa without the wake word.

6. What about “false wakes”?

In some cases, your Alexa-enabled device might interpret another word or sound as the wake word (for instance, the name “Alex” or someone saying “Alexa” on the radio or television). When this happens, we call that a “false wake.” We have a team of world-class scientists and engineers dedicated to continually improving our wake word detection technology and preventing false wakes from happening, including through the cloud verification mechanism described in the FAQ “How does Alexa minimize the amount of data sent to the cloud?”

Anytime your Echo device detects the wake word, a visual or audible indicator will signal it is recording audio to stream to the cloud, and you can review and delete the voice recordings associated with your account (including any audio resulting from a false wake) in Review Alexa History available at More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com.

7. Can I review and delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

Yes. You can review and delete Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts of those recordings, and typed requests to Alexa associated with your Amazon account by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. When you make a series of requests to Alexa, your requests may be grouped together for review into a single “chat” if Alexa determines those requests are related to one other. For example, if you ask several questions in short succession about places to visit in Paris, those requests may be grouped together into a single chat in Review Alexa History so you can easily go back to review the recommendations Alexa provided in that chat.

Deleting voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests may limit our ability to personalize your experience and make improvements based on your interactions with Alexa and cause certain features to stop working. For example, if you choose not to save any voice recordings, voice IDs associated with your account will be deleted and voice ID will not work. Similarly, if you delete the voice recordings Alexa used to create your voice ID (by, for example, choosing to have your Alexa voice recordings deleted automatically after 3 or 18 months), voice ID may not work.

If you have changed your default marketplace while using an Alexa-enabled product, you will need to delete all Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests associated with your account separately for each marketplace. To learn how to transfer your Amazon account to another marketplace, go here.

For voice requests you make to Alexa in the Amazon Shopping app, we automatically delete the voice recordings of those requests, but we retain their transcripts until you choose to delete them. See the Voice Shopping FAQs to learn more about how we handle your voice requests to Alexa in the Amazon Shopping app.

8. Can I choose to automatically delete my voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

Yes, you can choose to automatically delete your voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa after a specified period of time (3 or 18 months), or you can choose to not save any voice recordings. If you choose automatic deletion after 3 or 18 months, we will delete the voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests associated with a chat once the specified period of time has passed since your last request to Alexa within that chat. If you choose not to save any voice recordings, we will automatically delete your voice recordings after we process your requests and automatically delete all existing voice recordings associated with your account, but your text transcripts of those recordings and any typed requests will be retained for 30 days after your last interaction with Alexa in a given chat, after which they will automatically be deleted. We retain those text transcripts and typed requests to allow you to review the requests you make to Alexa, and to improve your Alexa experience and our services. You can delete the text transcripts at any time by going to More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app or amazon.com.

9. What happens when I delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?

When you delete Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa associated with a chat, we will delete those items from Amazon’s cloud. We may still retain other records of your Alexa interactions, such as attachments you shared with Alexa, information you provided through your interactions, records of actions Alexa took in response to your requests, records of products you searched for, and other information related to your requests. This allows us, for instance, to continue to provide your reminders, timers, and alarms, process your orders, personalize your experience, remember your preferences and the things you’ve shared with Alexa (like notes in Remember This and information relevant to you), show your shopping lists, tasks, and messages sent through Alexa Communication, and answer questions about attachments you’ve shared with Alexa. If your request was processed by an Alexa skill, deleting your voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa does not delete any information retained by the developer of that skill (skill developers do not receive voice recordings). For more information on Alexa skills, refer to the FAQ “How do Alexa skills work?” For more information on notes, refer to the FAQ “What is Remember This?” For more information on removing messages sent through Alexa Communication, refer to the FAQ “How do I remove Alexa messages from my conversation list?” For more information about reviewing, downloading, or deleting an attachment you’ve shared with Alexa, refer to the FAQ “How does Review Attachments work?” For more information on deleting the voice recordings you used to teach Alexa your voice when you created a voice ID, refer to the FAQ “How does voice ID work?”

10. How does deletion work?

You can delete certain data associated with your account. For instance, you can delete your voice recordings, text transcripts of those recordings, and typed requests to Alexa, as well as information Alexa receives from third-party smart home devices, using settings available in the Alexa app or at amazon.com. When you request deletion, we begin the process of securely deleting your data from Amazon’s cloud storage systems.

Our deletion processes are designed to be comprehensive and can take some time to complete. While we are processing your deletion request, the data for which you requested deletion may still be used to personalize your experience, including by informing Alexa’s responses, and we may still provide that data to you in response to a data access request. We make every effort to ensure our deletion processes run smoothly; however, the specific timing of deletion may vary based on the type of information requested for deletion and the technical operation of our internal systems. Alexa does not support voice requests to delete data in all circumstances, and Alexa may not always interpret or execute requests to delete information made by voice correctly. We design our systems to continue securely processing your requests until deletion is completed. You can always review the voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa associated with your account at any time by going to More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. Data that is collected by third parties, like skill developers, and data stored outside of Amazon’s cloud, like data stored on your Echo or mobile devices, may not be deleted. Your deletion requests may not delete copies of data that have been de-identified and are no longer linked to you or your account. If we have used your data to improve our services, we may continue to retain and use the systems trained on your data after your data has been deleted from our data stores.

For more information on how deletion works in various contexts, see the FAQs “What happens when I delete my Alexa voice recordings, text transcripts, and typed requests to Alexa?”, “How can I delete the information Alexa receives from my third-party smart home devices?”, and “Can I review and delete my Alexa Emergency Assist audio recordings?”

11. What is the Review Alexa History feature?

Review Alexa History is a feature that allows you to play the audio of your voice recordings that were streamed to the cloud, review the text transcript of what Alexa thought you said, and review your typed requests to Alexa, as well as Alexa’s responses. This feature can help you better understand how Alexa works and what Alexa is and is not recording. You can also use it to recall answers Alexa gave you previously, such as the name of a restaurant Alexa recommended. If Alexa makes a mistake, you can use this feature to see what may have gone wrong, such as whether Alexa misunderstood a particular word or phrase. You can access Review Alexa History by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. You can also help us improve our services by providing feedback within Review Alexa History.

12. How can I manage the use of my voice recordings?

You can manage the use of your voice recordings to improve our services and develop new features by visiting More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com.

13. How does Alexa use my voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other information?

Alexa uses your voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other information, including your notes, calendars, emails, and attachments you send to Alexa, as well as information from third-party services, (such as your linked accounts) to answer your questions, fulfill your requests, and personalize and improve your experience and our services. For example, with Alexa+, Alexa can have human-like conversations by adapting the sentiment, tone, and content of its responses to address your request. This enables Alexa to sound excited or empathetic if, for example, your favorite sports team wins or loses. We also associate your requests and other information with your Amazon account to enable you to review your voice recordings, access other Amazon services, and provide you with a more personalized experience. For example, Alexa can pick up from where you left off if you ask Alexa to play an audiobook from Audible and can provide you with personalized recommendations and responses to your requests that are based on your order history, the songs you have listened to on Amazon Music, or the topics you have discussed with Alexa. We also personalize your experience based on conversations you’ve had with Alexa. For example, if you discuss your preference for Thai food with Alexa, Alexa may remember that preference and take it into account when you ask for restaurant recommendations. With Alexa+, we may also share relevant information from your interactions with our services to enable skill developers to provide you with a more personalized experience and deliver the content or services you request. See the FAQ “What information do we make available to developers to enable skill personalization in Alexa+?”

14. How do my voice recordings, text transcripts, typed requests to Alexa, and other interactions with Alexa improve Amazon’s services?

Alexa is designed to get smarter and more personalized every day. For example, we use your Alexa interactions to help improve Alexa’s ability to understand and respond to natural language requests and to train Amazon’s machine learning models. Training our models with real world interactions from a diverse range of customers is necessary for Alexa to respond properly to variations in our customers’ speech patterns, dialects, accents, and vocabulary, the acoustic environments where customers use Alexa, and the many ways in which customers engage with Alexa. This training relies in part on supervised machine learning, an industry-standard practice where humans review an extremely small sample of your Alexa interactions to help Alexa understand how to interpret your requests correctly and provide appropriate responses. For example, a human reviewing a customer’s voice request for the weather in Austin may identify that Alexa misinterpreted it as a request for the weather in Boston. And a human reviewing Alexa’s response to a request about a current event may determine whether Alexa’s response was accurate, appropriate, and properly personalized. Our supervised learning process includes multiple safeguards to protect customer privacy. For example, you can review and delete your voice recordings, and you can manage the use of your voice recordings to improve our services and develop new features, by visiting More > Alexa Privacy in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. We also may use your interactions with Alexa to improve other Amazon products and services. For example, when you shop on Alexa, we may use those interactions to improve the systems we use to help customers search for products.

15. How can I manage my Alexa advertising preferences?

Certain experiences on Alexa, such as streaming music or news videos on your Echo Show device, may contain ads. Some of those ads may be interest-based. Interest-based ads, sometimes referred to as personalized or targeted ads, present you with features, products, and services that might be of interest to you based on your interactions with certain content or services. For instance, if you ask Alexa to order paper towels or for recipe ideas, you might see or hear ads related to cleaning products or cooking utensils. We offer you settings to manage your interest-based advertising preferences.

We make available unique, user-resettable identifiers called advertising IDs to third-party skill developers and content providers (like radio providers) for advertising and analytics purposes. Each third-party developer and content provider receives a different Alexa Advertising ID for you, and a different Alexa Advertising ID for each device you use to access the applicable third-party skill or content. You can instruct these third parties not to use these advertising IDs to deliver interest-based ads to you or to build profiles for advertising. Developers and content providers are responsible for honoring your preferences.

To manage your preferences for third parties and reset your Alexa Advertising IDs, visit More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Skill Permissions and Ad Preferences in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. Even if you turn this setting off, developers and content providers will still receive Alexa Advertising IDs for other purposes, such as reducing ad repetition and fraud detection, but you can reset your Alexa Advertising IDs at any time.

You can also choose whether to receive interest-based ads delivered by Amazon on Alexa. If you choose not to receive interest-based ads from Amazon, you may still receive personalized recommendations and other similar features. You will still receive ads provided by Amazon, but they will not be based on your interests. You can manage this setting at More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Your Alexa Data in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. This setting does not apply to ads delivered by Amazon when you use other Amazon apps or services, such as Amazon Music and Fire TV, even if you use Alexa to interact with those apps or services. To learn more about Amazon’s interest-based advertising, see our Interest-Based Ads notice.

16. How do Alexa skills work?

Skills enable developers to make content or services available to you on Alexa. You can view and enable skills in the Alexa app and enable certain skills by voice. You can use a skill by saying a specific phrase, called the invocation name. When you use a skill, we may exchange relevant information with the developer of that skill, such as your answers when you play a trivia skill, your ZIP code when you ask for the weather, or the content of your requests, which may include text transcripts (but not your voice recordings). If you make a request to Alexa without using a skill invocation name, we may send the content of your request to several skills, and enable and launch the skill we think is best able to respond to your request. The Alexa app contains more information about skills, such as privacy policies and terms provided by skill developers. By default, we do not share your personal information with skill developers. You can choose to grant us permission to share additional information with a skill developer (such as your name and email address with a restaurant booking skill to make a reservation). With Alexa+, we may share relevant information from your interactions with our services to enable skill developers to provide a more personalized experience and deliver the content or services you request. For more information, see the FAQ “What information do we make available to developers to enable skill personalization in Alexa+?” You can see and manage the skills that you granted permission to access specific additional information through More > Alexa Privacy > Manage Skill Permissions and Ad Preferences in the Alexa app and Echo Show devices or amazon.com. If you are an Alexa+ user, you can see and manage certain skills through More > Settings > Manage Alexa+ Services in the Alexa app.
