Control your Fire TV devices with Alexa Routines

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Alexa Features Help ›

Alexa Routines ›

Control your Fire TV devices with Alexa Routines

Use Alexa Routines to control functions on your Fire TV devices, such as powering your TV on/off.

Review requirements for controlling your Fire TV devices using Alexa Routines:

  • Powering on and off: Using Alexa Routines to switch TV power on and off works best on TVs that support HDMI-CEC (Consumer Electronics Control). Check your TV’s user manual to see if your TV supports HDMI-CEC.

  • Linking your device: Your Fire TV devices can be used in a routine when linked to Alexa in the Alexa app. Open More and select Settings > TV & Video > Fire TV.

  • Other actions: On the Routine setup page in the Alexa app, you can see which Fire TV device control actions are available for Alexa Routines. For more help, go to:

  • Create an Alexa Routine in the Alexa App

  • Link Your Fire TV and Alexa Device Was this information helpful?

Fire TV Edition television FAQs

Fire TV Terms & Conditions ›

Fire TV Edition television FAQs

Does Amazon collect data when I watch over-the-air TV on my Fire TV Edition television? Why?

Amazon software collects information relating to your use of over-the-air TV content which may include the name of the channel watched, the name of the program watched, and the duration.

This helps us improve our services and personalize your experience. We will handle this information in accordance with the Amazon Privacy Notice available at www.amazon.com/privacy.

Can I opt out of providing data to Amazon related to use of over-the-air TV content on my Fire TV Edition television?

Yes. To opt out of providing information to Amazon on your use of over-the-air TV content received through an antenna connected directly to your TV, please visit Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings of your Fire TV Edition television. Turning off this setting may affect our ability to personalize your experience.

Fire TV Won’t Turn ON or Screen is Frozen

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Device Issues on Fire TV ›

Fire TV Won’t Turn ON or Screen is Frozen

Can’t get your Fire TV device to power on or the devcie is frozen? Follow these tips.

  • Replace the batteries in your remote. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

  • Use the power cable and adapter included with your Fire TV device.

  • Note: If you lose your Fire TV device power cable or adapter, replace them with Amazon branded equipment to ensure compatibility.

  • Unplug the power cord from your device or wall outlet for several seconds then plug it back in.

  • Press the source or input button on your TV remote to check that your TV input matches the HDMI port your Fire TV uses, and use a high-speed HDMI cable (sold separately).

  • Unplug your Fire TV from your HDMI hub (if you’re using one) and plug it directly into your TV’s HDMI port. If the device turns on but the screen is frozen, try:

  • Press and hold the Select button and the Play/Pause button on your remote at the same time for about 5 seconds to force a restart.

  • Unplug the power cord from your Fire TV device. Wait 60 seconds. Plug it back in. If the issue still persists, go to Fire TV Screen is Frozen for other common solutions.

For more help, go to:

  • Fire TV Smart TV Won’t Turn On
  • Fix a Blank TV Screen on Fire TV Devices

Get More from Your Fire TV

Get the most out of your Fire TV device with this quick guide on features and tips.

  • Fire TV Home Screen Basics
  • Fire TV Remote Basics
  • Use Your Mobile Device Like a Fire TV Remote
  • Learn to Use Alexa with Fire TV
  • Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV
  • Connect Fire TV to Supported Third-Party Devices
Fire TV Home Screen Basics

Your Home screen displays a Main Menu, recommendations, your recently watched items, and featured categories to help you find new content. Use your home screen to access videos, apps, device settings, and other content on your Fire TV.

The Fire TV experience differs across some devices.

Learn how to navigate the New Fire TV Experience

The Fire TV Main Menu includes:

  • My Stuff - Access your: Watchlist, Purchases, and Rentals.
  • Games - Discover and play games from the Amazon Appstore.
  • Find - Search for videos, apps available in the Amazon Appstore, or browse different content categories.
  • Free - Discover free content available on your Fire TV.
  • Live - Watch live TV content from sources like supported apps and subscriptions.
  • Settings - Manage your profiles, network, display, sound, applications, preferences, and more.
  • Fire TV Profiles - Fire TV profiles let you personalize certain features on the home screen for each profile on your device.
  • Apps - Select the Apps icon to find apps on your Fire TV. Tip: To remove something from your recently watched items, press the Menu button and select Remove from Recent. You can’t remove items from featured categories.
Fire TV Remote Basics

You can control your Fire TV device with an Alexa Voice Remote or the Fire TV App. The remote has the following buttons:

  • Alexa Voice - Press and hold the Voice button to interact with your Fire TV device, play videos, search content, and more.
  • Navigation Ring - Navigate your Fire TV by pressing the Up button , Down button , Left button , or Right button on the ring.
  • Select - In the center of the remote, use the Select button to select a content item, function, or category.
  • Home - Use the Home button to return to the home screen from any other screen.
  • Menu - Use the Menu button to access more options for your current selection.
  • Back - Use the Back button to return to the previous screen or action.
  • Media controls - Use the Rewind button , Play/Pause button , and Fast-Forward button to control your video.
Use Your Mobile Device Like a Fire TV Remote

To control your Fire TV with your mobile phone:

  • Download the Fire TV app on your mobile device.
  • Connect your mobile device to the same Wi-Fi network as your Fire TV Device.
  • Open the Fire TV app on your mobile device.
  • Select an available device on the screen.
  • Follow the on-screen prompt.
  • Use the on-screen navigation, keyboard, and other menu options to control the selected Fire TV device.
Learn to Use Alexa with Fire TV

You Fire TV also features Alexa. Perform specific actions, and watch and listen to content on your Fire TV device with Alexa.

To interact with Alexa, hold down the Alexa button on your remote and talk to Alexa. You can say things like:

  • “Open [app name].”
  • “Find [movie title].”
  • “Search for action movies.”
  • “Look for racing game apps.”
  • “Play some study music.” Alexa gives helpful information about topics related to your viewing or listening content and can also do things like control playback.

Many features open in a separate display on your TV screen. To return to the previous screen, press the Back or Home buttons on your Fire TV remote.

Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV

You can link your Fire TV and your compatible Alexa-enabled device to control certain features on your Fire TV. For the devices to pair properly and work together, register your Alexa device and Fire TV to the same account.

To link your Fire TV and your compatible Alexa-enabled device:

  • Open the Alexa app .
  • Open More and select Settings .
  • Select TV & Video.
  • Select Fire TV.
  • Select Link Your Alexa Device and follow the on-screen instructions.
Connect Fire TV to Supported Third-Party Devices

Use your voice to control supported third-party devices, such as antennas, soundbars, and AV receivers. Fire TV devices automatically detect compatible equipment and provide an on-screen interface to add them.

If your Fire TV doesn’t detect your equipment, or you’d like to set up equipment control manually, follow these steps:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment.
  • Select Add Equipment and choose the equipment you’d like to add.

How to Set Up Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Fire TV Remotes ›

How to Set Up Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)

Pair your Alexa Voice Remote with your Fire TV to easily control your streaming experience.

  • Basic Requirements
  • How to Set Up Your New Remote with Your Original Remote
  • How to Set Up Your New Remote without Your Original Remote
  • Remote Overview
  • Troubleshoot Setup Issues
Basic Requirements

To start, have the following devices, parts and accessories ready:

  • A compatible Fire TV device connected to your TV, or a compatible Fire TV Smart TV
  • Original Fire TV Remote (if applicable)
  • Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)
  • Two AAA batteries Back to top
How to Set Up Your New Remote with Your Original Remote
  • Insert the included batteries into the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release).
  • Tip: To insert the batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumb on the arrow of the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.
  • Press the Home button on your original remote.
  • Go to Settings on your Fire TV device.
  • Select Controllers & Bluetooth Devices.
  • Select Amazon Fire TV Remotes.
  • Select Add New Remote.
  • Your Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release) appears in the list when it successfully pairs. Back to top
How to Set Up Your New Remote without Your Original Remote
  • Restart your Fire TV device by unplugging it from power.
  • Plug in your Fire TV device and wait until “Cannot detect your remote” appears on-screen.
  • Insert the included batteries into the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release).
  • Tip: To insert the batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumb on the arrow of the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.
  • Your Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release) should pair with your Fire TV device.
  • Note: If it doesn’t pair, press and hold the Home button for 10 seconds. Back to top
Remote Overview

Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content. Use the Alexa Voice button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to navigate quickly to select apps.

For a text description of the button layout, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote (2024 Release)?.

Back to top

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If your remote doesn’t connect, or doesn’t work, try the following:

  • Remove and reinsert its batteries.
  • Replace the batteries in your remote.
  • Note: Always replace dead batteries with new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2V NiMH rechargeable AAA batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.
  • Move your remote closer to your Fire TV device, within 10 feet (3 m).
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • If you have seven controllers paired, remove one of them before attempting to pair another.
  • Use the Fire TV app to pair your remote. Download the Fire TV app on your mobile device and follow the steps in Use the Fire TV App to Pair Your Remote.
  • Reset Your Fire TV Remote and then try pairing it again. Back to top

How to Set Up Amazon Ember Artline (2026 Release)

Setup and register your device to use Alexa, access the full Amazon Appstore, and receive Fire TV software updates.

  • Basic Requirements
  • Unpacking Your TV
  • Install Your TV
  • Control Buttons and Ports
  • How to Set Up Your Device
  • Remote Overview
  • Troubleshoot Setup Issues
  • Privacy & Support

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • The Amazon Ember Artline TV and in-box accessories.
  • Alexa Voice Remote, power cord, AAA batteries for the remote, wall mount, and wall mount hardware. TV Frame is shipped separately.
  • Note: Amazon Ember Artline TV comes with a wall mount kit. If you don’t intend to wall mount this TV, purchase the legs separately here:
    • 55” TV Legs
    • 65” TV Legs
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password.
    • Don’t have an account? Visit this page: Create an Amazon Account
    • If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password. Back to top
Unpacking Your TV

To unpack your TV:

  • Carefully remove the TV and all included accessories from the box.
  • Note: Make sure that you remove all parts and accessories before disposing the box.
  • Lay your TV on a flat surface with the screen facing down.
  • Carefully remove the plastic wrap off of the TV. Back to top
Install Your TV

To mount your TV on the wall:

  • To mount your Amazon Ember Artline on the wall with the wall mounting kit (included in the box), visit How to Wall Mount Amazon Ember Artline TV.
  • Note: To avoid any damage or serious injury during the mounting process, follow the instructions provided with the wall mount exactly. This process requires two people. To install the TV legs (sold separately as an accessory):

Amazon Ember Artline TV comes with a custom-designed wall mount. If you would like to use the TV legs instead of the wall mount, purchase it separately here:

  • 55” TV Legs
  • 65” TV Legs Screw both TV stand legs into the bottom of the TV as shown in the image. Use the included hardware and a Phillips screwdriver.

Note: To prevent stripping the screw holes, don’t use an electric drill.

To install the TV frame:

The Amazon Ember Artline comes with a customized frame that you can attach to your TV. The frame is divided into four pieces, which attach to your TV with magnetic clip-ons.

Note: Make sure that you install the TV either on the wall mount or on legs before attaching the frame.

  • Lay out all four frame pieces and identify the top, bottom, left, and right pieces.
  • Align all the frame pieces with the edges of the TV and firmly press for the magnets to engage. Back to top
Control Buttons and Ports

The Amazon Ember Artline TV has the following buttons, indicators, and ports located on the front and back of the device:

On the front of the device (bottom of the TV):

  • Microphones on/off button

  • Microphones

  • Power button

  • Light bar On the back of the device:

  • Power port

  • Optical audio output (S/PDIF) port

  • Ethernet port

  • 1 USB 3.0

  • Antenna/Cable port

  • HDMI 2.1 eARC port

  • Three HDMI 2.0 ports

  • IR Emitter port

  • 1 digital optical audio port (headphone jack) Back to top

How to Set Up Your Device

Video guide to set up your device

To set up your Amazon Ember TV:

  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Plug in the power cord into your TV’s power port, then plug the other end into a power outlet.
  • Press the Power button on your remote or TV.
  • Your Fire TV remote should pair automatically with your Amazon Ember Artline TV.
  • Note: If your remote didn’t pair, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • If connecting to a Wi-Fi network, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically connect your Fire TV to Wi-Fi.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually connect your Fire TV to Wi-Fi.
  • If connecting to a router or modem:
    • Connect one end of an Ethernet cable (sold separately) to your TV.
    • Connect the other end to your modem or router.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the setup. Back to top
Remote Overview

Your device comes with the remote that you can use to browse your Fire TV. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content. Use the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to navigate quickly to select apps.

To insert the batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.

Note: For best performance, always replace dead batteries with new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2V NiMH rechargeable AAA batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

For a text description of the button layout, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced?

Note: Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

Back to top

Troubleshoot Setup Issues

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try the following suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to the Forgot Your Password page.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds). Visit the Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, visit the Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi During Setup page to find more troubleshooting information.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If you can’t download apps or games, add a default payment method. Visit the Your Payments page. Back to top
Privacy & Support

You can take control of your privacy settings. Toggle the microphone on/off switch on your device to deactivate microphones whenever you need. In the Alexa app, you are able to access, listen to, or delete any voice recordings associated with your account at any time.

For additional options to customize your privacy, visit Alexa Privacy Hub page.

Back to top

Accessibility Features on Fire TV

Fire TV devices have a set of features designed to enhance the viewing experience for customers with disabilities. These features include things like closed captions, a screen reader, screen magnifier, and audio descriptions. To learn more, go to the Accessibility Features for Fire TV page.

Back to top

How to Set Up Fire TV 4-Series

Set up and register your device to use Alexa, access the full Amazon Appstore, and receive Fire TV software updates.

Basic Requirements

To start, have the following parts, accessories, and information ready:

  • The Fire TV 4-Series TV and in-box accessories
    • Alexa Voice Remote, power cord, AAA batteries for the remote, 2 TV stand legs, and 4 TV stand screws
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password
    • Don’t have an account? Visit this page: Create an Amazon Account
    • If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password
  • Philips screwdriver and scissors
  • TV wall mounts (sold separately) if you decide to mount the TV on a wall Back to top
Unpack Your TV

To unpack your TV:

  • Carefully unpack the TV and all included accessories from the box. Make sure you remove all parts and accessories before disposing of the box.
  • Lay your Fire TV on a flat surface with the plastic wrap still on the TV.
  • Cut the plastic wrap off of the TV. Back to top
Install Your TV

Important:

  • The installation process requires two people.

  • Make sure your TV is powered off before installation. Installing while your TV is on may put you at risk of electric shock.

  • Make sure to place your TV on a stable surface. An unstable location risks your TV sliding or falling, potentially causing serious injury or damage. To install the TV stand:

  • Screw both TV stand legs into the bottom of the TV. The legs are interchangeable and can be installed on either side. To mount your Fire TV on the wall:

  • Check that the wall can support the weight of the TV set and wall mount assembly.

    • Compatible VESA wall mount patterns: 300 mm (w) x 300 mm (h)
    • Compatible screws: Type M6, 15 mm length

  • Follow the mounting instructions provided with the wall mount.

  • Note: Follow the mounting instructions exactly as provided. This will help you avoid any damage or serious injury during the mounting process.

  • Make sure to install the TV on a vertical wall.

  • Only use screws that are suitable for the wall’s material.

  • Make sure no one can trip over the TV cables. Follow these tips to place your TV:

  • Don’t place your TV on an unstable surface.

  • Place your TV somewhere that allows good ventilation.

  • Don’t use your TV near damp or cold areas.

  • Keep your TV away from direct sunlight to protect the TV from overheating.

  • Keep liquids and liquid-filled containers away from your TV. Back to top

Control Buttons and Ports

The Fire TV 4-Series TV has the following buttons, indicators and ports located on the front and back of the device.

On the front of the device:

  • Power button: Press once to select the input source. Press and hold to turn the TV on or put into standby mode. On the back of the device:

  • Ethernet/LAN port: Ethernet (10/100 Mbps) to connect to your internet modem or home network.

  • 4 HDMI ports: Use these ports to connect devices such as gaming consoles. The HDMI (eARC) port supports the audio return channel for returning digital audio to receivers or soundbars.

  • Antenna/Cable: Use this port to connect a coaxial cable or antenna.

  • USB: Use this port to connect a USB cable.

  • IR Emitter: Use this port to connect an IR emitter cable to control other devices by IR commands from your TV.

  • Audio out/headphone: Use this port to connect headphones or an analog soundbar to the TV’s headphone jack.

  • Optical audio output (S/PDIF): Use this port to connect an optical cable from the TV to the optical input on your receiver or soundbar.

  • AC-in (input): Use this port to connect the supplied power cable to your TV. Back to top

How to Set Up Your Device
  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Plug in the power cord first into your TV’s power (AC-in) port, and then plug the other end into a power outlet.
  • Note: If the power cord is damaged, don’t connect it to an outlet, as there is a risk of electric shock.
  • (Optional) Connect an external antenna to your TV’s antenna port to watch broadcast TV.
  • Press the Power button on your remote or your TV.
  • Your Fire TV remote should already be paired with your Fire TV.
  • Note: If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds).
  • If connecting to a Wi-Fi network, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • If connecting to a router or modem:
    • Connect one end of an Ethernet cable (sold separately) to your Fire TV.
    • Connect the other end to your modem or router.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete setup. Note: When turning off your TV with the power button on your remote or TV, the device enters standby mode. To completely shut down your TV, unplug the power cord from the outlet.

Back to top

Your device comes with a remote that you can use to navigate your Fire TV. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content. Use the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to quickly navigate and select apps.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press the arrow firmly to release the latch, and slide the cover down.

Note: For best performance, always replace both dead batteries with new 1.5V alkaline or 1.2V NiMH rechargeable AAA batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

For a text description of the button layout, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote Enhanced?

Note: Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

    • Alexa Voice Remote, power cable, power adapter, and AAA batteries for the remote.
  • High-speed remote HDMI cable (not included)
  • A TV with an available HDMI port
  • An Amazon account, including your email address or phone number and password
    • If you created an account without a password, press the Back button on your remote when prompted to enter your password. Use your mobile phone or computer to visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the verification code.
  • An internet connection, including your Wi-Fi name and password Back to top
Control Buttons and Ports

The Fire TV Cube has the following buttons, indicators and ports located on the front, and on the back of the device.

Front of the device:

  • Microphones on/off button
    • Press the microphone on/off button to mute
  • Microphones
    • Detects voice from any direction
  • Volume buttons
    • Control the internal speaker of Fire TV Cube
  • Action button
    • Multi-function button used to wake Alexa
  • Light bar
    • Shows device status and voice response. Back of the device:
  • HDMI input port
  • HDMI output port
  • IR extender port
  • USB-A ports
  • Ethernet port
  • Power port Back to top
How to Set Up Your Device
  • Put the batteries into the remote.
  • Place your Fire TV Cube 1 ft (30 cm) away from any speakers. Position the device with the ports facing away from you.
  • Note: Don’t place the Fire TV Cube in a closed cabinet as it needs to hear your voice. To control components in closed cabinets, use an IR extender (sold separately).
  • Plug the power adapter into an outlet and then into your Fire TV Cube.
  • Plug one end of your high-speed HDMI cable into your TV and the other end in the HDMI out port of your Fire TV Cube.
  • Turn on your TV and switch to the correct HDMI input.
  • Tip: Use the remote that came with your TV to select the HDMI source or input.
  • To set up Wi-Fi, choose one of the options:
    • Use your mobile phone to scan the on-screen QR code to automatically set up Wi-Fi connection.
    • Use your Fire TV remote and follow on-screen instructions to manually set up Wi-Fi connection.
  • To sign-in or sign up with your Amazon account, choose one of these options:
    • Scan the on-screen QR code with your mobile phone.
    • Visit the on-screen web address (amazon.com/code) and enter the activation code shown on your screen.
  • Follow the on-screen questions to set up equipment control for devices like soundbars. Back to top
Remote Overview

Your device comes with the a remote that you can use to browse your Fire TV Cube. Use the playback buttons to play, pause, rewind, or fast forward video content or the Alexa button for voice commands. You can also use the preset app buttons at the bottom of the remote to navigate quickly to select apps.

To insert batteries, turn your remote upside down and place your thumbs on the back cover. Press firmly and slide the cover down. For best performance, use AAA alkaline batteries. To purchase batteries compatible with your device, go to the Amazon AAA batteries product page.

For an overview of button placement, go to What are the Buttons on the Alexa Voice Remote.

Remote appearance, features, and preset apps vary by remote. Check out the device detail page for more information on your device’s remote.

If setting up your device doesn’t go as expected, try the following suggestions:

  • If you get a login error or have forgotten your Amazon account password, you can reset your password. Go to Forgot Your Password page.
  • If your remote doesn’t pair automatically, press the Home button until “Press to start” appears on-screen (about 10 seconds). For more troubleshooting information, go to Can’t Pair Your Fire TV Remote.
  • If you can’t find your network or connect to Wi-Fi, you can find more troubleshooting by visiting the Can’t Connect Your Fire TV Device to Wi-Fi During Setup page.
  • If you’re having issues with your Wi-Fi password, contact your internet service provider.
  • If you can’t download apps or games, add a default payment method. Go to Your Payments. Back to top
Get More with Alexa

Simply say “Alexa” to Fire TV Cube or press the voice button on your remote to find, launch, and control content. Let Alexa control your smart home devices, help you enjoy music and shows, and keep you informed, organized, and connected. To learn more, go to: Learn to Use Alexa on Your Fire TV Cube

Enhance Your Experience

Ethernet cable: If you prefer, you can connect an Ethernet cable for a wired connection instead of Wi-Fi.

IR extender: If using an IR extender (sold separately) to control devices in a closed cabinet, place it on the same shelf as your devices.

Cable or satellite boxes: You can connect your Cable/Satellite box, gaming console, or DVD/Blu-Ray player to the HDMI input port. Use Alexa to easily switch between and access content from these devices.

Alexa Home Theater: Pair your Fire TV Cube wirelessly with compatible Echo devices for immersive sound. To learn more, go to Set Up Alexa Home Theater on Your Fire TV.

Video calling: Connect a compatible USB webcam to make two-way video calls. To learn more, go to Set Up Alexa Two-Way Video Calling on Your Fire TV Device.

Privacy Control

Press the microphone on/off button to turn off voice control. The blue indicator light shows when Alexa is recording and sending your request to Amazon’s secure cloud.

You can access, hear, and delete your voice recordings in the Alexa app, or simply say “Alexa, delete what I just said” or “Alexa, delete everything I’ve ever said”.

How to set up your device

Video guide to set up your device

  • Plug the included USB-C power cable (0.4m) into the Fire TV Stick’s USB-C power port.
  • Plug the Fire TV Stick into your TV’s HDMI port.
  • If there’s not enough space, use any HDMI extender you have at home or try the HDMI extender for Fire TV Stick HD. Review Use an HDMI extender in these scenarios for more information.
  • Plug the other end of the included power cable into the USB-A port on your TV.
    • The short cable (0.4m) is designed for Direct Power — a clean, clutter-free setup that powers your Fire TV Stick directly from your TV.
    • If your TV’s USB-A port is too far from the HDMI port for the included cable to reach, or you see an on-screen message about insufficient power, try using a USB-C cable and 5V 1A USB power adapter you may already have at home to connect to a wall outlet instead.
    • If you don’t have a longer cable or adapter available, contact Amazon Customer Service for troubleshooting help and additional options.

  • Set up your remote:
    • On the back of the remote, press and hold your thumb on the arrow to release the latch. Make sure that you press the arrow firmly to release the latch as you slide the cover off.
    • Insert the included AAA batteries.
  • Using your TV remote, turn on your TV and switch to the correct input.

Use an HDMI extender in these scenarios

An HDMI extender provides access to hard-to-reach HDMI ports behind your TV and reduces over-crowded cables in your entertainment setup. You may need an HDMI extender if the following situations apply to your set up:

  • Your TV’s back panel pocket is smaller than 4.5 inches
  • Other cables are crowding your TV’s back panel on either side
  • The TV has back-facing HDMI ports and is mounted or sits flush with the wall If these situations apply to you, use the following link to purchase an HDMI extender and then contact our customer service to request a refund.

Overview

Warning:

  • When installing on drywall or plasterboard, this mount MUST be secured into two wall studs or contact a professional for installation.

  • Failure to follow instructions could cause serious injury and/or TV damage.

  • Setup requires at least two people.

  • Wall mount is designed for use only with the included TV. Before getting started, you need:

  • The included wall mounting template, along with the bolts, screws, and anchors.

  • An electric drill with a 1/8” (or 3 mm) drill bit for stud mounting, 3/16” (or 5 mm) drill bit for magnet plate installation, or 5/16” drill bit (or 7 mm) drill bit for brick/concrete mounting and a Phillips #2 driver bit

  • A hammer

  • A level or level app

  • Stud finder Back to top

Safety Guidelines

Warning:

  • When installing on drywall or plasterboard, this mount MUST be secured into two wall studs or contact a professional for installation.

  • Failure to follow instructions could cause serious injury and/or TV damage.

  • If stud spacing is not standard or if studs are not present, contact a professional for installation to prevent potential mount failure. Read these tips before installing the wall mount:

  • If you are installing the wall mount on a drywall without proper stud spacing, we recommend that you contact a professional to complete the installation.

  • Use TV dimensions to plan the placement of the mount.

  • Consider the height of everyone using the device. We recommend placing the TV at eye level.

  • Find a mount location away from water or moisture.

  • Don’t drill holes over electrical wiring or piping.

  • Before mounting, unplug the device from electric outlets.

  • If you’re installing the mount on a brick wall, locate an area free of cracks. Back to top

Mounting Instructions

Video guide to set up your device

  • Carefully unpack the TV and all included accessories from the box.
  • Note: Make sure that you remove all the parts and accessories before disposing of the box.
  • Remove the plastic bag and lay the TV screen-side down to access the recess cover.
  • Remove the recess cover and install the 2 mount bolts using a Phillips screwdriver as shown below. To prevent stripping the bolt holes, do not use an electric drill. Back to top
Install the Mount

Warning:

  • When installing on drywall or plasterboard, this mount MUST be secured into two wall studs or contact a professional for installation.
  • Failure to follow instructions could cause serious injury and/or TV damage.
  • If stud spacing is not standard or if studs are not present, contact a professional for installation to prevent potential mount failure.

  1. Use a stud finder to locate two studs when installing on the studs behind drywall or plasterboard. Use a level or level app and mark the center of each stud with a pencil. If installing on brick/concrete, locate an area free of cracks.

  2. Place the mount template on the wall and attach it with a double-sided tape. Use the template to see approximately where the TV will be mounted on the wall.

  3. Place the mount against the wall and mark at least 4 screw holes. Use a level or level app. For studs, line up the screw holes with the center of each stud. For brick/concrete, line up the screw holes with bricks on each side of the mount, avoiding mortar between bricks.

  4. Drill the pilot holes using an electric drill.

  • If installing on studs, use a 1/8” drill bit.
  • Warning: When installing on drywall or plaster board, this mount MUST be secured into two wall studs, or contact a professional for installation.
  • If installing on a brick/concrete wall, use a 5/16” drill bit. After drilling, insert the mount anchors into the holes and secure them using a hammer.
  1. Attach the mount to the wall using the mount screws, an electric drill, and a Philips #2 bit.
  • If installing on studs, install the screws through the mount and into the studs.
  • Warning: DO NOT use mount anchors for drywall or plaster board installation.
  • If installing on brick/concrete, install the screws through the mount and into the anchors.

  1. Mark the locations for the 4 magnet plates on the wall and remove the template.

  2. Drill the pilot holes using a 3/16” drill bit and an electric drill.

  3. Install the 4 magnet plate anchors using a hammer.

  4. Install the magnet plates to the anchors using the magnet screws and an electric drill.

Back to top

Attach the TV to the Mount

Warning:

  • At least two people needed for lifting and attaching TV to the mount.
  • DO NOT press against the screen during installation.

  1. Gently release the bolt latches and fully extend the TV bracket away from the wall.

  2. Place four alignment stickers above the mount bolts and bolt latches. Fold the stickers up for visibility during installation.

  3. Attach the TV to the TV bracket by hanging the mount bolts on to the mount hooks. Use the alignment stickers for guidance.

  4. Close the bolt latches to secure the mount bolts into mount hooks.

  5. Gently push the TV to the wall and connect the magnets with the magnet plates on the wall.

Back to top

Privacy Settings FAQs for Fire TV Products, Fire Tablets and Kindle E-readers

Find more solutions

Amazon Device Terms, Warranties, and Notices ›

Privacy Settings FAQs for Fire TV Products, Fire Tablets and Kindle E-readers

We know you care how information about you is used, and we appreciate your trust that we will do so carefully and sensibly. This FAQ describes the privacy settings available to you for Amazon Fire TV devices, Amazon Ember devices , or Fire TV devices that are developed and manufactured by a third party (collectively, “Fire TV Products”), Fire tablets and Kindle e-readers (“Amazon Devices”).

Visit www.amazon.com/privacynotice to learn more about how we handle personal data.

  1. What information is collected by Amazon Devices?

The operating system of your Amazon Device collects data about your use of the device and its features, such as your navigation of the home screen, selection of device settings (such as device language, display size, WiFi and Bluetooth options), or open and close of apps and services.

Apps and services may also collect info when you use them on Amazon Devices (see FAQ 8 and FAQ 9).

  1. What does Amazon do with information collected through the device operating system?

We use this data to provide you with the features of your device, for example, to fulfill the actions you take on the device (such as opening an app), to allow you to restore the settings on your device, and to help you troubleshoot when you experience technical issues. We also use it to develop and improve products and features for all our customers and to gain insights into how our products are being used, assess customer engagement, identify potential quality issues, analyze our business, and customize marketing offers.

  1. Can I control what information is collected by Fire TV Products or what Amazon does with that information?

Yes, there are several ways you can control what data is collected by Fire TV Products, or how we use data collected by Fire TV Products.

Device Usage Data: You may opt out of processing of your personal data relating to the use of your Fire TV Products collected by the operating system of that device (“device usage data”) for marketing and product improvement purposes via Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings > Device Usage Data. If you turn this setting off, we will stop processing this device usage data for purposes of serving you customized marketing offers and improving our products and features. Turning this setting off will not affect:

  • Your ability to use features of the device (such as Parental Controls, or the “Recents” row), as we will continue to collect and process your data to deliver these features to you;
  • Whether you receive marketing offers, though those offers may be less relevant to you;
  • The processing of data other than device usage data to show you interest-based advertising (to learn more, see “Interest-based Ads” setting below) or
  • The processing of data related to your use of Amazon services, such as Prime Video, on the device (see FAQ 8). App Usage Data: You may opt out of Amazon’s collection of your data relating to open, close, and duration of use of third-party apps on your Fire TV Products via Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings > Collect App Usage Data.

Interest-based Ads: The advertising ID is a resettable identifier we make available to apps on certain Amazon devices for advertising and analytics purposes. You can instruct apps that use your device’s advertising ID not to use that ID to build profiles for advertising purposes or target you with interest-based ads on the device via Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings > Interest-based Ads.

Over-the-air Viewing Data: On smart TVs with Fire TV, you may opt out of providing information to Amazon on your use of over-the-air TV content received through an antenna connected directly to your TV via Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings.

For certain smart TVs with Fire TV, you can view and manage the above settings from your Amazon account by visiting www.amazon.com/mycd and selecting Privacy Settings > Amazon Devices Privacy.

  1. Can I control what information is collected by Fire tablets or what Amazon does with that information?

Yes, there are several ways you can control what data is collected by Fire tablets or how we use data collected by Fire tablets.

Device Usage Data: You may opt out of processing of your personal data relating to the use of your Fire tablets collected by the operating system of that device (“device usage data”) for marketing and product improvement purposes via Settings > Security & Privacy > Device Usage Data. If you turn this setting off, we will stop processing this device usage data for purposes of serving you customized marketing offers and improving our products and features. Turning this setting off will not affect:

  • Your ability to use features of the device (such as data syncing or backup features or Special Offers we display if you purchased a device that includes Special Offers), as we will continue to collect and process your data to deliver these features to you;
  • Whether you receive marketing offers, though those offers may be less relevant to you;
  • The processing of data other than device usage data to show you interest-based advertising (to learn more, see “Interest-based Ads” setting below) or
  • The processing of data related to your use of Amazon services, such as Prime Video, on the device (see FAQ 8). App Usage Data: You may opt out of Amazon’s collection of your data relating to open, close, and duration of use of third-party apps on your Fire tablet via Settings > Apps & Games > Collect App Usage Data.

Interest-based Ads: An Advertising ID is a user-resettable, unique identifier we make available to apps on certain Amazon devices for advertising and analytics purposes. You can instruct apps that use your device’s Advertising ID not to use that ID to build profiles or show you interest-based ads via Settings > Apps & Games > Advertising ID > Interest-based Ads.

Location-Based Services: Location-based services allow maps, other apps, and Amazon to use your estimated location and related information. You can turn off location-based services for your device, or for individual apps, at Settings > Wireless > Location-Based Services. For more about location-based services, please visit www.amazon.com/help/TabletLBS.

For Fire tablets, the above settings are configurable on a profile basis.

For certain Fire tablets, you can view and manage the above settings from your Amazon account by visiting www.amazon.com/mycd and selecting Privacy Settings > Amazon Devices Privacy.

  1. Can I control what information is collected by Kindle e-readers or what Amazon does with that information?

Yes, you may opt out of processing of your personal data relating to the use of your Kindle e-reader collected by the operating system of that device (“device usage data”) for marketing and product improvement purposes via All Settings > Device Options > Advanced Options > Privacy. If you turn this setting off, we will stop processing this device usage data for the purposes of serving you customized marketing offers and improving our products and features. Turning this setting off will not affect:

  • Your ability to use features of the device, such as data syncing or backup features or Special Offers we display if you purchased a device that includes Special Offers, as we will continue to collect and process your data to deliver those features to you;
  • Whether you receive marketing offers, though those offers may be less relevant to you; or
  • The processing of data related to your use of Amazon services on this device (see FAQ 8). For certain Kindle e-readers, you can view and manage the above setting from your Amazon account by visiting www.amazon.com/mycd and selecting Privacy Settings > Amazon Devices Privacy.
  1. If I set my preferences on one Amazon Device, will the setting be applied to all my devices?

No, these settings are device-specific. In addition, if you use multiple user profiles on a tablet, you will choose your settings for each profile.

  1. Where can I manage privacy settings for my Fire TV Product, Fire tablet, or Kindle e-reader?

You can access many of these settings through the device settings on your device. You can also edit privacy settings for certain devices from your Amazon account, by visiting www.amazon.com/mycd and selecting Privacy Settings > Amazon Devices Privacy.

  1. Where can I learn more about privacy options for Amazon apps or services that I use on my Amazon Device?

To learn more about privacy options relating to an Amazon service (such as Prime Video), please consult the settings for the relevant service or app. For more information about your privacy options relating to Alexa and Echo devices, visit amazon.com.

  1. Where can I learn more about privacy options for third-party apps or services that I use on my Amazon Device?

To learn more about privacy options relating to a third-party app or service, we suggest you review the settings and privacy notice for the relevant app or service, or contact the developer or provider of the app or service.

Reset Your Child PIN on Your Fire TV Device

Your child PIN keeps kids in their profiles where they can only access kid-friendly and parent-approved content. If you forgot your child PIN, use these steps to reset it.

Note: To check if your device supports Amazon Kids profiles, go to What is Amazon Kids on Fire TV Devices?

To reset your child PIN:

  • When prompted to enter a Child PIN, try entering your PIN.
  • If the PIN is incorrect, a code appears below the PIN prompt.
  • Visit the amazon.com/code page.
  • Sign in with your Amazon login and password.
  • Enter the reset code shown on your Fire TV in the text box on the Amazon Code page and select Continue.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to reset your child PIN.

Safety and Compliance Information for Fire TV Stick HD (2nd Generation)

Find more solutions

Safety and Compliance Information for Fire TV Stick HD (2nd Generation)

IMPORTANT PRODUCT INFORMATION
SAFETY INFORMATION

READ ALL SAFETY INFORMATION BEFORE USING THE DEVICE. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN FIRE, ELECTRIC SHOCK, OR OTHER INJURY OR DAMAGE.

Watch for Small Parts

Your device, its accessories, and batteries may present a choking hazard to small children. Keep them out of reach of small children.

BATTERY SAFETY

This product contains alkaline batteries. The remote requires batteries for use. Only use new 1.5 V alkaline or 1.2 NiMH rechargeable AAA-sized batteries. Never mix old and new batteries. Keep all of the batteries out of the reach of children. If any batteries begin to leak, take steps to prevent the fluid from coming into direct contact with skin or clothes as the fluid could be corrosive and may be toxic. Remove the batteries and clean the battery compartment in accordance with the battery manufacturer’s recommendations.

Maintaining Your Fire TV Stick HD

Only handle your devices with clean hands. Clean your devices only with a soft cloth that is slightly damp with water and a touch of rubbing alcohol; be careful not to wipe it with anything abrasive or to use any harsh chemicals. Don’t expose your devices to steam, extreme heat or cold. For example, do not install your device near any heat sources such as space heaters, heater vents, radiators, stoves, or other things that produce heat. Store devices in a cool, dust-free areas out of direct sunlight.

Use of third party accessories may impact your devices’ performance. In limited circumstances, use of third party accessories may void your devices’ limited warranty. In addition, use of incompatible third-party accessories may lead to damage to device or the accessory. Read all safety instructions for any accessories before using with your Fire TV Stick HD

Your Fire TV Stick HD does not have an on/off button. It can be powered either by directly connecting to the TV’s USB-A port with the cable provided in-box or using an external power adapter (not provided in-box). If you wish to stop power from flowing into your Fire TV Stick HD, unplug the USB-A cable from the TV or remove the power adapter. Only use Amazon recommended power adapter with your device. Do not force the power adapter into a power outlet. If the power adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately. Do not plug multiple electric devices into the same wall socket. Overloading a socket can cause it to overheat and may result in a fire. Your device may get hot during normal use. If you find the Fire TV Stick HD has become hot to the touch, unplug it from the TV’s USB-A port or the power supply and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling.

OTHER SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS
  • A small percentage of people may be susceptible to blackouts or seizures (even if they have never had one before) when exposed to flashing lights or light patterns, such as when watching video or playing games. If you have experienced seizures or blackouts or have a family history of such occurrences, you should consult a doctor before watching videos or playing games.
  • Engaging in repetitive motions such as pressing buttons or playing some games may cause you to experience occasional discomfort in your hands, arms, shoulders, neck, or other parts of your body.
  • Discontinue use of your device and consult a physician if you experience headaches, blackouts, seizures, convulsion, eye or muscle twitching, loss of awareness, involuntary movement, disorientation, or other discomfort. To reduce risk of these symptoms avoid prolonged use, watch your television from a far distance and in a well-lit room, and take frequent breaks.
  • Handle your device and its accessories with care. Your device and its accessories may have pointed edges which can lead to scratches, cuts, or other physical injury.
  • Small parts contained in your device and its accessories may present a choking hazard to small children.
  • The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that television should be avoided for infants and children under 2 years of age.
  • Do not touch your Fire TV Stick HD or any wires connected to your Fire TV Stick HD during a lightning storm. Do not expose adapter or cable to liquids.
  • If the adapter or cable appears damaged, discontinue use immediately.
  • Your Fire TV Stick HD may get hot during normal use. To reduce the effect of the warming, place your Fire TV Stick HD on a heat resistant surface. If you find the device has become hot to the touch, unplug power and let it cool down for a few minutes before handling
SERVICING YOUR DEVICE

If your device needs service, please contact Amazon Customer Service. Contact details can be found at www.amazon.com/devicesupport.

Using Your Fire TV Stick HD and Alexa Voice Remote Around Other Electronic Devices

The Fire TV Stick HD and Alexa Voice Remote generate, use, and can radiate radio frequency (RF) energy and, if not used in accordance with its instructions, may cause interference to radio communications and electronic equipment. External RF signals may affect improperly installed or inadequately shielded electronic operating systems, entertainment systems, and personal medical devices. While most modern electronic equipment is shielded from external RF signals, if in doubt, check with the manufacturer. For personal medical devices (such as pacemakers and hearing aids), consult with your physician or the manufacturer to determine if they are adequately shielded from external RF signals.

PRODUCT SPECIFICATIONS

Fire TV Stick HD

Model Number: C79G24

Electrical Rating: 5.25V⎓ 1.0A

Operating Temperature Range: 0–35°C (32–95°F)

Alexa Voice Remote

Model Number: PA38CA and PA2M36

Electrical Rating: 3.0V⎓ (2 AAA Batteries)

Operating Temperature Range: 0–35°C (32–95°F)

FCC COMPLIANCE

This device and its related accessories (the “Products”) comply with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation of each Product is subject to the following two conditions: (1) each Product may not cause harmful interference, and (2) each Product must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

Note: The Products have been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device or external switching power supply, pursuant to part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference in a residential installation. The Products generate, use and can radiate radio frequency energy and, if not installed and used in accordance with the instructions, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. However, there is no guarantee that interference will not occur in a particular installation. If a Product does cause harmful interference to radio or television reception, which can be determined by turning the Product off and on, the user is encouraged to try to correct the interference by one or more of the following measures:

Reorient or relocate the receiving antenna.

Increase the separation between the equipment and receiver.

Connect the equipment into an outlet on a circuit different from that to which the receiver is connected.

Consult the dealer or an experienced radio/TV technician for help.

Pursuant to Section 15.21 of the FCC rules, changes or modifications to a Product by the user that are not expressly approved by the party responsible for compliance could void the user’s authority to operate the equipment.

The device meets the FCC Radio Frequency Emission Guidelines. Information on the product is on file with the FCC and can be found by inputting such Product’s FCC ID (which can be found on the device) into the FCC ID Search form available at fcc.gov.

Screen Mirror Your Device to Fire TV

You can mirror devices that support Miracast to your Fire TV, allowing you to access its display on the bigger screen.

Important: Make sure that your device and Fire TV support screen mirroring. Check our Can’t Screen Mirror on Fire TV Devices page page for more information.

To screen mirror your device to Fire TV:

  • Connect your device that supports Miracast and your Fire TV to the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Activate the mirroring option on your device. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions if needed.
  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.
  • Select Display & Sounds.
  • Select Enable Display Mirroring.
  • Note: If the option doesn’t appear, then screen mirroring isn’t compatible with your Fire TV.
  • To complete the connection, follow the on-screen instructions. After sharing your screen, your Fire TV reflects every action you take on your device. Press any button on your Fire TV remote to exit the Display Mirroring screen and end the connection with your device.

Note: While mirroring, Alexa functionality isn’t available on your Fire TV.

Set Up Picture-in-Picture on Fire TV Devices

When you ask Alexa to show your smart home camera, a small window appears on-screen with your live camera feed.

Important: Please read the Safety Information for Using Smart Home Devices with Alexa page before you turn on a smart home skill.

Note: Picture-in-picture feature isn’t available on all Fire TV devices.

To set up picture-in-picture, link your smart home camera in the Alexa app:

  • Open the Alexa app .

  • Open More .

  • Select Add a Device.

  • Select Camera.

  • Select the brand and follow the on-screen instructions. You can now use voice commands to access and manage your camera feed. Say things like:

  • “Show my camera.”

  • “Switch to full screen.”

  • “Switch to picture-in-picture.”

  • “Minimize to picture-in-picture.”

  • “End picture-in-picture.” If you have a Ring Video Doorbell, picture-in-picture automatically appears on-screen when you receive a Ring notification.

Silk Web Browser Not Working on Fire TV

Try these troubleshooting steps if Silk freezes or doesn’t respond or you can’t scroll.

If you’re having issues using the app, try:

  • Clearing the Silk app data and cache. For how to steps, go to Clear App Data and Cache on Fire TV.

  • Restarting your Fire TV by going to Settings , and then My Fire TV or Device & Software. You can also press and hold the Select or OK button and the Play/Pause button at the same time on your remote for 10 seconds. If there’s more than one section you can scroll through on your screen, follow these steps:

  • Use your Fire TV remote to move your cursor to the section of the screen that you want to scroll through.

  • Press and hold the Select or OK button on your remote.

  • While still holding the Select or OK button , press the directional pad to scroll through that section.

  • Tip: For example, if you want to scroll down, press and hold the Select or OK button and push Up on the directional pad. For more help, go to:

  • Clear App Data and Cache on Fire TV Was this information helpful?

Use Dual Audio on Your Fire TV Smart TV

Find more solutions

Digital Services and Device Support ›

Fire TV Support ›

Accessibility on Fire TV ›

Use Dual Audio on Your Fire TV Smart TV

Stream audio to paired hearing aids while others listen through the TV’s built-in speakers.

The Dual Audio feature is available on:

  • Fire TV Omni Mini-LED Series TVs Important: Fire TV supports the Audio Streaming for Hearing Aids (ASHA) protocol, which sends TV audio directly to your hearing aids. Make sure you have paired an ASHA-compatible hearing aid device to your Fire TV. Compatible hearing aids include Starkey hearing aids, Widex hearing aids, and Cochlear hearing devices. For more information, visit: Accessibility Features for Fire TV.

To activate Dual Audio once your hearing aids are paired to your Fire TV:

  • Go to Settings from your Fire TV menu.

  • Select Display & Sounds.

  • Select Audio Output.

  • Select the TV Speaker and Hearing Aids option. While in Dual Audio mode, you can adjust hearing aid volume through Quick Settings:

  • Press and hold the Home button on your Fire TV remote to access Quick Settings.

  • Select Hearing Aids.

  • Select Media Volume and adjust the slider to your preferred audio settings. Note: While in Dual Audio mode, hearing aid volume is controlled through Quick Settings. TV speaker volume is controlled by the Fire TV remote.

If you are experiencing audio delay while in Dual Audio mode:

  • Press and hold the Home button on your Fire TV remote to access Quick Settings.
  • Select Hearing Aids.
  • Select Hearing Aid Delay Adjust to change audio delay settings.

Use Your Fire TV Cube to Switch to a Set-Top Box Connected to Your TV

More Fire TV Devices ›

Fire TV Cube Help ›

Use Your Fire TV Cube to Switch to a Set-Top Box Connected to Your TV

After you set up equipment control, you can use Alexa voice commands to do things like switch inputs or go to specific channels.

The set-top box and Fire TV Cube need to be within line of sight of each other.

For a list of supported set-top box providers, go to Supported Set-Top Box Providers on Fire TV Cube. If you’re connecting your set-top box directly to your Fire TV Cube, go to Control Your Set-Top Box on Fire TV Cube.

To set up equipment control for devices connected to your TV’s HDMI input:

  • Go to Settings from the Fire TV menu.
  • Select Equipment Control.
  • Select Manage Equipment.
  • Select Add Equipment.
  • Select Live TV.
  • Select Set-top box.
  • Select Satellite or Cable depending on your setup.
  • Choose your TV provider or select Provider not listed.
  • Note: Selecting Provider not listed will exit the setup process.
  • Use your TV remote to switch to a live channel. After the channel switches, press the Fast Forward button on your Fire TV remote.
  • Follow the on-screen prompts to complete setup.
  • Once set up is complete, you can use the following Alexa voice commands in the table below to control your set-top box:
  • Command Type
  • Voice Commands
  • Channel change
    • “Tune to CNN.”
    • “Channel up.”
    • “Channel down.”
    • “Tune to [channel number] on cable.”
  • Directional pad navigation
    • “Go up / down.”
    • “Move left / right”
    • “Select.”
  • Menu
  • “Open program guide.”
  • Media control
    • “Play / Pause.”
    • “Rewind / fast forward.” For more help, go to:
  • IR Extension Cables with Fire TV Cube
  • Use Your Alexa Device to Control Your Fire TV Was this information helpful?

  • Apps & Games: Works with compatible apps and games available in the Amazon Appstore.
  • Tip: Look for the Works With section on the detail page for an app or game to confirm whether it’s compatible with Fire TV Stick.
  • Music: Access the Amazon Music app and many other third-party music apps and services.
